#### The policy 

Policy ____________________________________________________________________________________ 

The policy contract is the wrapper that combines benefits in a single policy. 

Multiple insured lives (maximum 20) are allowed on a policy. 

Cessions _____________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

A cession is the process where all the rights, title and interest in the policy or benefits are transferred to another person or legal entity who then becomes the new owner. The person who transfers the policy is known as the cedent and the person or legal entity to whom the policy is transferred is known as the cessionary. 

**An absolute or outright cession** : The cedent transfers all his rights, entitlements and obligations under the policy contract to the cessionary. No residual rights remain with the cedent. The cessionary will then replace the cedent as the policyholder 

**A collateral cession** : With a collateral cession, the rights ceded to the cessionary may revert to the cedent at some future date, e.g., when the cedent meets their obligations. At the time of the cession, the actual date of the reversion may or may not be known. With a collateral cession, the cedent retains the ownership of the policy. 

Momentum may only note outright cessions for the entire policy but may note collateral cessions for the following stand-alone benefits: 

- Death Benefit 

- Modified Death Benefit 

- Education Protector 

- Death Income Benefit 

- Comprehensive Disability Benefit 

- Own Occupation Disability Benefit 

- Comprehensive ADW Disability Benefit 

- ADW Disability Benefit 

- Functional Impairment Benefit 

- Complete Critical Illness Benefit 

- Complete Enhanced Critical Illness Benefit 

- Comprehensive Living Benefit 

Acceptance __________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

Cover starts on the day of acceptance unless the policyholder has specified a future starting date. 

If by the time of acceptance, the specified starting date is in the past, it is adjusted in accordance with the starting date procedure mentioned below. 

Starting date _________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The starting date of any benefit and policy will always be the first of a month. 

The policyholder may choose a starting date in the future if it is not more than a maximum of the current month plus one month into the future. 

The policyholder may select one of the following starting date options: 

- Automatic starting date 

   - The starting date will be the first day of the month following the acceptance of the benefits. Free cover applies to this option. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 3 

- Fixed starting date 

   - The starting date will be the date the policyholder completes on the application form. Free cover will only apply to this option if Momentum moves the starting date to a later, future starting date, because the processing of the application is delayed. 

- Starting date option to be advised 

   - If the policyholder is unable to select one of the starting date options mentioned above now, the must inform their Financial Adviser of their preferred starting date option (automatic starting date or fixed starting date). The Financial Adviser will upload the relevant documentation to the Momentum system for processing. 

Premium payment date ______________________________________________________________________________________ 

The policyholder may select the premium payment date upfront. 

The payment date may be any day of the month. 

The premium is due on the first of the month but we do allow clients to pay their premiums on a later date. Clients can choose a debit date until the 20th to pay the premium for same month. The policy will show will arrears until the debit date. Debits between the 21st and 31st will be in credit on the policy until the 1st of the following month. 

**Note:** There is a two-day buffer built in for new business cases that have a debit order date between the 21st and the 31st. This is to reduce the amount of double debits Momentum will take for these policies in the following month. 

###### **Example:** 

New business policy issued in October with a 1 November starting date: 

If the policyholder chose a debit order date for the policy between the 1st and 20th of October and the policy is accepted on any day in October, Momentum will deduct the debit order for November on the correct date. 

###### HOWEVER 

If the policyholder chose a debit order date of the 25th, and the policy is accepted on: 

- 20 October. The November premium will be deducted on 25 October (in advance for November, prior to starting date). 

- 26 October. The November premium will be deducted that same night. 

- 29<sup>th</sup> October. Momentum will double debit the policyholders account in November. (1 x for November and 1 x for December. Note: This scenario falls outside of the two-day buffer). 

Cooling-off ___________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The cooling-off period is 31 days from the date on which a policyholder receives his new business (or alteration) contract but is no longer than 60 days after the policy's starting date (or alteration date). 

If the policyholder cancels a policy or benefits within the cooling-off period, Momentum will refund any premiums they paid after the cost of any risk cover is deducted. Cooling-off may apply to a stand-alone benefit or the entire policy (at new business stage) or a stand-alone or ancillary benefit in the event of alterations. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 4 

Fees _________________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The contract policy fee is R30 per month. The policy fee goes towards covering some of the costs in administering the policy. The policy fee may increase due to increases in administrative expenses. Premium frequencies ________________________________________________________________________________________ Premiums may be paid monthly or annually. If the policyholder chooses annual premiums: • all benefits on the policy must have the same policy anniversary date • all benefits on the policy must have the same payment frequency. Annual premiums are subject to a 5% discount. Annual premiums are not allowed on Complete Income Protector, Temporary Income Protector, Business Overheads Protector and Business Protector (SelfEmployed) and Business Protector (Professional). 

Payment methods ____________________________________________________________________________________________ Only debit order payments are allowed. The premium payer must give instruction to change debit order details. Momentum cannot accept instruction to change bank details from the policyholder. Contract premiums ___________________________________________________________________________________________ The current minimum contract premium is: 

- R200 a month for Myriad policyholders 

- R100 a month for Student Package 

The minimum contract premium includes all benefit premiums, fees and loadings. This premium is determined after underwriting has taken place. 

The premium the policyholder pays may be lower than the contract premium due to premium discounts. 

The contractual premium that the policyholder must pay will reduce at the end of the benefit term for an ancillary benefit. Non-payment of the first premium ___________________________________________________________________________ If the first premium under a policy is not collected, the insured life will not enjoy cover until all the premiums due are received, provided that the policy has not lapsed.

Beneficiary for ownership ____________________________________________________________________________________ 

The policyholder may nominate a person to whom ownership is transferred if the policyholder dies while the policy is still in force. This can happen if the insured life is someone other than the policyholder. 

If the policyholder dies, ownership is transferred to the nominated person and the policy will remain in force. 

If the policyholder and the insured life are different and the policyholder dies, ownership of the policy is transferred to the deceased's estate if there is no beneficiary for ownership. 

A beneficiary of ownership nomination must add up to 100%. Momentum only allows one beneficiary of ownership per policy. 

If a policy has multiple owners, multiple beneficiaries of ownership will be allowed, provided that the total percentage split adds up to 100%. 

One policyholder cannot appoint a beneficiary of ownership without the consent of the other policyholder.  All the policyholders must sign the beneficiary of ownership nomination. This is the case even if there is only one beneficiary of ownership.

#### Funding 

Premium patterns ____________________________________________________________________________________________ 

###### **Level premium pattern** 

Under the level premium pattern, the policyholder will pay a level premium for a level benefit amount for the benefit term. 

###### **Compulsory premium pattern** 

A compulsory premium pattern offers a cheaper initial premium for a level benefit than the level premium pattern but gets more expensive over time. The policyholder may choose compulsory premium increases of 3% to 10% 

A compulsory premium increase of 5% is available on all benefits with a fixed term. 

Once a policyholder has chosen this premium pattern, these increases become an obligation under the policy and will automatically occur every year on the benefit anniversary date. 

The compulsory increases will not lead to an increase in the benefit amount. 

If the policyholder chooses the compulsory premium pattern, they may only add an increasing premium waiver to the benefit. 

###### **LifeStage and Aggressive LifeStage premium pattern** 

The premium will automatically increase every year with a percentage based on the insured life's age at the time of the increase. 

The Aggressive LifeStage premium pattern is not available on income protection benefits. 

These premium patterns are not available on benefits with a fixed term. 

|Age|LifeStage|Aggressive LifeStage|
|---|---|---|
|<45|5%|10%|
|45-54|6%|11%|
|55-64|7%|12%|
|65-69|5%|10%|
|70-74|3%|8%|
|>74|3%|6%|



Premium guarantees _________________________________________________________________________________________ 

###### **Standard premium guarantee option** 

This option provides a premium guarantee for a fixed term. 

###### **Extended premium guarantee option** 

Policyholders who want more peace of mind may choose the extended premium guarantee. The extended premium guarantee is not available for all benefits. 

If a policyholder chooses an extended premium guarantee, the premium they pay is higher than the premium under the standard premium guarantee option. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 8 

###### **10-year capped premium guarantee option** 

The premium during the first ten years of the guarantee term is guaranteed not to increase. 

The premium may need to be reviewed at any time after the initial ten-year guarantee term. 

The premium will never be higher than the premium as at the end of the guarantee period increased by 15%, plus an additional 15% for every completed five-year period after that. (The 15% limit is over and above all voluntary and compulsory increases). 

###### **General rules** 

Momentum will not increase the contract premium or decrease the benefit amounts during the premium guarantee term. 

All benefits funded with a Level, LifeStage, Aggressive LifeStage, or Compulsory premium pattern are priced to provide cover for the benefit term at the disclosed applicable premium level(s). If Momentum's experience differs from what was initially expected, the premium may be adjusted at the end of the premium guarantee term. 

The chosen premium guarantee can also influence the premium payable. 

The premium guarantee term: 

- is the benefit term for term benefits 

- is five years for the Education Protector and Modified Death Benefit. 

- is ten years for any benefit with a 10-year capped premium guarantee option. 

- is calculated by Momentum for whole-life benefits and benefits with a particular (retirement) age if funded with a level or increasing premium pattern. 

- is calculated again if any alteration other than a regular premium/ benefit amount increase is made. 

- of ancillary benefits will equal the guarantee term of the stand-alone benefit to which they are attached. 

Premium Guarantee Term Extender __________________________________________________________________________ 

Momentum will extend the premium guarantee term by one year for every two of any of the following regular increases: 

- premium increases of 10% or more 

- premium increases in line with the increase in the general increase in the South African Consumer Price Index (CPI) 

- benefit amount increases of 5% or more 

- benefit amount increases below 5% in combination with any compulsory premium increase 

- benefit amount increases (including increases in line with the general increase in the CPI or the Rand Depreciation Index (RDI). 

Only one of the above increases is taken into account per year. 

The Premium Guarantee Term Extender does not apply to the following: 

- 10-year capped premium guarantee option 

- benefits with a fixed term 

- Complete Income Protector 

- Temporary Income Protector 

- Functional Protector

Increase options _____________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The policyholder may select benefit amount increases or premium increases. 

When the benefit amount increases, Momentum will calculate the corresponding increase in the premiums. 

When the premium increases Momentum will calculate the corresponding increase in the benefit amount. 

Increases automatically apply each year on the benefit anniversary. 

###### **Premium increases** 

Momentum uses the chosen voluntary premium increase to calculate the additional benefit amount that the policyholder may purchase. 

Compulsory premium increases will not lead to an increase in the benefit amount. 

Voluntary premium increases are not available on LifeStage premium patterns. 

The following premium increase options are offered: 

- Voluntary premium increases: 3% to 20% with increments of 0.1%. 

- Compulsory premium increases: 3% to 10%. 

- Increases in line with the general increase in the South African Consumer Price Index (CPI) (limited to a maximum of 15%). 

###### **Benefit amount increases** 

The following benefit amount increase options are offered: 

- 3% to 10% with increments of 0.1%. 

- In line with the general increase in the South African Consumer Price Index (CPI) (limited to a maximum of 15%). 

- The greater of the Rand Depreciation Index (RDI) and the general increase in the South African Consumer Price Index (CPI). The RDI is calculated as the greater of the rand's depreciation against the US dollar or the Euro. 

The policyholder may add benefit amount increases to a policy with a Level, LifeStage, Aggressive LifeStage or Compulsory premium pattern. 

Certain benefits may have limited benefit amount increase options (refer to details in the Benefits section). 

Momentum will not increase the benefit amount if: 

- a policyholder has given Momentum notice to cancel future increases 

- a policyholder has given Momentum notice to suspend the increases for that year 

- any premiums are in arrears. 

Momentum will cancel all future increases if no increases are applied for two consecutive years.

#### Lapses and reinstatements 

Premiums in arrears (Lapse) __________________________________________________________________________________ 

A 30-day grace period will apply. 

If the arrear premiums are paid before the end of the grace period, no underwriting is required. A written request for the reinstatement of the benefit will be required. 

Momentum requires a fully completed application form and all arrear premiums paid if the grace period has expired. Medical underwriting will apply. 

Momentum can cancel the policy if the premium is not paid within the 30-day grace period. 

CPI increases are included when calculating the outstanding premiums. 

The benefit will not lapse if premiums are waived, or if the policyholder does not have to pay premiums for a benefit due to a claim. 

Restarting the policy (Reinstatement)  ________________________________________________________________________ 

Policies can only be reinstated within 12 months from the lapse date, provided that at least one premium was received prior to the lapse. 

A reinstatement without paying back arrear premiums will be allowed for the first reinstatement of a policy. 

Subsequent reinstatements (without paying back arrear premiums) will be allowed if at least 12 consecutive premiums were received. 

For all other reinstatements, at least one premium must be paid.  This premium is considered a commitment premium and not meant for future premiums. (The next premium will still be payable). 

Standard underwriting rules will apply. 

Momentum will request the outstanding premium(s) to be paid only once a decision has been received from underwriting. The policy will only then be reinstated. 

Policies with the Modified Death Benefit do not qualify for the write-off option. 

The reinstatement request must be emailed to the Myriad Retention Unit directly at myriadretentionunit@momentum.co.za. 

Telephonic reinstatements can be done by calling the Retention Unit on 012 675 3911. 

A Reinstatement form (UNDERW070) must be submitted with all reinstatement requests. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024

Premium reviews 

Momentum reserves the right to review the contract benefit premium at the end of the guarantee term to cover the benefit(s) cost until the next review date. 

If the policyholder has a 10 year-capped premium guarantee, Momentum will review the contract benefit premium at the end of every 10- years. The premium will never be higher than the premium as at the end of the guarantee period increased by 15%, plus an additional 15% for every completed five-year period after that. (The 15% limit excludes all voluntary and compulsory increases.) 

The assumptions Momentum used to calculate the premium are adopted to cover the whole period of the policy and may be reviewed as set out below. 

- When Momentum reviews the assumptions, the actual investment returns on premium income are compared with those used to calculate the premium at the start date of the benefit. 

- Momentum will review the assumptions relating to expected future claims, investment returns, cost of reinsurance, incidence of taxation and lapse rates. 

- Momentum will analyse the claims experience for similar policies and industry claims experience and the impact of future medical advances and practices. 

- Momentum will use a fair and reasonable increase or decrease at each review due to any differences relative to previous assumptions. 

Any change to the premium will not depend on the policyholder's individual circumstances, for example their health, at the time of the review. 

Momentum will inform the policyholder in writing at least 90 days before any change to the premium. Any change is effective from the next relevant policy anniversary date.

#### Additional features 

Immediate Cover _____________________________________________________________________________________________ 

Immediate Cover only starts when Momentum receives the signed application. 

Immediate cover is only available on the Death Benefit, Death Income Benefit, Estate Provider and Education Protector. 

The amount of the immediate life cover is limited to the lesser of: 

- R500 000 or 

- The initial death cover the policyholder applied for. 

Immediate Cover does not apply to accident, disability, functional impairment or critical illness benefits. 

A policyholder must submit valid debit order details to Momentum together with the application form. If the bank refers the debit for the first premium back to Momentum for any reason, the cover will be considered never to have started. 

The insured life must be under the age of sixty years at the date of application. 

Immediate life cover does not apply to claim events linked to any accidents where the insured life took part in any form of aviation or dangerous activities such as, but not limited to hang-gliding, parachuting motor racing or any other extreme sport. No long-term insurer may ever have declined, deferred or accepted on special terms an application for life cover that the insured life has made. 

The insured life may not negotiate for life cover insurance with any other company and may not have done so during the three months before the date they apply for a Momentum policy. 

Immediate Cover will not be paid if the cause of death is directly or indirectly related to any condition, disease or injury that existed before the policy application date and of which the insured life reasonably ought to have been aware. 

The insured life must complete a declaration of health, and the information disclosed must not pose a substandard risk to Momentum. 

Immediate Cover will end if a loading or exclusion applies to the policy application. 

All the policy conditions set out in the policy contract will apply to immediate life cover. 

Immediate Cover will end on the earliest of: 

- a loading or exclusion being applied to the policy application. 

- the acceptance of the application. 

- the rejection of the application. 

- thirty days after the signing of the application. 

- the policyholder cancelling the benefit in writing. 

Free Cover ___________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

Free Cover is available on all stand-alone and ancillary benefits if: 

- the policyholder did not specify a future starting date on the policy, or 

- the policyholder specified a future starting date on the policy and Momentum moved the start date forward. 

Momentum will pay a valid claim if the claim event occurs on or after the date of acceptance of the policy 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024

###### **Homeloan Free Cover** 

To qualify for the Homeloan Free Cover, the selected starting date may only be up to 3 months from the date of acceptance. 

If the policyholder specifies a future starting date on the policy and the policy contains a Homeloan Protector, the full benefit amount, limited to a maximum of R3 million, is paid only under the Homeloan Protector or the Death Benefit to which it is attached. 

Instant Cash __________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

This special feature is available on the Death Benefit and Estate Provider Benefit only. 

Momentum will pay a proportion of the Death Benefit or Estate Provider Benefit, after the deduction of any debt, within one working day of the submission of the death claim. 

The amount paid is subject to current practice at the time of the claim. At present, 10% of the benefit amount, limited to R50 000 per insured life (over all death claims, excluding Estate Provider Benefit), will be paid. 

Momentum will pay the balance of the claim amount if the claim is admitted. 

Momentum will only make this payment if the insured life dies more than two years after the starting date of the Death Benefit or Estate Provider Benefit. 

When restarting the benefit, a new two-year period will apply. If a policyholder increases the benefit amount, a new two-year period will apply for the increased portion from the increase date. 

All required documentation must accompany the death claim. Refer to the Claim requirements section of this guide for more information. 

Momentum does not acknowledge the validity of the death claim by paying the Instant Cash amount. Momentum will not pay the balance of the amount claimed if the claim is not admitted after assessment. In addition, the Instant Cash amount that was paid out will have to be returned to Momentum. 

Momentum will only pay Instant Cash if there is a beneficiary.  If no beneficiary is nominated, the full claim amount is paid into the estate when the claim is admitted. 

Terminal Illness ______________________________________________________________________________________________ 

Terminal Illness is only available on the Death Benefit. 

This feature is not available in the last year of a term benefit. 

This special feature is available free of charge and gives policyholders the right to claim the full benefit amount of the Death Benefit if the insured life becomes terminally ill. 

A terminal illness is a medical condition that, with reasonable certainty, in the opinion of Momentum's Medical Officer, will result in the death of the insured life within 12 months of the date on which Momentum receives medical evidence to that effect. 

Momentum will pay the Terminal Illness amount to the cessionary if the benefit is ceded.

Reinstatement Option ________________________________________________________________________________________

- Complete Critical Illness Benefit

Buy-and-Sell Future Cover ____________________________________________________________________________________ 

Buy-and-Sell Future Cover is only available on the Death Benefit. 

If a claim is admitted on one of the policies under the Buy-and-Sell agreement, the policyholder has the option to increase the benefit amount on the remaining policies under the agreement by the insured life's share of the claim amount, without any proof of health or insurability. 

Requirements for exercising the Buy-and-Sell Future Cover option: 

- The original Buy-and-Sell agreement (a new one 

- drawn up free of charge by the Momentum Business Solutions team). 

- All the individual policies under the Buy-and-Sell agreement must be Myriad policies. 

- The option must be exercised on all the policies under the Buy-and-Sell agreement. 

- The policyholder does not have to increase the benefit amount by the full amount available to him. However, the percentage of the available amount the benefit amount is increased by must be the same for each of the remaining policies under the Buy-and-Sell arrangement (e.g. 50% of the amount available). 

- There must be three or more policies under the Buy-and-Sell agreement before the claim. 

- Any specific exclusions and/or loadings on the remaining policies will also apply to the increase in the benefit amount. 

Retirement Booster __________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The Retirement Booster is a risk feature available to policyholders with qualifying Myriad risk benefits linked to a qualifying retirement annuity. 

Every year Momentum rewards policyholders with qualifying benefits by allocating a portion of the premium paid for each risk benefit to the Retirement Booster. 

###### **Retirement Booster allocations** 

Allocations are made on the benefit anniversary of each qualifying Myriad benefit. 

Momentum will only make these allocations if the policyholder has: 

- qualifying Myriad risk benefits that are linked to a qualifying retirement annuity, and 

- a qualifying retirement annuity with up-to-date recurring premiums, and 

- accepted a qualifying increase on the qualifying Myriad risk benefit during the past policy year. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 16 

If the policyholder has more than one qualifying Momentum retirement annuity at the time of each Retirement Booster allocation, the retirement annuity with the longest term to maturity is used to calculate the booster allocation at that time. 

Momentum will pay the accumulated Retirement Booster on the maturity date of the retirement annuity with the longest term to maturity. No further allocations is made to the Retirement Booster after the maturity date. 

If the maturity date of the qualifying Momentum Retirement Annuity is after the end date of the qualifying Myriad benefit, Momentum will pay the Retirement Booster (without interest) in respect of that benefit, at the end of the Myriad benefit term. 

Momentum may review the Retirement Booster allocation percentage at any time. 

The Retirement Booster allocation percentage is enhanced from 1.5% to 4.5% for Longevity Protector® and the Permanent Disability Enhancer AND the stand-alone benefits to which they are attached. 

Myriad policies with multiple policyholders 

- At least one of the policyholders has to be a fund member of a qualifying Momentum retirement annuity. The allocations to and the payment of the Retirement Booster is based on the later maturity date of all the qualifying Momentum retirement annuities of which the policyholders are members. The Retirement Booster payment is split between the policyholders according to their percentage ownership. 

Myriad policies with owners other than natural persons 

- Sole proprietors who purchase an income protection solution through Momentum's business packages qualify for Retirement Booster allocations on these particular benefits 

- Other Myriad policies with owners other than natural persons: benefits on these policies will not qualify for Retirement Booster allocations. 

Business assurance policies 

- Benefits on these policies will not qualify for Retirement Booster allocations. 

###### **Maturity date** 

The maturity date refers to the end of the initial savings term. 

Momentum will pay the accumulated Retirement Booster amount on the earlier of retirement or age 70. 

Open ending of the qualifying Momentum retirement annuity 

- Momentum will pay the accumulated Retirement Booster value on the original maturity date that the annuity is open-ended, with no further allocations to the Retirement Booster. 

Auto-continue of the qualifying Momentum retirement annuity 

- Momentum will pay the accumulated Retirement Booster value on the original maturity date before the annuity is auto continued, with no further allocations to the Retirement Booster. 

###### **Qualifying Momentum retirement annuity** 

A recurring premium Investo retirement annuity

###### **Qualifying Myriad benefits**

- Death Benefit 

- Unnatural Death Benefit

- Funeral Benefit 

- Death Income Benefit 

- Estate Provider

- Own Occupation Disability Benefit

- Business Overheads Protector 

- Business Protector (Self Employed)

The following Myriad benefits do not qualify for an allocation to the Retirement Booster: 

- Future cover benefits 

- Premium waiver benefits 

- Education Protector 

- Modified Death Benefit 

- All Myriad benefits with a fixed term (excluding benefits for which the policyholder selects the age when the benefit should end). 

- Contingent Liability Insurance 

- Buy-and-sell Insurance 

- Keyperson Insurance

- Business Overheads Cover* 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 18 

- Income Replacement* 

- Share Buyback 

- Buy-and-sell Insurance - Alternate 

*Except where the policyholder is a sole proprietor or a natural person. 

Momentum may review the list of qualifying benefits from time to time. 

If the policyholder commutes 100% of their income, under the Permanent Disability Enhancer attached to a Complete Income Protector or Complete Income Protector (Whole Life) no further allocations to the Retirement Booster for the main benefit is made. 

Momentum will continue to make allocations to the Retirement Booster if premiums are paid under a premium waiver. 

###### **Qualifying increases** 

The qualifying Myriad benefit must have any of the following regular annual increases to qualify for an allocation to the Retirement Booster: Premium increases of 10% or more. 

Premium increases in line with the general increase in the South African Consumer Price Index (CPI). 

Benefit amount increases of 5% or more. 

Benefit amount increases below 5% in combination with any compulsory premium increase including LifeStage and Aggressive LifeStage premium increases. 

Benefit amount increases in line with the general increase in the South African Consumer Price Index (CPI) or the rand depreciation index (RDI). 

Momentum may review the list of qualifying increases from time to time. 

###### **Annual Retirement Booster allocation calculation** 

Momentum will calculate the allocations to the Retirement Booster in respect of each qualifying Myriad benefit as follows: 

- the sum of the benefit premiums payable for the qualifying Myriad benefit, during the past policy year, multiplied by 

- the Retirement Booster allocation percentage, currently 1.5%, multiplied by 

- the minimum of the outstanding term of the qualifying Myriad benefit and the outstanding term until the maturity date of your qualifying Momentum retirement annuity. If a policyholder has multiple qualifying retirement annuities the retirement annuity with the longest term is used as the date for the booster allocation. 

###### **Death of the policyholder** 

Momentum will cancel all the accumulated allocations to the Retirement Booster on the death of the fund member. 

Momentum will cancel all the accumulated allocations to the Retirement Booster if: 

- there are multiple policyholders and the policyholder with the main retirement annuity dies and 

- the other policyholders do not have nor decide to take out a qualifying retirement annuity. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 19 

###### **Lapse and reinstatement of a Myriad policy** 

Momentum will not make Retirement Booster allocations after a policy has lapsed unless it is reinstated. 

Momentum will reinstate the accumulated Retirement Booster allocations from the lapse date when the policy reinstates. 

Momentum will exclude any special debit orders collected during the reinstatement process from the calculation of the Retirement Booster allocation. 

Momentum will exclude any premiums written off during the reinstatement process when calculating the Retirement Booster allocation. 

The annual Retirement Booster allocations will continue normally from the next policy anniversary. 

###### **Alterations to a qualifying Myriad benefit that will affect the Retirement Booster** 

Cancellation 

- Momentum will cancel all the accumulated allocations to the Retirement Booster in respect of a qualifying Myriad benefit cancelled as a result of: 

   - a claim, or 

   - any event covered in the policy contract, or 

   - notification from the policyholder to cancel the policy or benefit. 

Premium reduction 

- Where an alteration leads to a premium reduction, Momentum will reduce all the accumulated allocations to the Retirement Booster, in respect of that benefit, in the same proportion. 

###### **Alterations to a qualifying Momentum retirement annuity that will affect the Retirement Booster** 

Premium reduction 

- If the premium reduces, it will not affect the accumulated Retirement Booster amount. 

Paid-up 

- If the policyholder stops paying premiums under all the qualifying Momentum retirement annuities, no further allocations are made to the Retirement Booster. 

- The Retirement Booster will remain unchanged until the policyholder starts paying premiums again. 

Transfer of funds 

- If the policyholder transfers all of the qualifying Momentum retirement annuities to another company's retirement annuity fund, Momentum will cancel all the accumulated allocations to the Retirement Booster. 

- When the qualifying Momentum Retirement Annuity with the later maturity date is transferred, all future allocations and Retirement Booster payment is based on the remaining Retirement Annuity with the latest maturity date. A 10% penalty is applied to the Retirement Booster value for every year the maturity date is brought forward. 

   - All future Retirement Booster allocations and the maturity date is based on the new qualifying Momentum retirement annuity if: 

   - If the policyholder transfers all of their qualifying Momentum retirement annuities to another company's retirement annuity fund and 

   - takes out a new qualifying Momentum retirement annuity shortly before the transfer 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 20 

- A 10% penalty will apply to the Retirement Booster value for every year that the maturity date is brought forward if the new qualifying Momentum retirement annuity's term is shorter. 

Term extensions (changing the maturity date of the qualifying Momentum retirement annuity) 

- If the term of the qualifying Momentum Retirement Annuity with the later 

- maturity date is extended by changing the maturity date to a later maturity date, future Retirement Booster allocations is based on the extended term. Historic booster values accumulated will not be affected. 

- The accumulated booster amount is paid on the maturity date of the retirement annuity with the longest term to maturity. No further allocations is made to the Retirement Booster after the maturity date. 

Early Retirement/Term reductions 

- Momentum will reduce the Retirement Booster by 10% for every full year that the maturity date is brought forward, if the policyholder: 

   - retires before the maturity date of the qualifying Momentum Retirement Annuity with the later maturity date (except as a result of disability) or, 

   - reduces the term of the qualifying Momentum Retirement Annuity with the later maturity date by changing the maturity date to an earlier maturity date. 

- Momentum will pay the balance of the Retirement Booster as a cash lump sum. 

###### **Outright cessions** 

On the outright cession of the policy the Retirement Booster value is cancelled.

#### Alterations 

Alteration rules ______________________________________________________________________________________________ 

An alteration is any change to insured life's risk rating factor information (change life details) or covers on an existing contract. 

The following general business rules apply: 

- The policyholder and insured life must both sign the _<u>Myriad consent form</u>_ <u>(MYRIAD015), and the policyholder must accept the quote.</u> 

- If the policy or benefit is ceded, the cessionary needs to consent if any negative 

- alterations are done. 

- Alteration quotes on VIA will either include a short declaration (when applicable) or a confirmation that an application needs to be completed. 

- A counteroffer may change the structure of the original request (e.g. increasing a stand-alone benefit with loadings as opposed to increasing an existing benefit with standard rates). 

- Alterations cannot be done before the starting date of a new policy. 

Note: A signed _<u>Myriad consent form</u>_ <u>(MYRIAD015)</u> is required for all alterations 

###### **Information on the application form and quote are different** 

If the information on the application form and the quote are different, the financial adviser must redo the quote before submitting the case to Underwriting. 

Any changes to personal information may impact the quoted premiums. 

If the quote is more expensive by LESS than R50.00, Momentum will accept the quote and update the case. Refer to the contractual premium to calculate the difference (more or less than R50). 

Discounted premiums cannot be guaranteed in most instances. (e.g. Momentum cannot be certain that the BMI used in the quote was correct). 

###### **Validity period of the alteration quote and alteration application** 

The alteration quote and alteration application must not be older than 21 days on the day: 

- Momentum receives them 

- the alteration application was signed. 

Momentum may accept a signed quote that is older than 21 days but not older than three months, provided that the policy did not pass an anniversary date, an insured life's birthday or there were no changes to the policy in the period that the quote was printed, and the date Momentum received it. 

###### **Effective date** 

Alterations are effective from the first of the month following the date on which all requirements were met. If the date is moved to the first of the next month, the insured life is covered for the increased risk from the date all requirements were met. 

If the update corresponds to the quote in all respects except the effective alteration date, a new alteration quote is not required. The application form and the alteration quote will state that the effective alteration date will be moved if all requirements are not met on or before the date quoted. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 22 

If the update differs from the quote in any way except for the effective alteration date, a new signed alteration quote is required if the premium difference is more than R50. 

###### **Alteration replacing existing cover** 

Momentum require financial advisers to complete a _<u>Replacement Advice Record</u>_ <u>(RAR). The alteration with Momentum may be replacing cover at another insurer</u> and should only go in force once that insurer has confirmed that Momentum may proceed. 

Alterations will always be applied from the first of the following month. 

Free cover will apply between the acceptance date and the starting date of the altered benefits. 

###### **Myriad replacement policy** 

Myriad does not allow replacements of _"like for like"_ benefits. 

###### **Negative alterations** 

The following rules apply to negative alterations: 

- Momentum will backdate alterations if the policy is in arrears or the debit date has not been reached, unless otherwise stated in writing. 

- All alterations require an accepted quote (for positive and negative alterations). 

- Email requests for an alteration received from the financial adviser or policyholder will not be processed. 

- Skipping of annual increases can be accepted with a written request from the policyholder or an instruction from the email address on record. 

Refer to Documents required for alterations for a list of the documents required when an alteration is done.

#### Commission 

General ______________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

All commission is paid in Rands. 

Commission is calculated in accordance with current legislation on the premium that the policyholder has to pay. 

The commission term in respect of the Funeral Benefit for extended family members, is limited to 10 years. 

Level of maximum commission taken. 

- The financial adviser may choose the level of maximum commission required (between 0% and 100%). The Modified Death Benefit allows a choice of between 0% and 50% commission. 

- The financial adviser may not change his level of maximum commission after the benefit is accepted unless an alteration was made. 

- Every stand-alone benefit has its own level of maximum commission. 

- All financial advisers on a specific stand-alone benefit have the same level of maximum commission. 

- Commission is paid at the same level of maximum commission as the standalone benefit with the highest level of maximum commission on the policy fee. This rule will also be applied to any stand-alone benefits added to the policy by the policyholder's direct instruction. 

Multiple financial advisers 

- Different financial advisers may split the commission for a stand-alone benefit. 

- The commission split between financial advisers may only be changed if the policyholder makes an alteration to the stand-alone benefit concerned. 

- Momentum communicates with only one financial adviser per policy. 

- The financial adviser for communication can be changed at any stage at the policyholder request. 

Upfront and as-and-when commission _________________________________________________________ 

A percentage of the commission is chosen as upfront commission. This percentage may not change during the term of a benefit. 

The remaining percentage applies to ongoing commission. The term of the benefit determines the as-and-when commission percentage applicable to a benefit. 

The as-and-when commission is paid on the payable premium regardless of whether the premium changed due to an alteration. 

The amount of commission taken up front is chosen on an individual product level. 

A different percentage can be chosen for each main benefit and all ancillary benefits will follow the same values as the main benefit. 

The as-and-when percentage applicable to a benefit is recalculated to take account of the outstanding term on the benefit whenever the payable premium increases. 

A lump sum commission payment is made at: 

- the start of the policy and 

- on the first policy anniversary. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 26 

###### **Claw-back for as-and–when commission** 

If a policy lapses after two premiums have not been received, the As-and-When commission paid on the two premiums will be clawed back. 

- All commission paid is clawed back for benefits that lapsed within the first six months of the start date. 

- If the benefits are reinstated and the arrear premiums waived, Momentum will not refund the clawed back commission provided the policy lapsed more than six months since its inception. 

- If the benefit is reinstated with all arrear premiums paid, Momentum will refund the As-and-When commission which was clawed back. 

###### **Claw-back for upfront commission** 

All upfront commission is clawed back if the benefit lapsed in the first six months since the start date. 

A policy which lapses will generate negative commission which can be clawed back from any commission payments received in the past 24 months.

#### Stand-alone and ancillary benefits 

Certain benefits are available as stand-alone as well as ancillary benefits. 

Stand-alone __________________________________________________________________________________________________ If a stand-alone benefit ends, all ancillary benefits attached to this benefit are cancelled. Ancillary benefits _____________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The policyholder may only choose one of the following benefits from each category listed below: 

- Disability or impairment benefits 

- Critical illness benefits 

- Future cover benefits 

- • Living benefits. 

The benefit amount may not be more than the stand-alone benefit to which it is attached. 

The term of the ancillary benefit may not be longer than the term of the stand-alone benefit. 

If the ancillary benefit is attached to a stand-alone benefit with a fixed term, the term of the ancillary benefit may not be shorter than the stand-alone benefit, except if the term of the ancillary benefit is limited to a specific age. 

The premium pattern of the ancillary benefit is the same as the premium pattern of the stand-alone benefit. 

The guarantee term of the ancillary benefit is the same as the guarantee term of the stand-alone benefit. 

If the term of the ancillary benefit is shorter than the stand-alone benefit to which it is attached, the premium for the ancillary benefit will fall away at the end of the term of the ancillary benefit. 

The contract benefit premium reduces if an ancillary benefit falls away due to a claim. 

A claim on an ancillary benefit will reduce a benefit amount as follows: 

- The benefit amount of the ancillary benefit on which there was a claim reduces by the claim amount. 

- The benefit amount under any other ancillary benefit attached to the same stand-alone benefit will remain unchanged if the benefit amount of this other ancillary is less than the reduced stand-alone benefit amount. 

- The benefit amount of the other ancillary is reduced to the same level as the reduced stand-alone benefit amount if the benefit amount of the other ancillary is greater than the reduced stand-alone benefit amount. 

- The benefit amount of the stand-alone benefit reduces by the claim amount on the ancillary benefit. 

- A claim on a stand-alone benefit will reduce the benefit amount of all ancillary benefits attached to that stand-alone benefit. The benefit amounts will reduce as follows: 

   - The benefit amount of the stand-alone benefit reduces by the claim amount. 

   - − The benefit amount of any ancillary benefit reduces by the same proportion as the benefit amount of the stand-alone benefit reduces.

#### Education Protector 

Benefits _____________________________________________________________________________________ 

Momentum offers a choice of three Education Protectors: 

- Education Protector – Death 

- Education Protector – Death and Disability 

- Education Protector – Death and Impairment 

Description __________________________________________________________________________________ 

###### **Education Protector – Death** 

Momentum will 

- pay the full benefit amount as a lump sum on the death of the insured life OR 

- • return all premiums paid, at the end of the benefit term. 

###### **Education Protector – Death and Disability** 

Momentum will: 

- pay the full benefit amount as a lump sum on the death of the insured life, OR 

- • pay the full benefit amount as a lump sum if the insured life suffers a disability caused by a bodily injury or illness to such an extent that he is totally and permanently unable to perform the normal duties of his own occupation (up to the policy anniversary before the insured life's 65th birthday), OR 

- pay the full benefit amount if the insured life meets the requirements of one of the defined functional impairment claim events with 100% payout (up to the policy anniversary before the insured life's 70th birthday), OR 

- return all premiums paid, at the end of the benefit term. 

###### **Education Protector – Death and Impairment** 

Momentum will: 

- pay the full benefit amount as a lump sum on the death of the insured life, OR 

- • pay the full benefit amount as a lump sum if the insured life meets the requirements of one of the defined functional impairment claim events with 100% payout (up to the policy anniversary before the insured life's 70th birthday), OR 

- return all premiums paid, at the end of the benefit term. 

Special conditions ________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The policyholder can only link one child to the benefit. 

The child must be the biological child or the legally adopted child of the insured life. Benefits can only be linked to children aged 15 next birthday and younger. 

The maximum annual benefit amount linked to any one child on a policy is R120 000.

###### Stand-alone

All lives are eligible subject to age limits and underwriting.

###### **Occupational disability** 

Occupational disability claims are only applicable to Education Protector – Disability. 

An occupational disability is a disability caused by a bodily injury or illness to such an extent that the insured life is totally and permanently unable to perform the normal duties of their own occupation (up to the policy anniversary before the insured life's 65th birthday). 

The insured life will not qualify for a claim under the occupational disability criteria if the insured life is not gainfully employed at the time of the claim event occurring. Such a claim will be assessed against the impairment and illness criteria. 

Momentum will not pay a claim if the insured life is not receiving or is refusing the medical treatment, they could reasonably be expected to undergo according to current best practice medical protocols and which could substantially improve or remove the condition being claimed for. 

###### **Functional impairment** 

Functional impairment claims are only applicable to Education Protector – Disability and Education Protector – Functional Impairment 

The claim events are not linked to the insured life's ability to perform occupational activities. 

The claim amount is based on the severity of a medical impairment that occurs after the starting date of the benefit as diagnosed by an appropriate specialist (registered with the Health Professions Council of South Africa (HPCSA) and resulting in the specified functional restrictions defined below. 

The insured life must undergo reasonable optimal treatment and their functional impairment will be determined after they have reached (reasonable) Maximal Medical Improvement (MMI). At this stage, a specialist approved by Momentum must declare the functional impairment total, permanent, and continuous for the foreseeable future. 

The insured life will not be required to undergo reasonable optimal treatment if a specialist that Momentum has approved has established that the functional impairment is permanent, and that further treatment will not lessen the severity of the condition. 

- Reasonable optimal treatment: This is the treatment that Momentum may reasonably expect the insured life to undergo according to the guidelines for the specific condition under the generally accepted medical practice at claim stage. The insured life is expected to comply with their treatment routine. 

- Maximal Medical Improvement (MMI): A condition or state that is well stabilised and unlikely to change substantially in the next year with or without medical treatment. There may be some change over time, but further recovery is not expected. 

A panel of accredited medical specialists will determine how many Activities of Daily Living (ADL) the insured life can perform. 

A claim will be admitted only if the claim event is a permanent condition. 

Momentum will pay for the event that provides the highest payout if the insured life qualifies for a claim amount payment under more than one of the impairment events. 

Refer to Appendix 1 in the technical guide for the functional impairment claim events.

#### Funeral Benefit 

Description _______________________________________________________________________________ 

Momentum will pay the benefit amount as a lump sum on the death of the insured life. 

Special conditions ____________________________________________________________________________________________ 

###### **General** 

The following lives may be added as insured lives (per policy): 

- one or two underwritten insured lives 

- five children 

- eight extended family members. 

Momentum does not require any medical underwriting in respect of children and extended family members. 

The underwritten insured life will be required to provide a health declaration on behalf of their children and extended family. 

###### **Extended family members** 

Extended family members are the biological parents of an underwritten insured life under the Funeral Benefit, the parents that legally adopted him, his parents- in-law or his biological or legally adopted children. 

The extended family members must be permanent residents of the Republic of South Africa. 

###### **Children** 

Children are the biological or legally adopted children of an underwritten insured life under the Funeral Benefit that is a permanent resident of the Republic of South Africa. 

A stillbirth benefit is included for all female underwritten insured lives. The benefit is applicable to babies that die after 28 weeks of pregnancy but before delivery. 

Momentum will pay up to a maximum of two claims under this benefit. 

###### **Expiry of cover for Children** 

All children covered under the Funeral benefit issued after September 2010 will automatically be converted to an extended family member on the expiry of the child benefit at age 19 next birthday. 

All children covered under the Funeral Benefit issued before September 2010 will fall away at the policy anniversary before age 19 next birthday. The policyholder may add the child insured life as an Extended family member through an alteration. 

The child insured life that is converted to an extended family member will retain the benefit amount before the conversion. 

The premium and cover will change every year in the same way as normal extended family members.

Beneficiaries and cessions ________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The policyholder may only appoint a beneficiary for the Instant Cash feature. 

Momentum Trust Limited will automatically be the beneficiary of the remainder of the benefit amount excluding the instant cash payout. 

The policyholder cannot change Momentum Trust Limited as the beneficiary on this benefit. 

Cessions are not allowed. 

Instant Cash ______________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The nominated beneficiary (if applicable) will receive a proportion of the benefit amount, currently 10% of the benefit amount, limited to R50 000 per insured life, within one working day of the submission of the death claim. This excludes any payment made under the Instant Cash feature for the Death Benefit. The balance of the claim amount will be paid to the Momentum Trust Limited if the claim is admitted. 

If a beneficiary was not nominated, the full claim amount will be paid to Momentum Trust Limited (Momentum Trust), who will use the payout as described in the Executorship and Executor Fee Benefit and the Professional Fee Benefit clauses. 

Momentum will only make this payment if the insured life dies more than two years after the starting date of the Death Benefit. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 3 

When restarting the benefit, a new two-year period will apply. If a policyholder increases the benefit amount, a new two-year period will apply for the increased portion from the date of the increase. By paying the Instant Cash amount, Momentum does not acknowledge the validity of the death claim. If a claim is not admitted when it is assessed, the balance of the amount being claimed will not be paid. In addition, the policyholder will have to repay Momentum the Instant Cash amount that was paid to them. 

Terminal Illness __________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

Momentum will **<u>not</u>** pay a claim before the death of the insured life if they contract a terminal illness that in the opinion of Momentum’s Medical Officer will with reasonable certainty result in their death within 12 months of the date that medical evidence to that effect is provided. 

Will and Safe-Custody Benefit ____________________________________________________________________________________ 

Momentum Trust will draft the policyholder’s will and once signed, it will be collected and it will held in safe-custody by Momentum Trust. 

The policyholder may review his/her will from time to time. 

There is no additional cost for the drafting, collection, safe custody or reviews of the will. 

Executorship and Executor Fee Benefit ___________________________________________________________________________ 

Momentum Trust must be nominated as the executor of the estate in order to attend to the administration of the estate. 

The benefit will cover 100% of the executors’ fees on the estate if the maximum gross value of the estate, reflected in the Liquidation and Distribution Account, is less than R10 million. 

For estates with a gross value of less than R10 million, Momentum Trust guarantees a discount, as determined from time to time on the fixed Government Regulation fee, for acting as the executor. 

If the gross value of the estate exceeds R10 million, Momentum Trust guarantees a 50% discount on the fixed Government Regulation fee for acting as the executor. 

No executor fees will be charged on the benefit amount payable from the Estate Provider Benefit to the estate. 

The minimum executors fee payable by the estate will be R50 000 (excluding VAT). 

Professional Fee Benefit __________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The Estate Provider Benefit amount paid to Momentum Trust, which is only made after payment of the Instant Cash Benefit to the nominated beneficiary (if applicable), will be used to settle all professional fees incurred during the administration process. 

These costs will be paid in the following order: 

- The balance of the benefit amount, after the Instant Cash pay-out (if applicable), will be used to pay for executor fees. 

- The balance of the benefit amount, after the payment of the executor fees, will be used to settle the following Administration fees: 

   - Advice fee payable to the servicing financial planner of R20 000 

   - Fees payable to the Master of the High Court of the Republic of South Africa 

   - Fees incurred in the conveyance of property from the estate to the beneficiary/ies 

   - Fees incurred in transferring any motor vehicles to the beneficiary/ies 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 4 

- Costs associated with the collection, storage and relicensing of firearms in terms of the Firearms Control Act (No. 60 of 2000) 

- Sworn Appraiser’s valuation fees 

- Trustee fees 

Estate Top-up Benefit ____________________________________________________________________________________________ 

If the total value of the claim for attending to the administration of the estate (instant cash, executor fee, professional and financial adviser fees) is less than the Estate Provider benefit amount, Momentum Trust will pay this difference into the estate. 

No executor fees will be charged on the benefit amount payable from the Estate Provider Benefit to your estate, only if Momentum Trust is the executor of the estate. 

This payment must be used to settle expenses and/or liabilities not covered by the benefit or distributed to the heirs in the event that all expenses or liabilities are settled. 

Forfeiture clause _________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

In the event of the death of the insured life, Momentum Trust will receive the benefit amount, as defined in the policy contract, and use the payout as described in the Executorship and Executor Fee Benefit, Professional Fee Benefit and Estate Top-up Benefit clauses. 

The estate will only be indemnified against executor fees incurred if: 

- Momentum Trust is appointed as the sole executor on the estate and; 

- the gross value of the estate as reflected in the liquidation account is below R10 million and 

- the minimum cover amount was taken out. 

If another person or legal entity is appointed as executor and/or trustee or if this person or legal entity elects not to appoint Momentum Trust to provide the abovementioned services, the appointed executor on the insured life’s estate, may institute a claim against the Estate Provider Benefit. 

A cancellation fee, which is equal to one and a half times Momentum Trust’s minimum executor’s fee, as applicable at the time of the claim, will be deducted from the benefit amount. 

The remaining portion will be paid into the bank account opened by the executor of the insured life’s estate in the name of the estate. 

The policyholder will not enjoy the discounts, benefits, and services as described in the Executorship and Executor Fee Benefit, Professional Fee Benefit and Estate Top-up Benefit clauses.

The death of the insured life.

Tapering _____________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The policyholder can choose between tapering or no tapering. 

Momentum will reduce the lump-sum benefit amount annually in even amounts by the chosen tapering option, until it reaches zero. 

Tapering starts from the benefit anniversary after the insured life's chosen tapering age to the end of the benefit term. 

The benefit amount can reduce by: 

- 20% a year during the last five years of the benefit term 

- 10% a year during the last ten years of the benefit term 

Tapering is not available on term benefits. 

The last voluntary premium or benefit increase will occur on the benefit anniversary before the insured life’s chosen tapering age.

Beneficiaries and cessions ____________________________________________________________________________________ 

The policyholder may not nominate beneficiaries. 

Collateral cessions are allowed on the stand-alone benefit. 

Claim event __________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The insured life can qualify for a claim under either: 

- Occupational disability or 

- Functional impairment 

###### **Occupational disability** 

An occupational disability is a disability caused by a bodily injury or illness to such an extent that the insured life is totally and permanently unable to perform the normal duties of their own occupation (up to the policy anniversary before the insured life's 65th birthday). 

The insured life will not qualify for a claim under the occupational disability criteria if the insured life is not gainfully employed at the time of the claim event occurring. Such a claim will be assessed against the impairment and illness criteria. 

Momentum will not pay a claim if the insured life is not receiving or is refusing the medical treatment they could reasonably be expected to undergo according to current best practice medical protocols and which could substantially improve or remove the condition being claimed for. 

###### **Functional impairment** 

The claim events are not linked to the insured life's ability to perform occupational activities. 

The claim event is based on a medical impairment that occurs after the start date of the benefit as diagnosed by an appropriate specialist (registered with the Health Professions Council of South Africa (HPCSA) and resulting in the specified functional restrictions defined below. 

The insured life must undergo reasonable optimal treatment, and their functional impairment will be determined after they have reached (reasonable) Maximal Medical Improvement (MMI). At this stage, a specialist approved by Momentum must declare the functional impairment total, permanent and continuous for the foreseeable future. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 4 

The insured life will not be required to undergo reasonable optimal treatment if a specialist that Momentum has approved has established that the functional impairment is permanent, and that further treatment will not lessen the severity of the condition. 

- Reasonable optimal treatment: This is the treatment that Momentum may reasonably expect the insured life to undergo according to the guidelines for the specific condition under the generally accepted medical practice at claim stage. The insured life is expected to comply with their treatment routine. 

- Maximal Medical Improvement (MMI): A condition or state that is well stabilised and unlikely to change substantially in the next year with or without medical treatment. There may be some change over time, but further recovery is not expected. 

Momentum will not pay a claim if the insured life is not receiving or is refusing the medical treatment they could reasonably be expected to undergo according to current best practice medical protocols and which could substantially improve or remove the condition being claimed for. 

A panel of accredited medical specialists will determine how many Activities of Daily Living (ADL) the insured life can perform. 

A claim will be admitted only if the claim event is a permanent condition. 

Refer to Appendix 1 in the technical guide for the functional impairment claim events. 

Claim amount ________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

###### **Occupational disability** 

The claim amount is the full benefit amount. 

###### **Functional impairment** 

The functional impairment claim events are divided into categories. 

For certain categories, claim payments are divided into severity levels, depending on the severity of the functional impairment event. 

Each level has an associated "percentage payout". 

For the first claim, the claim amount is calculated as the percentage payout multiplied by the benefit amount. The benefit amount for this benefit will be reduced by the claim amount. 

The claim amount for a subsequent claim in a different category is calculated by multiplying the percentage payout by the reduced benefit amount. This amount is paid, irrespective of the relative severity level of the new claim and the original claim. 

A subsequent claim in the same category will only be paid if the claim event is more severe than previous claims in the same category. The claim amount paid is based on the difference between the percentage payout for the new claim and the total percentage paid for that category (the "additional percentage payout"). In this case, the claim amount is calculated as the additional percentage payout multiplied by the benefit amount (only adjusted for claims in other categories). 

Related claims: A related claim is where the claim event progressed from a previous claim event. Momentum will treat a claim that is related to any previous claim in a different category as if it is in the same category as the claim it progressed from. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 5 

If more than one claim event occurs as a result of the same cause, a claim will be admitted for the claim event resulting in the highest payment. 

Momentum will always pay the balance of the benefit amount for claims with a percentage payout of 100%. 

###### **General** 

If tapering is selected, the lump sum benefit amount will be reduced to zero evenly from the benefit anniversary after the insured life's chosen tapering age, to the benefit anniversary before the insured life's chosen expiry age. 

Any outstanding debt will be deducted from the claim amount. 

If a claim for the full benefit amount is admitted, the benefit will be cancelled and the contract benefit premium reduced. 

The benefit premium will not reduce in the event of a partial claim. 

Waiting period _______________________________________________________________________________________________ 

There is no explicit waiting period. 

A claim will only be admitted once we have established the permanency of the disability according to our definition. 

No claim will be admitted if the insured life dies before permanency is established. 

Survival period _______________________________________________________________________________________________ 

There is no explicit survival period. 

A claim will only be admitted if the insured life meets the requirements of the defined claim event, prior to their death. 

No medical test or examination concluded after the insured life’s death will be considered when evaluating a claim. 

Conversion option ____________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The policyholder has the option to convert this benefit (stand-alone and ancillary) to a Functional Protector or a Complete Functional Protector. 

These benefits pay a monthly claim amount for the remainder of the insured's life if they are permanently impaired (subject to the benefit limits that apply at the time of the conversion). 

A claim will not be paid under the Functional Protector or Complete Functional Protector, that was converted from an existing disability or impairment benefit if the claim event occurred before the conversion. 

A partial conversion will not be allowed 

The policyholder may choose any increase option and premium pattern for the Functional Protector or Complete Functional Protector subject to the new business rules. 

When the benefit is converted, the policyholder must add a premium waiver to the Functional Protector or Complete Functional Protector. If this is the same Premium Waiver as the one on the previous policy the only underwriting required will be a declaration of health. The policyholder may select any increase option on the waiver of premium (increasing or level). The new waiver of premium will be subject to new business age and benefit limits. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 6 

A new policy contract will be issued for the Functional Protector or Complete Functional Protector on conversion. 

The conversion will be an add and remove alteration. If this benefit is added without the removal of the benefit being converted, normal underwriting will apply. 

If the benefit being converted is removed or it is within three months of the expiry, special underwriting conditions will apply. 

###### **If tapering was not selected:** 

The monthly income for the benefit issued under this conversion option is limited to 1% of the benefit amount at the time of the conversion. 

###### **If tapering was selected:** 

The monthly income for the benefit issued under this conversion option is limited to 1% of: 

- the benefit amount at the time of the conversion if tapering has not started, or 

- the benefit amount before the tapering started. 

###### **Medical underwriting will be required if:** 

- any specific exclusion applies to this benefit, or 

- a health or occupational loading applies to this benefit. 

End of benefit ____________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

This benefit ends on the earliest of: 

- The death of the insured life. 

- The end of the benefit term. 

- The payment of the full benefit amount. 

- Conversion to a Functional Protector or Complete Functional Protector 

- The cancellation of the policy or benefit as a result of: 

   - any event covered in the policy contract 

   - notification from the policyholder.

Claim event ______________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The insured life can qualify for a claim under either: 

- Occupational disability or 

- Functional impairment 

###### **Occupational disability** 

An occupational disability is a disability caused by a bodily injury or illness to such an extent that the insured life is totally and permanently unable to perform the normal duties of their own occupation. 

The insured life will not qualify for a claim under the occupational disability criteria if the insured life is not gainfully employed at the time of the claim event occurring. Such a claim will be assessed against the impairment and illness criteria. 

Momentum will not pay a claim if the insured life is not receiving or is refusing the medical treatment they could reasonably be expected to undergo according to current best practice medical protocols and which could substantially improve or remove the condition being claimed for. 

###### **Functional impairment** 

The claim events are not linked to the insured life's ability to perform occupational activities. 

The claim event is based on a medical impairment that occurs after the start date of the benefit as diagnosed by an appropriate specialist (registered with the Health Professions Council of South Africa (HPCSA) and resulting in the specified functional restrictions defined below. 

The insured life must undergo reasonable optimal treatment and their functional impairment will be determined after they have reached (reasonable) Maximal Medical Improvement (MMI). At this stage a specialist approved by Momentum must declare the functional impairment total, permanent and continuous for the foreseeable future. The insured life will not be required to undergo reasonable optimal treatment if a specialist, that Momentum has approved, has established that the functional impairment is permanent, and that further treatment will not lessen the severity of the condition. 

- Reasonable optimal treatment: This is the treatment that Momentum may reasonably expect the insured life to undergo according to the guidelines for the specific condition under the generally accepted medical practice at claim stage. The insured life is expected to comply with their treatment routine.

Activities of Daily Work ___________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The insured life will be assessed against one of two categories. The category used will depend on the occupational duties performed by the insured life at the time of a claim and the occupation like it is usually performed in the open labour market. Assessments will be done by our panel of specialists. If the insured life’s occupational duties has changed in the six months before the claim event occurred, the insured life will have to achieve a total score of six for the set of tests on both categories (relating to the current occupational duties and the previous occupational duties) for us to admit a claim. Each occupational definition category has different tests and different points are allocated to the various severity/ability levels. 

The category that we use will depend on the proportion of time that the insured life normally spends on performing the following duties: Supervisory, Administrative and Other duties. Insured lives that spend more than 75% of their time on supervisory and administrative duties, will be assessed against category 1, and other insured lives against category 2. 

The insured life needs to achieve a total score of 6 or more on the following tests before we will consider a claim. Only one item in each of the tests may be selected before the total score is calculated.

#### ADW Disability Benefit 

Description ___________________________________________________________________________________ 

Momentum will pay the full benefit amount as a lump sum if the insured life: 

- the full benefit amount as a lump sum if the insured life meets the requirements of the Activities of Daily Work (ADW) claim events (up to the policy anniversary before the insured life's 65th birthday). OR 

- meets the requirements of one of the defined functional impairment claim events with 100% payout. 

Type of benefit ___________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

Stand-alone or ancillary 

Eligible lives ______________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

All lives are eligible, subject to age limits and underwriting.
