Tapering _________________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The policyholder can choose between tapering or no tapering. 

Momentum will reduce the lump-sum benefit amount annually in even amounts by the chosen tapering option, until it reaches zero. 

Tapering starts from the benefit anniversary after the insured life's chosen tapering age to the end of the benefit term. 

The benefit amount can reduce by: 

- 20% a year during the last five years of the benefit term 

- 10% a year during the last ten years of the benefit term 

Tapering is not available on term benefits. 

The last voluntary premium or benefit increase will occur on the benefit anniversary before the insured life’s chosen tapering age. 

Premium patterns ________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The policyholder may choose one of the following premium patterns: 

- Level 

- LifeStage 

- Aggressive LifeStage 

- Compulsory 

Premium guarantee ______________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The premium guarantee depends on the chosen premium pattern: 

|Term|Premium pattern|Premium guarantee|
|---|---|---|
|To age 65|Level; Compulsory; LifeStage;<br>Aggressive LifeStage|Standard or Extended|
|Term|The premium is guaranteed for|the term of the benefit.|



Increase options _________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The policyholder may choose either voluntary premium or benefit amount increases. Voluntary premium increases are not available on LifeStage premium patterns. 

The last voluntary increase will take place on the benefit anniversary before the insured life's chosen tapering age. 

|Premium pattern|Premium increases|Benefit amount increases|
|---|---|---|
|Level|0%, 3 — 20%, CPI|0%, 3 — 10%, CPI, RDI|
|LifeStage|Age related increases only|0%, 3 — 10%, CPI, RDI|
|Aggressive LifeStage|Age related increases only|0%, 3 — 10%, CPI, RDI|
|Compulsory|3 — 20%|0%, 3 — 10%, CPI, RDI|

Page 3 

Additional features _______________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The following additional features are available free of charge: 

- Free Cover 

- Retirement Booster 

- • LifeReturns® 

Ancillary benefits_________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The policyholder may add the following ancillary benefits: 

- Premium Waiver (increasing or level) - Death 

- Premium Waiver (increasing or level) - Comprehensive Disability 

- Premium Waiver (increasing or level) - Functional Impairment 

- Premium Waiver - Retrenchment 

- Longevity Protector®- Disability 

Beneficiaries and cessions ________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The policyholder may not nominate beneficiaries. 

Collateral cessions are allowed on the stand-alone benefit. 

Claim event ______________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The insured life can qualify for a claim under either: 

- Activities of Daily Work (ADW) or 

- Functional impairment 

###### **Activities of Daily Work (ADW)** 

The insured life is assessed on one of two occupational definition categories. Momentum will base the definition on the one that most closely matches the insured life's occupation at the time of the claim and the occupation as it is usually performed in the open labour market. 

A panel of Momentum specialists will do the assessments. 

Each occupation definition category has different tests, and different points are allocated to the various severity/ability levels. 

The Activities of Daily Work (ADW) claim event is applicable up to the policy anniversary before the insured life's 65th birthday. 

The insured life will not qualify for a claim under the occupational disability criteria if they are not gainfully employed at the time of the claim event.. Such a claim will be assessed against the impairment and illness criteria. 

Momentum will not pay a claim if the insured life is not receiving or is refusing the medical treatment, they could reasonably be expected to undergo according to current best practice medical protocols and could substantially improve or remove the condition being claimed for. 

###### **Functional impairment** 

The claim events are linked to the insured life's ability to perform occupational activities. 

The claim event is based on a medical impairment that occurs after the start date of the benefit as diagnosed by an appropriate specialist (registered with the Health Professions Council of South Africa (HPCSA) and resulting in the specified functional restrictions defined below. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 4 

The insured life must undergo reasonable optimal treatment and their functional impairment will be determined after they have reached (reasonable) Maximal Medical Improvement (MMI). At this stage, a specialist approved by Momentum must declare the functional impairment total, permanent and continuous for the foreseeable future. The insured life will not be required to undergo reasonable optimal treatment if a specialist that Momentum has approved has established that the functional impairment is permanent, and that further treatment will not lessen the severity of the condition. 

- Reasonable optimal treatment: This is the treatment that Momentum may reasonably expect the insured life to undergo according to the guidelines for the specific condition under the generally accepted medical practice at claim stage. The insured  is expected to comply with their treatment routine. 

- Maximal Medical Improvement (MMI): A condition or state that is well stabilised and unlikely to change substantially in the next year with or without medical treatment. There may be some change over time, but further recovery is not expected. 

Momentum will not pay a claim if the insured life is not receiving or is refusing the medical treatment they could reasonably be expected to undergo according to current best practice medical protocols, and which could substantially improve or remove the condition being claimed for. 

A panel of accredited medical specialists will determine how many Activities of Daily Living (ADL) and Activities of Daily Work (ADW) the insured life can perform. 

A claim will be admitted only if the claim event is a permanent condition. 

Refer to Appendix 1 in the technical guide for the functional impairment claim events. 

Claim amount ____________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

Momentum will pay the full benefit amount if the insured life meets the requirements of one of the defined claim events. 

If tapering is selected, the lump sum benefit amount will be reduced to zero evenly from the benefit anniversary after the insured life's chosen tapering age, to the end of the benefit term. 

Any outstanding debt will be deducted from the claim amount. 

If a claim for the full benefit amount is admitted, the benefit will be cancelled and the contract benefit premium reduced. 

Survival period ___________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

There is no explicit survival period. 

A claim will only be admitted if the insured life meets the requirements of the defined claim event, prior to their death. 

No medical test or examination concluded after the insured life’s death will be considered when evaluating a claim. 

Conversion option _______________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The policyholder has the option to convert this benefit (stand-alone and ancillary) to a Functional Protector or a Complete Functional Protector. 

These benefits pay a monthly claim amount for the remainder of the insured's life if they are permanently impaired (subject to the benefit limits that apply at the time of the conversion). 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 5 

A claim will not be paid under the Functional Protector or Complete Functional Protector that was converted from an existing disability or impairment benefit if the claim event occurred before the conversion. 

A partial conversion will not be allowed 

The policyholder may choose any increase option and premium pattern for the Functional Protector or Complete Functional Protector subject to the new business rules. 

When the benefit is converted, the policyholder must add a premium waiver to the Functional Protector or Complete Functional Protector. If this is the same Premium Waiver as the one on the previous policy the only underwriting required will be a declaration of health. The policyholder may select any increase option on the waiver of premium (increasing or level). The new waiver of premium will be subject to new business age and benefit limits. 

A new policy contract will be issued for the Functional Protector or Complete Functional Protector on conversion. 

The conversion will be an add and remove alteration. If this benefit is added without the removal of the benefit being converted, normal underwriting will apply. 

If the benefit being converted is removed or it is within three months of the expiry, special underwriting conditions will apply. 

###### **If tapering was not selected:** 

The monthly income for the benefit issued under this conversion option is limited to 1% of the benefit amount at the time of the conversion. 

###### **If tapering was selected:** 

The monthly income for the benefit issued under this conversion option is limited to 1% of: 

- the benefit amount at the time of the conversion if tapering has not started, or 

- the benefit amount before the tapering started. 

###### **Medical underwriting will be required if:** 

- any specific exclusion applies to this benefit, or 

- a health or occupational loading applies to this benefit. 

End of benefit ____________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

This benefit ends on the earliest of: 

- The death of the insured life. 

- The end of the benefit term. 

- The payment of the full benefit amount. 

- Conversion to a Functional Protector or Complete Functional Protector 

- The cancellation of the policy or benefit as a result of: 

   - any event covered in the policy contract 

   - notification from the policyholder. 

Claim requirements ______________________________________________________________________________________________ 

Refer to the Claim requirements section of this technical guide for information on the documents required to assess a claim under this benefit. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 6 

Activities of Daily Work ___________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The insured life will be assessed against one of two categories. The category used will depend on the occupational duties performed by the insured life at the time of a claim and the occupation like it is usually performed in the open labour market. Assessments will be done by our panel of specialists. If the insured life’s occupational duties have changed in the six months before the claim event occurred, the insured life will have to achieve a total score of six for the set of tests on both categories (relating to the current occupational duties and the previous occupational duties) for us to admit a claim. Each occupational definition category has different tests and different points are allocated to the various severity/ability levels. 

The category that we use will depend on the proportion of time that the insured life normally spends on performing the following duties: Supervisory, Administrative and Other duties. Insured lives that spend more than 75% of their time on supervisory and administrative duties, will be assessed against category 1, and other insured lives against category 2. 

The insured life needs to achieve a total score of 6 or more on the following tests before we will consider a claim. Only one item in each of the tests may be selected before the total score is calculated.

Tapering _____________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The policyholder can choose between tapering or no tapering. 

Momentum will reduce the lump-sum benefit amount annually in even amounts by the chosen tapering option, until it reaches zero. 

Tapering starts from the benefit anniversary after the insured life's chosen tapering age to the end of the benefit term. 

The benefit amount can reduce by: 

- 20% a year during the last five years of the benefit term 

- 10% a year during the last ten years of the benefit term. 

Tapering is not available on term benefits. 

The last voluntary premium or benefit increase will occur on the benefit anniversary before the insured life’s chosen tapering age. 

Premium patterns ____________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The policyholder may choose one of the following premium patterns: 

- Level 

- LifeStage 

- Aggressive LifeStage 

- Compulsory

|Student Package|Level; Compulsory; LifeStage|Standard|

Beneficiaries and cessions ____________________________________________________________________________________ 

The policyholder may not nominate beneficiaries. 

Collateral cessions are allowed on the stand-alone benefit. 

Claim event __________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The claim events are not linked to the insured life's ability to perform occupational activities. 

The claim event is based on the severity of a medical impairment that occurs after the starting date of the benefit as diagnosed by an appropriate specialist (registered with the Health Professions Council of South Africa (HPCSA) and resulting in the specified functional restrictions defined below. 

The insured life must undergo reasonable optimal treatment, and their functional impairment will be determined after they have reached (reasonable) Maximal Medical Improvement (MMI). At this stage, a specialist approved by Momentum must declare the functional impairment total, permanent and continuous for the foreseeable future. The insured life will not be required to undergo reasonable optimal treatment if a specialist that Momentum has approved has established that the functional impairment is permanent, and that further treatment will not lessen the severity of the condition. 

- Reasonable optimal treatment: This is the treatment that Momentum may reasonably expect the insured life to undergo according to the guidelines for the specific condition under the generally accepted medical practice at claim stage. The insured life is expected to comply with their treatment routine. 

- Maximal Medical Improvement (MMI): A condition or state that is well stabilised and unlikely to change substantially in the next year with or without medical treatment. There may be some change over time, but further recovery is not expected. 

Momentum will not pay a claim if the insured life is not receiving or is refusing the medical treatment, they could reasonably be expected to undergo according to current best practice medical protocols and which could substantially improve or remove the condition being claimed for. 

A panel of accredited medical specialists will determine how many Activities of Daily Living (ADL) the insured life can perform. 

A claim will be admitted only if the claim event is a permanent condition. 

Refer to Appendix 1 in the technical guide for the functional impairment claim events. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 4 

Claim amount ________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The functional impairment claim events are divided into categories. 

For certain categories, claim payments are divided into severity levels, depending on the severity of the functional impairment event. 

Each level has an associated "percentage payout". 

For the first claim made under the benefit, the claim amount is calculated as the percentage payout multiplied by the benefit amount. The benefit amount for this benefit will be reduced by the claim amount. 

The claim amount for a subsequent claim in a different category is calculated by multiplying the percentage payout by the reduced benefit amount. This amount is paid, irrespective of the relative severity level of the new claim and the original claim. 

A subsequent claim in the same category will only be paid if the claim event is more severe than previous claims in the same category. The claim amount that will be paid is based on the difference between the percentage payout for the new claim and the total percentage paid for that category (the "additional percentage payout"). In this case, the claim amount is calculated as the additional percentage payout, multiplied by the benefit amount (only adjusted for claims in other categories). 

Related claims: A related claim is where the claim event progressed from a previous claim event. Momentum will treat a claim that is related to any previous claim in a different category as if it is in the same category as the claim it progressed from. 

If more than one claim event occurs as a result of the same cause, a claim will be admitted for the claim event resulting in the highest payment. 

Momentum will always pay the balance of the benefit amount for claims with a percentage payout of 100%.If tapering is selected, the lump sum benefit amount will be reduced to zero evenly from the benefit anniversary after the insured life's chosen tapering age, to the benefit anniversary before the insured life's chosen expiry age. 

Any outstanding debt will be deducted from the claim amount. 

If a claim for the full benefit amount is admitted, the benefit will be cancelled and the contract benefit premium reduced. The benefit premium will not reduce in the event of a partial claim. 

Survival period _______________________________________________________________________________________________ 

There is no explicit survival period. 

A claim will only be admitted if the insured life meets the requirements of the defined claim event, prior to their death. 

No medical test or examination concluded after the insured life’s death will be considered when evaluating a claim. 

Conversion option ____________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The policyholder has the option to convert this benefit (stand-alone and ancillary) to a Functional Protector or a Complete Functional Protector. 

These benefits pay a monthly claim amount for the remainder of the insured's life if they are permanently impaired (subject to the benefit limits that apply at the time of the conversion). 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 5 

A claim will not be paid under the Functional Protector or Complete Functional Protector, that was converted from an existing disability or impairment benefit if the claim event occurred before the conversion. 

A partial conversion will not be allowed 

The policyholder may choose any increase option and premium pattern for the Functional Protector or Complete Functional Protector subject to the new business rules. 

When the benefit is converted, the policyholder must add a premium waiver to the Functional Protector or Complete Functional Protector. If this is the same Premium Waiver as the one on the previous policy the only underwriting required will be a declaration of health. The policyholder may select any increase option on the waiver of premium (increasing or level). The new waiver of premium will be subject to new business age and benefit limits. 

A new policy contract will be issued for the Functional Protector or Complete Functional Protector on conversion. 

The conversion will be an add and remove alteration. If this benefit is added without the removal of the benefit being converted, normal underwriting will apply. 

If the benefit being converted is removed or it is within three months of the expiry, special underwriting conditions will apply. 

###### **If tapering was not selected:** 

The monthly income for the benefit issued under this conversion option is limited to 1% of the benefit amount at the time of the conversion. 

###### **If tapering was selected:** 

The monthly income for the benefit issued under this conversion option is limited to 1% of: 

- the benefit amount at the time of the conversion if tapering has not started, or 

- the benefit amount before the tapering started. 

###### **Medical underwriting will be required if:** 

- any specific exclusion applies to this benefit, or 

- a health or occupational loading applies to this benefit. 

End of benefit ____________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

This benefit ends on the earliest of: 

- The death of the insured life. 

- The end of the benefit term. 

- The payment of the full benefit amount. 

- Conversion to a Functional Protector or Complete Functional Protector 

- The cancellation of the policy or benefit as a result of: 

   - any event covered in the policy contract 

   - notification from the policyholder.

Claim event __________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The insured life can qualify for a claim under either: 

- occupational disability or 

- impairment or illness. 

###### **Occupational disability** 

An occupational disability is a temporary or permanent disability caused by a bodily injury or an illness to such an extent that the insured life is continuously unable to perform the main duties of his own occupation on a total or partial basis. 

A claim amount will only be paid if the insured life is unable to perform at least 25% of the main duties of his own occupation. The claim amount payment will end once the insured life has recovered to the extent that he can perform more than 75% of the main duties of his own occupation. 

The claim amount will be calculated according to the loss of income or the severity of disability criteria. 

The insured life will not qualify for a claim under the occupational disability criteria if the insured life is not gainfully employed at the time of the claim event occurring. Such a claim will be assessed against the impairment and illness criteria. 

Myriad technical guide – December2023 

Page 6 

###### **Impairment or illness** 

The insured life can qualify for a claim under: 

- functional impairment or 

- critical illness or 

- fracture and hospitalisation 

Momentum will pay for the event that provides the highest payout if the insured life qualifies for a claim amount payment under more than one of the impairment or illness claim events. 

If the insured life still qualifies for a functional impairment claim after a critical illness, fracture, or hospitalisation claim has been paid, Momentum will continue to pay the defined payment for the balance of the payment period. 

###### <u>Functional impairment</u> 

The claim events are not linked to the insured life's ability to perform occupational activities. 

The claim amount is based on the severity of a medical impairment that occurs after the starting date of the benefit as diagnosed by an appropriate specialist (registered with the Health Professions Council of South Africa (HPCSA)) and resulting in the specified functional restrictions defined below. 

The insured life will not be able to claim under functional impairment after the chosen expiry age. 

The insured life must undergo reasonable optimal treatment and their functional impairment will be determined after they have reached (reasonable) Maximal Medical Improvement (MMI). At this stage, a specialist approved by Momentum must declare the functional impairment total, permanent, and continuous for the foreseeable future. 

The insured life will not be required to undergo reasonable optimal treatment if a specialist, that Momentum has approved, has established that the functional impairment is permanent, and that further treatment will not lessen the severity of the condition. 

- Reasonable optimal treatment: This is the treatment that Momentum may reasonably expect the insured life to undergo according to the guidelines for the specific condition under the generally accepted medical practice at claim stage. The insured life is expected to comply with his treatment routine. 

- Maximal Medical Improvement (MMI): A condition or state that is well stabilised and unlikely to change substantially in the next year with or without medical treatment. There may be some change over time, but further recovery is not expected. 

A panel of accredited medical specialists will determine how many Activities of Daily Living (ADL) the insured life can perform. 

A claim will be admitted only if the claim event is a permanent condition. 

Momentum will pay for the event that provides the highest payout if the insured life qualifies for a claim amount payment under more than one of the impairment events. 

Refer to Appendix 1 in the technical guide for the functional impairment claim events. 

Myriad technical guide – December2023 

Page 7 

###### <u>Critical illness</u> 

Momentum will pay a percentage of the benefit amount if the insured life meets the requirements of one of the defined critical illnesses claim events. 

Momentum will not pay for a subsequent critical illness claim event while the insured life is receiving a critical illness claim amount payment. 

Refer to Appendix 2 and Appendix 3 in the technical guide for the critical illness claim events. 

###### <u>Fracture and hospitalisation</u> 

Momentum will pay a percentage of the benefit amount if the insured life meets the requirements of one of the defined fracture and hospitalisation claim events. 

Momentum will pay for the event with the longest payment period if the insured life qualifies for a payment under more than one of the defined fracture or hospitalisation claim events. 

Momentum will not pay for a subsequent claim event for fracture or hospitalisation that occurs while the insured life is receiving a fracture and hospitalisation claim amount payment. 

Refer to Appendix 6 in the technical guide for fracture and hospitalisation claim events. 

Claim amount ________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

Momentum will use the following assessment criteria to determine the monthly claim amount and will use the criteria resulting in the highest claim amount: 

- Loss of income 

- Severity of disability 

- Severity of impairment or illness 

###### **Loss of income** 

Momentum will pay the actual loss of income up to the maximum of the benefit amount. 

Actual loss of income is calculated as the difference between the insured life’s predisability net income and any income that the insured life earns during the disability. 

Net income refers to gross income less income tax payable on this income (determined by applying the relevant year of assessment’s income tax tables). 

###### **Severity of disability** 

The claim amount will be between 25% and 100% of the benefit amount, depending on the extent to which the insured life is unable to perform the main duties of his own occupation. 

The severity of disability assessment criteria, including the Partial Claim Upgrade, will only apply during the first year after the claim event. For professional occupations, these criteria will apply for the first two years after the claim event. 

Partial Claim Upgrade 

Myriad technical guide – December2023 

Page 8 

- If the full benefit amount has been paid for a continuous period of three months, the insured life will qualify for a Partial Claim upgrade. 

- Momentum will continue to pay the full benefit amount after the three months, provided that the insured life is partially disabled 

- The full benefit amount will only be paid while the severity of disability assessment criteria applies (the first year after the claim event or the first two years after the claim event for professionals). 

###### **Severity of impairment or illness** 

Momentum will pay a percentage of the benefit amount for a specified payment period if the insured life meets any of the requirements for functional impairment, critical illness or fracture and hospitalisation claim events. 

<mark>Refer to Appendix 6</mark> in the technical guide <mark>for payout levels and payment periods for severity of impairment and illness claim events.</mark> 

###### **General** 

The claim amount is paid monthly in arrears. 

The daily claim amount will be calculated as 1/30 of the monthly benefit amount. 

A proportionate payment will be made in respect of any part of a month should the insured life be rehabilitated before the payment date. Following rehabilitation, the insured life will retain his cover. 

Any outstanding debt will be deducted from the claim amount. 

###### **Premium waiver during a claim** 

The premium will be waived for this benefit while a claim is being paid. 

No proportionate premiums can be paid; therefore, premiums are waived from the next financial month after the expiry of the waiting period. 

If the claim amount is less than the full benefit amount, the whole premium will still be waived. 

For a seven-day or 14-day waiting period, premiums will be waived after the insured life has been continuously disabled for more than 28 days. 

If Momentum collected premiums for a period not applicable for premium payment, it will be refunded to the policyholder as an advance on the policy. This (advance) amount will be deducted from the next premium payment. 

If this benefit is the only benefit on the policy, the policy fee will be waived while a claim is being paid. 

Definition of income _________________________________________________________________________________________ 

Income is defined as one of the following: 

|Gross Taxable Income|The total sum of all taxable income payable or benefits<br>receivable on account of the insured life's employment, or<br>any services rendered by the insured life.|
|---|---|
|Cost to Company<br>Income|This equals Gross Taxable Income plus:<br>•<br>the value of any fringe benefits (as provided for in the<br>Income Tax Act) awarded to the employee,<br>•<br>retirement fund contributions made by the life<br>insured’s employer,|



Myriad technical guide – December2023 

Page 9 

||•<br>the cost of any other benefits paid for by the insured<br>life’s employer, and<br>•<br>any dividends received by the life insured due to<br>shareholding or member’s interest held in the<br>employer (where the employer is a company or close<br>corporation).|
|---|---|
|Gross Professional<br>Income (professionals<br>only)|For professionals that charge a fee for services, this equals<br>the sum of the professional fees and therevenue less cost of<br>salesfrom trading activities, after deducting business<br>overheads expenses.|



**Net income** refers to gross income less income tax payable on this income (determined by applying the relevant year of assessment’s income tax tables). 

Momentum will use the income definition that results in the highest net income when calculating loss of income or benefit reductions. 

Pre-disability net income will be increased by inflation from the date of the claim event to the date on which the loss of income is calculated. 

Benefit reductions ___________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The claim amount will be reduced if: 

- The benefit amount exceeds 100% of the insured life's pre-disability net income or 

- The policyholder is receiving a disability income from another insurance policy contract as a result of the insured life's disability 

###### **Benefit amount exceeds 100% of the pre-disability net income** 

The benefit amount will be reduced to ensure that it does not exceed 100% of the insured life's pre-disability net income. 

###### **Income from other income disability policy contracts** 

The claim amount will be reduced to ensure that the total of the claim amount payment and the income from the other policy contract does not exceed 100% of the insured life's pre-disability net income. 

###### **General** 

Pre-disability net income will be calculated as the insured life's net income (as defined under Definition of income) averaged over the period of 12 months immediately preceding the date of the disability. 

Any Functional Protector or Complete Functional Protector claim amount paid to the policyholder will not be considered in the benefit reduction calculations. 

Payments for lump sum disability benefits are specifically excluded from the benefit reduction calculation. 

###### **Removal of annual claim increases** 

If a claim arises as a direct or indirect result of any of the following conditions, the insured life will not qualify for any annual benefit claim increases for a period of up to five years following the first claim anniversary: 

Myriad technical guide – December2023 

Page 10 

- Any mental illness or psychiatric disorder which includes but is not limited to depression, dysthymia, post-traumatic stress disorder, and somatic symptom disorders 

- 

- 

- 

- 

   - Chronic pain syndrome (or any synonym thereof) 

   - Chronic fatigue syndrome (or any synonym thereof) 

   - Fibromyalgia 

   - Back or neck pain 

- Any orthopaedic condition which is based on pain, discomfort, loss of sensation, loss of range of motion, or any combination thereof 

- Any decline in cognitive functioning which does not meet the requirements for Activities of Daily Living (ADL's) stipulated under the functional impairment definitions; 

- Any injury, illness, complication, or treatment complications that arise as a result of any of the conditions listed above. 

The removal of annual claim increases will not apply if: 

- The insured life is receiving an income of less than 75% of his pre-disability net income (adjusted for inflation) 

- The insured life qualifies for a claim amount payment under one of the 100% functional impairment events. 

Waiting period _______________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The policyholder may choose one of the following waiting periods: 

- Seven days (only applicable to self-employed individuals) 

- 14 days 

- One month 

- Three months 

- Six months 

- 12 months 

- 24 months. 

Premiums are payable during the waiting period. 

If the insured life dies within the waiting period, a disability claim will not be paid. 

The first monthly claim amount payment will be made only after the insured life has been disabled for the waiting period that he chose. 

A proportionate payment will be made in respect of any part of a month that the insured life is rehabilitated before the payment date. 

Claim amount payments for functional impairment, critical illness or fracture, and hospitalisation will only be made after the waiting period has expired. 

###### **Seven-day waiting period** 

The premium due under this benefit will be waived after the insured life has been continuously disabled for more than 28 days. 

The claim amount payments will be made every seven days after the waiting period has expired. 

Claim payments will be made monthly in arrears after the insured life has been continuously disabled for 28 days. 

The insured life may qualify for a retrospective payment from day one of benefits after the seven-day waiting period in respect of disability. The first payment will be made seven days after the claim event occurred. 

Myriad technical guide – December2023

A proportionate payment will be made in respect of any part of a month that the insured life is rehabilitated before the payment date. 

To qualify for a retrospective payment, the insured life must be disabled for more than seven days and the insured life's disability must NOT be as a result of one of the following: 

- Cosmetic surgery 

- Influenza* 

- Upper or lower respiratory tract infections including SARS Cov-2/Covid19/Coronavirus* 

- Bronchitis* 

- Mental or psychiatric disorders* 

- Gastric influenza* 

- Gastritis* 

- Constipation* 

- Diarrhea* 

- Headaches* 

- Migraines* 

- Stress-related disorders 

- Chronic fatigue syndrome 

- 

   - Laryngitis, sinusitis, and pharyngitis 

- Abortions 

- Surgical procedures for infertility 

- Back injury 

- Fibromyalgia 

*These conditions will be covered if they require hospitalisation for longer than 24 hours. No retrospective payments will be made where the insured life was hospitalised for less than 24 hours. 

###### **14-day waiting period** 

After the insured life has been continuously disabled for 28 days, claim payments will be made monthly in arrears. 

The claim amount payments will be made every seven days after the waiting period has expired. 

A proportionate payment will be made in respect of any part of a month that the insured life is rehabilitated before the payment date. 

Momentum will waive the premiums due under this benefit, after the insured life has been continuously disabled for more than 28 days. Following rehabilitation, the insured life will retain their cover (at the premium rates applicable at that time). 

There are no retrospective payments under the 14-day waiting period. 

Off period ____________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

An "off period" of three months applies. 

This means that if the insured life is rehabilitated and claims again for the same cause within three months, the waiting period will be waived. 

###### **Seven-day and 14-day waiting period** 

The "off period" will only apply after the policyholder has been continuously disabled for more than 28 days. 

Income tax ___________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

Myriad technical guide – December2023 

Page 12 

If the benefit is owned by a natural person, the premiums are not tax-deductible. 

The claim amount payable in terms of this benefit will be tax-free. 

Annual Income Commutation Option _________________________________________________________________________ 

The policyholder has the option to convert up to one year’s monthly claim amount payments for this benefit and have it paid out as a lump sum if the insured life: 

- is totally unable to perform the normal duties of his own occupation or 

- satisfies the requirements for a 100% functional impairment claim event. 

The commutation feature may only be accessed after permanency has been established, but not before the second claim anniversary. 

Every year on the claim anniversary, from the second claim anniversary onwards, the policyholder will have the option to convert either 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, or 100% of one year’s monthly claim amount payments for this benefit to a lump sum payment. 

Momentum will notify the policyholder as soon as permanency has been established, of the option to convert. This feature must be exercised not later than two months before the subsequent claim anniversary. 

###### **Conversion of the full monthly payment** 

If the policyholder chooses to convert 100% of one year’s monthly claim amount payments, it will be paid in the form of a single lump-sum amount. 

This payment will be made on the next available payment date, following the subsequent claim anniversary. 

###### **Conversion of a portion of the monthly payment** 

If the policyholder chooses a lump sum conversion percentage that is less than 100%, the first payment following the subsequent claim anniversary will consist of one year’s monthly accumulated claim payments that are calculated using the chosen percentage. 

The monthly payments following the lump sum payment will also be calculated using the chosen conversion percentage. 

The first payment will be made on the next available payment date, following the subsequent claim anniversary. 

The current commutation factor is 11.5 for the lump sum calculations. 

Guaranteed insurability _____________________________________________________________________ 

Momentum will allow the policyholder to increase the benefit amount without any medical underwriting after the benefit anniversary if the insured life's income increases at a rate that exceeds the maximum voluntary benefit amount increase percentage. 

The total annual increase (annual voluntary benefit amount increase plus the guaranteed insurability increase) will be limited to twice the inflation rate used for increases by Momentum at that point, capped to 20%. 

This additional benefit amount increase may not be exercised if any of the following apply:

- the insured life is over the age of 55 

- voluntary benefit amount increases were not selected 

- the insured life is already disabled or was disabled during the 12 months preceding the date of the benefit amount increase 

- a health loading applies to the insured life 

Momentum must receive a written request to increase the benefit amount within one month after the benefit anniversary.

These benefits pay a monthly claim amount for the remainder of the insured's life if he is permanently impaired. 

The benefit amount being converted is subject to the maximum benefit limit for the chosen benefit at the time of the conversion. 

Medical underwriting will be required if: 

- any specific exclusion applies to this benefit, or

   - notification from the policyholder.

Claim event (before age 70) __________________________________________________________________________________ 

###### **Applicable before the benefit anniversary preceding the insured life’s 70**<sup>**th**</sup> **birthday** 

The insured life can qualify for a claim under either: 

- occupational disability or 

- impairment or illness. 

###### **Occupational disability** 

An occupational disability is a temporary or permanent disability caused by a bodily injury or an illness to such an extent that the insured life is continuously unable to perform the main duties of his own occupation on a total or partial basis. 

A claim amount will only be paid if the insured life is unable to perform at least 25% of the main duties of his own occupation. The claim amount payment will end once the insured life has recovered to the extent that he can perform more than 75% of the main duties of his own occupation. 

The claim amount will be calculated according to the loss of income or the severity of disability criteria. 

The insured life will not qualify for a claim under the occupational disability criteria if the insured life is not gainfully employed at the time of the claim event occurring. Any claim will be assessed against the impairment and illness criteria. 

###### **Impairment or illness** 

The insured life can qualify for a claim under: 

- functional impairment or 

- critical illness or 

- fracture and hospitalisation 

Myriad technical guide – December2023 

Page 18 

Momentum will pay for the event that provides the highest payout if the insured life qualifies for a claim amount payment under more than one of the impairment or illness claim events. 

If the insured life still qualifies for a functional impairment claim after a critical illness, fracture, or hospitalisation claim has been paid, Momentum will continue to pay the defined payment for the balance of the payment period. 

###### <u>Functional impairment</u> 

The claim events are not linked to the insured life's ability to perform occupational activities. 

The claim amount is based on the severity of a medical impairment that occurs after the starting date of the benefit as diagnosed by an appropriate specialist (registered with the Health Professions Council of South Africa (HPCSA) and resulting in the specified functional restrictions defined below. 

The insured life must undergo reasonable optimal treatment and their functional impairment will be determined after they have reached (reasonable) Maximal Medical Improvement (MMI). At this stage, a specialist approved by Momentum must declare the functional impairment total, permanent, and continuous for the foreseeable future. 

The insured life will not be required to undergo reasonable optimal treatment if a specialist, that Momentum has approved, has established that the functional impairment is permanent, and that further treatment will not lessen the severity of the condition. 

- Reasonable optimal treatment: This is the treatment that Momentum may reasonably expect the insured life to undergo according to the guidelines for the specific condition under the generally accepted medical practice at the claim stage. The insured life is expected to comply with his treatment routine. 

- Maximal Medical Improvement (MMI): A condition or state that is well stabilised and unlikely to change substantially in the next year with or without medical treatment. There may be some change over time, but further recovery is not expected. 

A panel of accredited medical specialists will determine how many Activities of Daily Living (ADL) the insured life can perform. 

A claim will be admitted only if the claim event is a permanent condition. 

Momentum will pay for the event that provides the highest payout if the insured life qualifies for a claim amount payment under more than one of the impairment events. 

Refer to Appendix 1 in the technical guide for the functional impairment claim events. 

###### <u>Critical illness</u> 

Momentum will pay a percentage of the benefit amount if the insured life meets the requirements of one of the defined critical illnesses claim events. 

A critical illness claim amount payment is only applicable to benefits with a sevenday, 14-day, one-month, or three-month waiting period. 

Momentum will not pay for a subsequent critical illness claim event while the insured life is receiving a critical illness claim amount payment. 

Myriad technical guide – December2023 

Page 19 

Refer to Appendix 2 and Appendix 3 in the technical guide for the critical illness claim events. 

<u>Fracture and hospitalisation</u> 

Momentum will pay a percentage of the benefit amount if the insured life meets the requirements of one of the defined fracture and hospitalisation claim events. 

A fracture and hospitalisation claim amount payment is only applicable to benefits with a seven-day, 14-day, or one-month waiting period. 

Momentum will pay for the event with the longest payment period if the insured life qualifies for a payment under more than one of the defined fracture or hospitalisation claim events. 

Momentum will not pay for a subsequent claim event for fracture or hospitalisation that occurs while the insured life is receiving a fracture and hospitalisation claim amount payment. 

Refer to Appendix 6 in the technical guide for fracture and hospitalisation claim events. 

Claim event (after age 70) ____________________________________________________________________________________ 

###### **Applicable after the benefit anniversary preceding the insured life’s 70th birthday** 

The same functional impairment claim events that apply before age 70 will continue to apply, but with the following exceptions: 

- The insured life will not be able to submit a claim for any of the 25% functional impairment events if that event occurs after the benefit anniversary immediately preceding the insured life’s 70th birthday. These events no longer apply. 

- All claim events in the following categories will not qualify for a claim payment after the stipulated benefit anniversary, even in instances where the insured life qualified for a claim before the benefit anniversary (preceding the insured life’s 70<sup>th</sup> birthday): 

   - 

      - Hearing 

   - Speech 

   - Facial disorders and/or disfigurement 

   - Cranial nerve VII (facial nerve) 

   - Peripheral venous disease 

- If the insured life met the requirements for a 25% functional impairment severity before the stipulated benefit anniversary (other than for hearing) and received a payout/series of payouts and still qualifies for a payout after undergoing a reassessment at the benefit anniversary preceding the insured life’s 70th birthday, Momentum will continue the payment until death. 

- Claim events for own occupation disability, fractures and hospitalization, and critical illness will no longer apply after the benefit anniversary preceding the insured life's 70th birthday. 

Claim amount (before age 70) ________________________________________________________________________________ 

###### **Applicable to claim events that occur before the benefit anniversary preceding the insured life’s 70th birthday** 

The monthly claim amount will be the higher of the claim amount calculated according to the following assessment criteria: 

- Loss of income 

- Severity of disability 

- Severity of impairment or illness 

Myriad technical guide – December2023 

Page 20 

###### **Loss of income** 

Momentum will pay the actual loss of income up to the maximum of the benefit amount. 

Actual loss of income is calculated as the difference between the insured life’s predisability net income and any income that the insured life earns during the disability. 

Net income refers to gross income less income tax payable on this income (determined by applying the relevant year of assessment’s income tax tables). 

###### **Severity of disability** 

The claim amount will be between 25% and 100% of the benefit amount, depending on the extent to which the insured life is unable to perform the main duties of his own occupation. 

The severity of disability assessment criteria, including the Partial Claim Upgrade, will only apply during the first year after the claim event. For professional occupations, these criteria will apply for the first two years after the claim event. 

Partial Claim Upgrade 

- If the full benefit amount has been paid for a continuous period of three months, the insured life will qualify for a Partial Claim Upgrade. 

- Momentum will continue to pay the full benefit amount after the three months, provided that the insured life is partially disabled 

- The full benefit amount will only be paid while the severity of disability assessment criteria applies (the first year after the claim event or the first two years after the claim event for professionals). 

###### **Severity of impairment or illness** 

Momentum will pay a percentage of the benefit amount for a specified payment period if the insured life meets any of the requirements for functional impairment, critical illness or fracture, and hospitalisation claim events. 

<mark>Refer to Appendix 6</mark> in the technical guide <mark>for payout levels and payment periods for severity of impairment and illness claim events.</mark> 

Claim events under the following categories will only qualify for a claim payment until the benefit anniversary immediately preceding the insured life’s 70th birthday: 

- Hearing 

- Speech 

- Facial disorders and/or disfigurement 

- Cranial nerve VII (facial nerve) 

- Peripheral venous disease 

###### **General** 

The claim amount is paid monthly in arrears. 

The daily claim amount will be calculated as 1/30 of the monthly benefit amount. 

A proportionate payment will be made in respect of any part of a month should the insured life be rehabilitated before the payment date. Following rehabilitation, the insured life will retain his cover. 

Any outstanding debt will be deducted from the claim amount. 

Myriad technical guide – December2023

###### **Premium waiver during a claim** 

The premium will be waived for this benefit while a claim is being paid. 

No proportionate premiums can be paid; therefore premiums are waived from the next financial month after the expiry of the waiting period. 

If the claim amount is less than the full benefit amount, the whole premium will still be waived. 

For a seven-day or 14-day waiting period, premiums will be waived after the insured life has been continuously disabled for more than 28 days. 

If Momentum collected premiums for a period not applicable for premium payment, it will be refunded to the policyholder as an advance on the policy. This (advance) amount will be deducted from the next premium payment. 

If this benefit is the only benefit on the policy, the policy fee will be waived while a claim is being paid.

Gross Professional For professionals that charge a fee for services, this Income (professionals equals the sum of the professional fees and the only) revenue less cost of sales from trading activities, after deducting business overheads expenses. 

**Net income** refers to gross income less income tax payable on this income (determined by applying the relevant year of assessment’s income tax tables).

Benefit reductions ___________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The claim amount will be reduced if: 

- The benefit amount exceeds 100% of the insured life's pre-disability net income or 

- The policyholder is receiving a disability income from another insurance policy contract as a result of the insured life's disability 

###### **Benefit amount exceeds 100% of the pre-disability net income** 

The benefit amount will be reduced to ensure that it does not exceed 100% of the insured life's pre-disability net income. 

###### **Income from other income disability policy contracts** 

The claim amount will be reduced to ensure that the total of the claim amount payment and the income from the other policy contract does not exceed 100% of the insured life's pre-disability net income. 

###### **General** 

Pre-disability net income will be calculated as the insured life's net income (as defined under Definition of income) averaged over the period of 12 months immediately preceding the date of the disability. 

Any Functional Protector or Complete Functional Protector claim amount paid to the policyholder will not be considered in the benefit reduction calculations. 

Payments for lump sum disability benefits are specifically excluded from the benefit reduction calculation. 

###### **Removal of annual claim increases** 

If a claim arises as a direct or indirect result of any of the following conditions, the insured life will not qualify for any annual benefit claim increases for a period of up to five years following the first claim anniversary: 

- Any mental illness or psychiatric disorder which includes but is not limited to depression, dysthymia, post-traumatic stress disorder, and somatic symptom disorders 

- Chronic pain syndrome (or any synonym thereof) 

- Chronic fatigue syndrome (or any synonym thereof) 

- Fibromyalgia 

- Back or neck pain

- Any decline in cognitive functioning which does not meet the requirements for Activities of Daily Living (ADL's) stipulated under our functional impairment definitions 

- Any injury, illness, complication, or treatment complications that arise as a result of any of the conditions listed above. 

The removal of annual claim increases will not apply if: 

- The insured life is receiving an income of less than 75% of his pre-disability net income (adjusted for inflation). 

- The insured life qualifies for a claim amount payment under one of the 100% functional impairment events.

Factors affecting monthly benefit payments __________________________________________________________________ 

The benefit payments end if: 

- the insured life no longer qualifies for a claim amount payment 

- the benefit ends 

- the insured life is not receiving or is refusing the medical treatment he/she could reasonably be expected to undergo according to current best practice medical protocols and which could substantially improve or remove the condition being claimed for. 

Ongoing assessment _________________________________________________________________________________________ 

Once a claim has been admitted and Momentum has started paying the monthly claim amount, the insured life's health will be assessed from time to time. If the insured life fails to undergo the reassessment within three months of Momentum's notification, the claim payments may be cancelled. 

These assessments will determine whether the insured life still qualifies for a claim and has been receiving such medical treatment as is appropriate for his condition. The benefit payments will end if the insured life no longer qualifies for a claim and the applicable premium must be paid. 

Momentum will cover the cost of the reassessment by a doctor chosen by Momentum. 

The ongoing assessment may be waived for the impairment or illness claim events. 

Following rehabilitation, the monthly benefit amount will start at the level of the last benefit payment and will increase on every benefit anniversary. 

The insured life will need to go for a re-assessment at the benefit anniversary preceding the insured life’s 70<sup>th</sup> birthday to establish whether they meet the specific post-retirement functional impairment requirements. 

Following the insured life’s rehabilitation any time before the benefit anniversary preceding the insured life’s 70th birthday, if voluntary income amount increases were chosen, the monthly benefit amount will start at the level of the last benefit payment and will increase on every benefit anniversary.

Benefit payment period _____________________________________________________________________ 

The policyholder may choose any of the following benefit payment periods: 

- Six months 

- 12 months 

- 24 months. 

The benefit payments will cease after the specified number of monthly payments have been made. 

If Momentum has paid for a specific cause for the benefit payment period, no further claims for that cause will be paid. If Momentum has paid for a specific cause for less than the benefit payment period and the insured life recovers, future claims resulting from the same cause will be paid for the balance of the benefit payment period. 

Claim event __________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The insured life can qualify for a claim under either: 

- occupational disability or 

- impairment or illness. 

###### **Occupational disability** 

An occupational disability is a temporary or permanent disability caused by a bodily injury or an illness to such an extent that the insured life is continuously unable to perform the main duties of his own occupation on a total or partial basis. 

A claim amount will only be paid if the insured life cannot perform at least 25% of the main duties of his own occupation. The claim amount payment will end once the insured life has recovered to the extent that he can perform more than 75% of the main duties of his own occupation. 

The claim amount will be calculated according to the loss of income or the severity of disability criteria. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 4 

The insured life will not qualify for a claim under the occupational disability criteria if they are not gainfully employed at the time of the claim event occurring. Such a claim will be assessed against the impairment and illness criteria. 

###### **Impairment or illness** 

The insured life can qualify for a claim under: 

- functional impairment or 

- critical illness or 

- fracture and hospitalisation 

Momentum will pay for the event that provides the highest payout if the insured life qualifies for a claim amount payment under more than one of the impairment or illness claim events. 

If the insured life still qualifies for a functional impairment claim after a critical illness, fracture or hospitalisation claim has been paid, we will continue to pay the defined payment for the balance of the payment period. 

###### <u>Functional impairment</u> 

The claim events are not linked to the insured life's ability to perform occupational activities. 

The claim amount is based on the severity of a medical impairment that occurs after the starting date of the benefit as diagnosed by an appropriate specialist (registered with the Health Professions Council of South Africa (HPCSA) and resulting in the specified functional restrictions defined below. 

The insured life will not be able to claim under functional impairment after the chosen expiry age. 

The insured life must undergo reasonable optimal treatment and their functional impairment will be determined after they have reached (reasonable) Maximal Medical Improvement (MMI). At this stage, a specialist approved by Momentum must declare the functional impairment total, permanent and continuous for the foreseeable future. 

The insured life will not be required to undergo reasonable optimal treatment if a specialist, that Momentum has approved, has established that the functional impairment is permanent, and that further treatment will not lessen the severity of the condition. 

- Reasonable optimal treatment: This is the treatment that Momentum may reasonably expect the insured life to undergo according to the guidelines for the specific condition under the generally accepted medical practice at claim stage. The insured life is expected to comply with his treatment routine. 

- Maximal Medical Improvement (MMI): A condition or state that is well stabilised and unlikely to change substantially in the next year with or without medical treatment. There may be some change over time, but further recovery is not expected. 

A panel of accredited medical specialists will determine how many Activities of Daily Living (ADL) the insured life can perform. 

A claim will be admitted only if the claim event is a permanent condition. 

Momentum will pay for the event that provides the highest payout if the insured life qualifies for a claim amount payment under more than one of the impairment events. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 5 

Refer to Appendix 1 in the technical guide for the functional impairment claim events. 

###### <u>Critical illness</u> 

Momentum will pay a percentage of the benefit amount if the insured life meets the requirements of one of the defined critical illnesses claim events. 

Momentum will not pay for a subsequent critical illness claim event that occurs while the insured life is receiving a critical illness claim amount payment. 

Refer to Appendix 2 and Appendix 3 in the technical guide for the critical illness claim events. 

###### <u>Fracture and hospitalisation</u> 

Momentum will pay a percentage of the benefit amount if the insured life meets the requirements of one of the defined fracture and hospitalisation claim events. 

Momentum will pay for the event with the longest payment period if the insured life qualifies for a payment under more than one of the defined fracture or hospitalisation claim events. 

Momentum will not pay for a subsequent claim event for fracture or hospitalisation that occurs while the insured life is receiving a fracture and hospitalisation claim amount payment. 

Refer to Appendix 6 in the technical guide for the fracture and hospitalisation claim events. 

Claim amount ________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

Momentum will use the following assessment criteria to determine the monthly claim amount and will use the criteria resulting in the highest claim amount: 

- Loss of income 

- Severity of disability 

- Severity of impairment or illness 

###### **Loss of income** 

Momentum will pay the actual loss of income up to the maximum of the benefit amount. 

Actual loss of income is calculated as the difference between the insured life’s net pre-disability income and any income the insured life earns during the period of disability. 

Net income refers to gross income less income tax payable on this income (determined by applying the relevant year of assessment’s income tax tables). 

###### **Severity of disability** 

The claim amount will be between 25% and 100% of the benefit amount, depending on the extent to which the insured life is unable to perform the main duties of his own occupation. 

The severity of disability assessment criteria, including the Partial Claim Upgrade, will only apply during the first year after the claim event. For professional occupations, these criteria will apply for the first two years after the claim event. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 6 

Partial Claim Upgrade 

- If the full benefit amount has been paid for a continuous period of three months, the insured life will qualify for a Partial Claim Upgrade. 

- Momentum will continue to pay the full benefit amount after the three months, provided that the insured life is partially disabled 

- The full benefit amount will only be paid while the severity of disability assessment criteria applies (the first year after the claim event or the first two years after the claim event for professionals). 

###### **Severity of impairment or illness** 

Momentum will pay a percentage of the benefit amount for a specified payment period if the insured life meets any of the requirements for functional impairment, critical illness or fracture and hospitalisation claim events. 

<mark>Refer to Appendix 6</mark> in the technical guide <mark>for payout levels and payment periods for severity of impairment and illness claim events.</mark> 

###### **General** 

The claim amount is paid monthly in arrears. 

The daily claim amount will be calculated as 1/30 of the monthly benefit amount. 

A proportionate payment will be made in respect of any part of a month should the insured life be rehabilitated before the payment date. Following rehabilitation, the insured life will retain his cover. 

The premium will be waived for this benefit while a claim is being paid. 

Any outstanding debt will be deducted from the claim amount. 

###### **Premium waiver during a claim** 

The premium will be waived for this benefit while a claim is being paid. 

No proportionate premiums can be paid; therefore, premiums are waived from the next financial month after the expiry of the waiting period. 

If the claim amount is less than the full benefit amount, the whole premium will still be waived. 

For a seven-day waiting period, premiums will be waived after the insured life has been continuously disabled for more than 28 days. 

If Momentum collected premiums for a period not applicable for premium payment, it will be refunded to the policyholder as an advance on the policy. This (advance) amount will be deducted from the next premium payment. 

If this benefit is the only benefit on the policy, the policy fee will be waived while a claim is being paid. 

Definition of income _________________________________________________________________________________________ 

Income is defined as one of the following: 

The total sum of all taxable income payable or Gross taxable income benefits receivable on account of the insured life's employment, or any services rendered by the insured life.

**Net income** refers to gross income less income tax payable on this income (determined by applying the relevant year of assessment’s income tax tables). 

Momentum will use the income definition that results in the highest net income when calculating loss of income or benefit reductions. 

Pre-disability net income will be increased by inflation from the date of the claim event to the date on which the loss of income is calculated. 

Benefit reductions _________________________________________________________________________ 

- <mark>Section 11(w)(ii) does not apply</mark> 

- The claim amount will be reduced if: • the benefit amount exceeds 100% of the insured life’s pre-disability **net** income or 

- the policyholder is receiving a disability income from another insurance policy contract as a result of the insured life’s disability. 

###### **Benefit amount exceeds 100% of the pre-disability net income** 

The benefit amount will be reduced to ensure that it does not exceed 100% of the insured life’s predisability **net** income. 

###### **Income from other income disability policy contracts** 

The claim amount will be reduced to ensure that the total of the claim amount payment and the income from the other policy contract does not exceed 100% of the insured life’s pre-disability **net** income. 

Pre-disability net income will be calculated as the insured life’s **net** income (as defined under Definition of income) averaged over the period of 12 months immediately preceding the date of disability. 

###### <mark>Section 11(w)(ii) applies</mark> 

The claim amount will be reduced if: 

- the benefit amount exceeds 100% of the insured life’s pre-disability income or 

- the policyholder is receiving a disability income from another insurance policy contract as a result of the insured life’s disability. 

###### **Benefit amount exceeds 100% of the pre-disability income** 

The benefit amount will be reduced to ensure that it does not exceed 100% of the insured life’s predisability income. 

###### **Income from other income disability policy contracts** 

The claim amount will be reduced to ensure that the total of the claim amount payment and the income from the other policy contract does not exceed 100% of the insured life’s pre-disability income. 

Pre-disability income will be calculated as the insured life’s income (as defined under Definition of income) averaged over the period of 12 months immediately preceding the date of disability. 

Any Functional Protector or Complete Functional Protector claim amount paid to the policyholder will not be considered in the benefit reduction calculations. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 8 

Payments for lump sum disability benefits are specifically excluded for the benefit reduction calculation. 

Successive claims __________________________________________________________________________ 

Total payments throughout the benefit term will be limited to the benefit payment period for claims due to the same bodily injury or related causes or illness. 

This limit will be waived for subsequent occupational disability claims if such related claims are separated by 24 months during which the insured life has fully resumed his nominated occupation. 

The limit will not be waived for subsequent impairment or illness claims. 

Waiting period _______________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The policyholder may choose one of the following waiting periods: 

- Seven days (only applicable to self-employed individuals) 

- 14 days 

- One month 

- Three months 

Premiums are payable during the waiting period. 

If the insured life dies within the waiting period, a disability claim will not be paid. 

The first monthly claim amount payment will be made only after the insured life has been disabled for the waiting period that he chose. 

A proportionate payment will be made in respect of any part of a month that the insured life is rehabilitated before the payment date. 

Claim amount payments for functional impairment, critical illness or fracture and hospitalisation will only be made after the waiting period has expired. 

###### **Seven-day waiting period** 

The premium due under this benefit will be waived after the insured life has been continuously disabled for more than 28 days. 

The claim amount payments will be made every seven days after the waiting period has expired. 

Claim payments will be made monthly in arrears after the insured life has been continuously disabled for 28 days. 

The insured life may qualify for a retrospective payment from day one of benefits after the seven-day waiting period in respect of disability. The first payment will be made seven days after the claim event occurred. 

A proportionate payment will be made in respect of any part of a month that the insured life is rehabilitated before the payment date. 

To qualify for a retrospective payment, the insured life must be disabled for more than seven days and the insured life's disability must NOT be as a result of one of the following: 

- Cosmetic surgery 

- Influenza* 

- Upper or lower respiratory tract infections including SARS Cov-2/Covid-19/ Coronavirus* 

- Bronchitis* 

- Mental or psychiatric disorders* 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 9 

- Gastric influenza* 

- Gastritis* 

- Constipation* 

- Diarrhoea* 

- Headaches* 

- Migraines* 

- Stress-related disorders 

- Chronic fatigue syndrome 

- Laryngitis, sinusitis and pharyngitis 

- Abortions 

- Surgical procedures for infertility 

- Back injury 

- Fibromyalgia 

*These conditions will be covered if they require hospitalisation for longer than 24 hours. No retrospective payments will be made where the insured life was hospitalised for less than 24 hours. 

###### **14-day waiting period** 

After the insured life has been continuously disabled for 28 days, claim payments will be made monthly in arrears. 

The claim amount payments will be made every seven days after the waiting period has expired. 

A proportionate payment will be made in respect of any part of a month that the insured life is rehabilitated before the payment date. 

Momentum will waive the premiums due under this benefit, after the insured life has been continuously disabled for more than 28 days. Following rehabilitation, the insured life will retain their cover (at the premium rates applicable at that time). 

There are no retrospective payments under the 14-day waiting period. 

Off period ____________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

An "off period" of three months applies. 

This means that if the insured life is rehabilitated and claims again for the same cause within the three months, the waiting period will be waived. 

###### **Seven-day and 14-day waiting period** 

The "off period" will only apply after the policyholder has been continuously disabled for at least 28 days. 

Income tax ___________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

If the benefit is owned by a natural person, the premiums are not tax-deductible. 

The claim amount payable in terms of this benefit will be tax-free. 

Guaranteed insurability ______________________________________________________________________________________ 

Momentum will allow policyholder to increase the benefit amount without any medical underwriting after the benefit anniversary if the insured life's income increases at a rate that exceeds the maximum voluntary benefit amount increase percentage. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 10 

The total annual increase (annual voluntary benefit amount increase plus the guaranteed insurability increase) will be limited to twice the inflation rate used for increases by Momentum at that point, capped to 20%. 

This additional benefit amount increase may not be exercised if any of the following apply: 

- the insured life is over the age of 55 

- voluntary benefit amount increases were not selected 

- The insured life is already disabled or was disabled during the 12 months preceding the date of the benefit amount increase 

- a health loading applies to the insured life 

Momentum must receive a written request to increase the benefit amount within one month after the benefit anniversary. 

End of benefit ________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

This benefit ends on the earliest of: 

- The death of the insured life. 

- The end of the benefit term. 

- The cancellation of the policy or benefit as a result of: 

   - any event covered in the policy contract 

   - notification from the policyholder. 

Claim requirements __________________________________________________________________________________________ 

Refer to the Claim requirements section of this technical guide for information on the documents required to assess a claim under this benefit. 

Factors affecting monthly benefit payments __________________________________________________________________ 

The benefit payments end if: 

- the insured life is no longer qualifies for a claim amount payment 

- the benefit ends 

- the aggregate benefit payment period for a single cause ends 

- The benefit payment period ends 

- the insured life is not receiving or is refusing the medical treatment they could reasonably be expected to undergo according to current best practice medical protocols and which could substantially improve or remove the condition being claimed for. 

Ongoing assessments ________________________________________________________________________________________ 

Once a claim has been admitted and Momentum has started paying the monthly claim amount, the insured life's health will be assessed from time to time. If the insured life fails to undergo the reassessment within three months of Momentum's notification, the claim payments may be cancelled. 

These assessments will determine whether the insured life still qualifies for a claim and has been receiving such medical treatment as is appropriate for his condition. The benefit payments will end if the insured life no longer qualifies for a claim and the applicable premium must be paid. 

Momentum will cover the cost of the reassessment by a doctor chosen by Momentum. 

The ongoing assessment may be waived for the impairment or illness claim events. 

Following rehabilitation, the monthly benefit amount will start at the level of the last benefit payment and will increase on every benefit anniversary.
