#### Business Protector (Self Employed) 

- Description _______________________________________________________________________________ Momentum will pay a monthly claim amount if: • the insured life is temporarily or permanently disabled as a result of a bodily injury or illness to such an extent that they are continuously unable to perform the main duties of their own occupation on a total or partial basis OR 

- • the insured life meets the requirements of one of the defined impairment or illness claim events. 

- Special conditions ____________________________________________________________________________________________ The claim amount is paid monthly in arrears. This benefit is only available to self-employed individuals. The insured life's disability must cause a significantly reduced income for the business The insured life must be involved in the business on a full-time basis. The insured life's participation in the day-to-day running of the business is essential. The insured life is a single business owner. In other words, the insured life can be any one of the following: 

   - an individual who works entirely for himself and has no partners (sole proprietor) 

   - the only owner of a private company 

   - the only member of a Closed Corporation (CC). 

The owner and the business are the same legal entity. A Business Protector (Self Employed) and a Business Overheads Protector on the same insured life may not be added together on one policy 

The Business Protector (Self Employed) may only be combined with a Complete Income Protector with a 12-month or 24-month waiting period, depending on the benefit payment period chosen at the start of the policy. 

The policyholder may add the Business Protector (Self Employed) to a policy together with any stand-alone or ancillary benefits. Benefit payment period ______________________________________________________________________________________ 

The policyholder may choose any of the following benefit payment periods: 

- 12 months 

- 24 months. 

The benefit payments will cease after the specified number of monthly payments have been made. 

If Momentum has paid for a specific cause for the benefit payment period, no further claims for that cause will be paid. If Momentum has paid for a specific cause for less than the benefit payment period and the insured life recovers, future claims resulting from the same cause will be paid for the balance of the benefit payment period. 

Claim event __________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The insured life can qualify for a claim under either: 

- occupational disability or 

- impairment or illness. 

###### **Occupational disability** 

An occupational disability is a temporary or permanent disability caused by a bodily injury or an illness to such an extent that the insured life is continuously unable to perform the main duties of his own occupation on a total or partial basis. 

A claim amount will only be paid if the insured life is unable to perform at least 25% of the main duties of his own occupation. The claim amount payment will end once the insured life has recovered to the extent that he can perform more than 75% of the main duties of his own occupation. 

The claim amount will be calculated according to the loss of income or the severity of disability criteria. 

The insured life will not qualify for a claim under the occupational disability criteria if the insured life is not gainfully employed at the time of the claim event occurring. Such a claim will be assessed against the impairment and illness criteria. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 4 

###### **Impairment or illness** 

The insured life can qualify for a claim under: 

- functional impairment or 

- critical illness or 

- fracture and hospitalisation 

Momentum will pay for the event that provides the highest payout if the insured life qualifies for a claim amount payment under more than one of the impairment or illness claim events. 

If the insured life still qualifies for a functional impairment claim after a critical illness, fracture or hospitalisation claim has been paid, we will continue to pay the defined payment for the balance of the payment period. 

###### <u>Functional impairment</u> 

The claim events are not linked to the insured life's ability to perform occupational activities. 

The claim amount is based on the severity of a medical impairment that occurs after the starting date of the benefit as diagnosed by an appropriate specialist (registered with the Health Professions Council of South Africa (HPCSA) and resulting in the specified functional restrictions defined below. 

The insured life will not be able to claim under functional impairment after the chosen expiry age. 

The insured life must undergo reasonable optimal treatment and their functional impairment will be determined after they have reached (reasonable) Maximal Medical Improvement (MMI). At this stage, a specialist approved by Momentum must declare the functional impairment total, permanent and continuous for the foreseeable future. The insured life will not be required to undergo reasonable optimal treatment if a specialist, that Momentum has approved, has established that the functional impairment is permanent, and that further treatment will not lessen the severity of the condition. 

- Reasonable optimal treatment: This is the treatment that Momentum may reasonably expect the insured life to undergo according to the guidelines for the specific condition under the generally accepted medical practice at claim stage. The insured life is expected to comply with their treatment routine. 

- Maximal Medical Improvement (MMI): A condition or state that is well stabilised and unlikely to change substantially in the next year with or without medical treatment. There may be some change over time, but further recovery is not expected. 

A panel of accredited medical specialists will determine how many Activities of Daily Living (ADL) the insured life can perform. 

A claim will be admitted only if the claim event is a permanent condition. 

Momentum will pay for the event that provides the highest payout if the insured life qualifies for a claim amount payment under more than one of the impairment events. 

Refer to <u>Appendix 1 in the technical guide for functional impairment claim events</u> 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 5 

###### <u>Critical illness</u> 

Momentum will pay a percentage of the benefit amount if the insured life meets the requirements of one of the defined critical illnesses claim events. 

Momentum will not pay for a subsequent critical illness claim event while the insured life is receiving a critical illness claim amount payment. 

Refer to Appendix 2 and Appendix 3 in the technical guide for critical illness claim events 

###### <u>Fracture and hospitalisation</u> 

Momentum will pay a percentage of the benefit amount if the insured life meets the requirements of one of the defined fracture and hospitalisation claim events. 

Momentum will pay for the event with the longest payment period if the insured life qualifies for a payment under more than one of the defined fracture or hospitalisation claim events. 

Momentum will not pay for a subsequent claim event for fracture or hospitalisation that occurs while the insured life is receiving a fracture and hospitalisation claim amount payment. 

Refer to Appendix 6 in the technical guide for fracture and hospitalisation claim events. 

Claim amount ________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

Momentum will use the following assessment criteria to determine the monthly claim amount and will use the criteria resulting in the highest claim amount: 

- Loss of income 

- Severity of disability 

- Severity of impairment or illness 

###### **Loss of income** 

Momentum will pay the actual loss of income up to the maximum of the benefit amount. 

The actual loss of income is calculated as the difference between the insured life’s pre-disability income and any income that the insured life earns during the period of disability. 

###### **Severity of disability** 

The claim amount will be between 25% and 100% of the benefit amount, depending on the extent to which the insured life is unable to perform the main duties of his own occupation. 

The severity of disability assessment criteria, including the Partial claim Upgrade, will only apply during the first year after the claim event. For professional occupations, these criteria will apply for the first two years after the claim event. 

Partial Claim Upgrade 

- If the full benefit amount has been paid for a continuous period of three months, the insured life will qualify for a Partial Claim Upgrade. 

- Momentum will continue to pay the full benefit amount after the three months, provided that the insured life is partially disabled. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 6 

- The full benefit amount will only be paid while the severity of disability assessment criteria applies. 

###### **Severity of impairment or illness** 

Momentum will pay a percentage of the benefit amount for a specified payment period if the insured life meets any of the requirements for functional impairment, critical illness or fracture and hospitalisation claim events. 

<mark>Refer to Appendix 6</mark> in the technical guide <mark>for payout levels and payment periods for severity of impairment and illness claim events.</mark> 

###### **General** 

The claim amount is paid monthly in arrears. 

The daily claim amount will be calculated as 1/30 of the monthly benefit amount. 

A proportionate payment will be made in respect of any part of a month should the insured life be rehabilitated before the payment date. Following rehabilitation, the insured life will retain his cover. 

Any outstanding debt will be deducted from the claim amount. 

###### **Premium waiver during a claim** 

The premium will be waived for this benefit while a claim is being paid. 

No proportionate premiums can be paid; therefore, premiums are waived from the next financial month after the expiry of the waiting period. 

If the claim amount is less than the full benefit amount, the whole premium will still be waived. 

For a seven-day waiting period, premiums will be waived after the insured life has been continuously disabled for more than 28 days. 

If Momentum collected premiums for a period not applicable for premium payment, it will be refunded to the policyholder as an advance on the policy. This (advance) amount will be deducted from the next premium payment. 

If this benefit is the only benefit on the policy, the policy fee will be waived while a claim is being paid. 

Definition of income _________________________________________________________________________________________ 

Income is defined as the gross profit of the business: 

|Gross profit|The gross profit of the business is defined as Revenue<br>(also known as Turnover)less the Cost of sales.|
|---|---|
|Turnover|Turnover is defined as the total amount generated by the<br>business from its normal business activities.|
|Cost of sales|Cost of Sales is defined as the cost to a business to buy or<br>make the product that is sold to the consumer. Cost of<br>Sales would not apply to a business that only generates<br>its business byrenderinga service.|



Benefit reductions ___________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The claim amount will be reduced if the benefit amount exceeds the pre-disability income earned by the insured life. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 7 

###### **Benefit amount exceeds the pre-disability income** 

The benefit amount will be reduced to ensure that it does not exceed the insured life’s pre-disability income (increased with inflation). 

If the policy is owned by a sole proprietor, a partner in a partnership, a company or a Closed Corporation (CC), the pre-disability income is calculated as: 

|Section 11(w)(ii) of<br>|the Income Tax Act<br>|
|---|---|
|Does**NOT**apply|Applies|
|85% of the gross profit of the business,<br>averaged over the period of 12 months|100% of the gross profit of the business,<br>averaged over the period of 12 months|
|immediately preceding the date of the<br>disability.|immediately preceding the date of the<br>disability.|



Any claim amount paid to the policyholder in respect of the Functional Protector or Complete Functional Protector will not be considered in the benefit reduction calculations. 

Payments for lump sum disability benefits are specifically excluded from the benefit reduction calculation. 

Successive claims_____________________________________________________________________________________________ 

Total payments throughout the benefit term will be limited to the benefit payment period for claims due to the same bodily injury or related causes or illness. 

This limit will be waived for subsequent occupational disability claims if such related claims are separated by 24 months during which the insured life has fully resumed his nominated occupation. 

The limit will not be waived for subsequent impairment or illness claims. 

Waiting period _______________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The policyholder may choose one of the following waiting periods: 

- Seven days 

- One-month 

Premiums are payable during the waiting period. 

A claim will not be paid if the insured life dies within the waiting period. 

The first monthly claim amount payment will be made only after the insured life has been disabled for the waiting period he chose. 

A proportionate payment will be made in respect of any part of a month that the insured life is rehabilitated before the payment date. 

The insured life will receive a retrospective payment at the end of the one month waiting period. 

Claim amount payments for functional impairment, critical illness or fracture and hospitalisation will only be made after the waiting period has expired. 

###### **Seven-day waiting period** 

The premium due under this benefit will be waived after the insured life has been continuously disabled for more than 28 days. 

The claim amount payments will be made every seven days after the waiting period has expired. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 8 

Claim payments will be made monthly in arrears after the insured life has been continuously disabled for 28 days. 

The insured life will qualify for a retrospective payment from day one of benefits after the seven-day waiting period in respect of disability. The first payment will be made seven days after the claim event occurred. 

A proportionate payment will be made in respect of any part of a month that the insured life is rehabilitated before the payment date. 

To qualify for a retrospective payment the insured life must be disabled for more than seven days and the insured life's disability must NOT be as a result of one of the following: 

- Cosmetic surgery 

- • Influenza* • Upper or lower respiratory tract infections including SARS Cov-2/Covid-19/ Coronavirus* 

- Bronchitis* 

- • Mental or psychiatric disorders* 

- Gastric influenza* 

- Gastritis* 

- • Constipation* 

- • Diarrhoea* • Headaches* • Migraines* 

- • Stress-related disorders • Chronic fatigue syndrome 

- • Laryngitis, sinusitis and pharyngitis 

- Abortions 

- • Surgical procedures for infertility 

- Back injury 

- Fibromyalgia 

*These conditions will be covered if they are chronic and require hospitalisation for longer than 24 hours. No retrospective payments will be made where the insured life was hospitalised for less than 24 hours. 

Off period ____________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

An "off period" of three months applies. 

This means that if the insured life is rehabilitated and claims again for the same cause within three months, the waiting period will be waived. 

###### **Seven-day waiting period** 

The "off period" will only apply after the policyholder has been continuously disabled for more than 28 days. 

Commuted value _____________________________________________________________________________________________ 

In the event of the insured life becoming totally and permanently disabled or if the insured life qualifies for a 100% functional impairment claim, Momentum will commute the remaining monthly payments and pay this as a lump sum. 

The commuted value will be calculated as the sum of the remaining payments, taking post-claim benefit increases into account. 

The commuted value will only be available after Momentum has made three monthly payments under this benefit.

Benefit payment period ______________________________________________________________________________________ 

The policyholder may choose any of the following benefit payment periods: 

- 12 months 

- 24 months. 

The benefit payments will cease after the specified number of monthly payments have been made. 

If Momentum has paid for a specific cause for the benefit payment period, no further claims for that cause will be paid. If Momentum has paid for a specific cause for less than the benefit payment period and the insured life recovers, future claims resulting from the same cause will be paid for the balance of the benefit payment period. 

Claim event __________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The insured life can qualify for a claim under either: 

- occupational disability or 

- impairment or illness. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 4 

###### **Occupational disability** 

An occupational disability is a temporary or permanent disability caused by a bodily injury or an illness to such an extent that the insured life is continuously unable to perform the main duties of his own occupation on a total or partial basis. 

A claim amount will only be paid if the insured life is unable to perform at least 25% of the main duties of his own occupation. The claim amount payment will end once the insured life has recovered to the extent that he can perform more than 75% of the main duties of his own occupation. 

The claim amount will be calculated according to the loss of income or the severity of disability criteria. 

The insured life will not qualify for a claim under the occupational disability criteria if the insured life is not gainfully employed at the time of the claim event occurring. Such a claim will be assessed against the impairment and illness criteria. 

###### **Impairment or illness** 

The insured life can qualify for a claim under: 

- functional impairment or 

- critical illness or 

- fracture and hospitalisation 

Momentum will pay for the event that provides the highest payout if the insured life qualifies for a claim amount payment under more than one of the impairment or illness claim events. 

If the insured life still qualifies for a functional impairment claim after a critical illness, fracture or hospitalisation claim has been paid; we will continue to pay the defined payment for the balance of the payment period. 

###### <u>Functional impairment</u> 

The claim events are not linked to the insured life's ability to perform occupational activities. 

The claim amount is based on the severity of a medical impairment that occurs after the starting date of the benefit as diagnosed by an appropriate specialist (registered with the Health Professions Council of South Africa (HPCSA) and resulting in the specified functional restrictions defined below. 

The insured life will not be able to claim under functional impairment after the chosen expiry age. 

The insured life must undergo reasonable optimal treatment and their functional impairment will be determined after they have reached (reasonable) Maximal Medical Improvement (MMI). At this stage, a specialist approved by Momentum must declare the functional impairment total, permanent and continuous for the foreseeable future. The insured life will not be required to undergo reasonable optimal treatment if a specialist that Momentum has approved has established that the functional impairment is permanent, and that further treatment will not lessen the severity of the condition. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 5 

- Reasonable optimal treatment: This is the treatment that Momentum may reasonably expect the insured life to undergo according to the guidelines for the specific condition under the generally accepted medical practice at claim stage. The insured life is expected to comply with his treatment routine. 

- Maximal Medical Improvement (MMI): A condition or state that is well stabilised and unlikely to change substantially in the next year with or without medical treatment. There may be some change over time, but further recovery is not expected. 

A panel of accredited medical specialists will determine how many Activities of Daily Living (ADL) the insured life can perform. 

A claim will be admitted only if the claim event is a permanent condition. 

Momentum will pay for the event that provides the highest payout if the insured life qualifies for a claim amount payment under more than one of the impairment events. 

Refer to Appendix 1 in the technical guide for functional impairment claim events 

###### <u>Critical illness</u> 

Momentum will pay a percentage of the benefit amount if the insured life meets the requirements of one of the defined critical illnesses claim events. 

Momentum will not pay for a subsequent critical illness claim event while the insured life is receiving a critical illness claim amount payment. 

Refer to Appendix 2 and Appendix 3 in the technical guide for critical illness claim events 

###### <u>Fracture and hospitalisation</u> 

Momentum will pay a percentage of the benefit amount if the insured life meets the requirements of one of the defined fracture and hospitalisation claim events. 

Momentum will pay for the event with the longest payment period if the insured life qualifies for a payment under more than one of the defined fracture or hospitalisation claim events. 

Momentum will not pay for a subsequent claim event for fracture or hospitalisation that occurs while the insured life is receiving a fracture and hospitalisation claim amount payment. 

Refer to Appendix 6 in the technical guide for fracture and hospitalisation claim events. 

Claim amount ________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

Momentum will use the following assessment criteria to determine the monthly claim amount and will use the criteria resulting in the highest claim amount: 

- Loss of income 

- Severity of disability 

- Severity of impairment or illness 

###### **Loss of income** 

Momentum will pay the actual loss of income up to the maximum of the benefit amount. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 6 

The actual loss of income is calculated as the difference between the insured life’s net pre-disability income and any net income that the insured life earns during the period of disability. 

###### **Severity of disability** 

The claim amount will be between 25% and 100% of the benefit amount, depending on the extent to which the insured life is unable to perform the main duties of his own occupation. 

The severity of disability assessment criteria, including the Partial Claim Upgrade, will only apply during the first year after the claim event. For professional occupations, these criteria will apply for the first two years after the claim event. 

Partial Claim Upgrade 

- If the full benefit amount has been paid for a continuous period of three months, the insured life will qualify for a Partial Claim Upgrade. 

- Momentum will continue to pay the full benefit amount after the three months, provided that the insured life is partially disabled. 

- The full benefit amount will only be paid while the severity of disability assessment criteria applies. 

###### **Severity of impairment or illness** 

Momentum will pay a percentage of the benefit amount for a specified payment period if the insured life meets any of the requirements for functional impairment, critical illness or fracture and hospitalisation claim events. 

<mark>Refer to Appendix 6</mark> in the technical guide in the technical guide <mark>for payout levels and payment periods for severity of impairment and illness claim events.</mark> 

###### **General** 

The claim amount is paid monthly in arrears. 

The daily claim amount will be calculated as 1/30 of the monthly benefit amount. 

A proportionate payment will be made in respect of any part of a month should the insured life be rehabilitated before the payment date. Following rehabilitation, the insured life will retain his cover. 

The premium will be waived for this benefit while a claim is being paid. 

Any outstanding debt will be deducted from the claim amount. 

###### **Premium waiver during a claim** 

The premium will be waived for this benefit while a claim is being paid. 

No proportionate premiums can be paid; therefore, premiums are waived from the next financial month after the expiry of the waiting period. 

If the claim amount is less than the full benefit amount, the whole premium will still be waived. 

For a seven-day waiting period, premiums will be waived after the insured life has been continuously disabled for more than 28 days. 

If Momentum collected premiums for a period not applicable for premium payment, it will be refunded to the policyholder as an advance on the policy. This (advance) amount will be deducted from the next premium payment. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 7 

If this benefit is the only benefit on the policy, the policy fee will be waived while a claim is being paid. 

Definition of income _________________________________________________________________________________________ 

Income is defined as the sum of the professional fees and the net income from trading activities. 

Pre-disability net income will be increased by inflation from the date of the claim event to the date on which the loss of income is calculated. 

Benefit reductions ___________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The claim amount will be reduced if the benefit amount exceeds the pre-disability income earned by the insured life. 

###### **Benefit amount exceeds the pre-disability income** 

The benefit amount will be reduced to ensure that it does not exceed the insured life’s pre-disability income (increased with inflation). 

If the policy is owned by a sole proprietor, a partner in a partnership, a company or a Closed Corporation, the pre-disability income is calculated as: 

|Section 11(w)(ii) of the<br>Does**NOT**apply|Income Tax Act<br>Applies|
|---|---|
|85% of the insured life’s income averaged<br>over the period of 12 months immediately<br>preceding the date of the disability.|The insured life’s income averaged<br>over the period of 12 months<br>immediately preceding the date of<br>the disability.|



Any claim amount paid to the policyholder in respect of the Functional Protector or Complete Functional Protector will not be considered in the benefit reduction calculations. 

Payments for lump sum disability benefits are specifically excluded from the benefit reduction calculation. 

Successive claims_____________________________________________________________________________________________ 

Total payments throughout the benefit term will be limited to the benefit payment period for claims due to the same bodily injury or related causes or illness. 

This limit will be waived for subsequent occupational disability claims if such related claims are separated by 24 months during which the insured life has fully resumed his nominated occupation. 

The limit will not be waived for subsequent impairment or illness claims. 

Waiting period _______________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The policyholder may choose one of the following waiting periods: 

- Seven days 

- One month 

Premiums are payable during the waiting period. 

If the insured life dies within the waiting period, a disability claim will not be paid. 

The first monthly claim amount payment will be made only after the insured life has been disabled for the waiting period he chose. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 8 

A proportionate payment will be made in respect of any part of a month that the insured life is rehabilitated before the payment date. 

The insured life will receive a retrospective payment at the end of the one month 

waiting period. 

Claim amount payments for functional impairment, critical illness or fracture and hospitalisation will only be made after the waiting period has expired. 

###### **Seven-day waiting period** 

The premium due under this benefit will be waived, after the insured life has been continuously disabled for more than 28 days. 

The claim amount payments will be made every seven days after the waiting period has expired. 

Claim payments will be made monthly in arrears after the insured life has been continuously disabled for 28 days. 

The insured life will qualify for a retrospective payment from day one of benefits after the seven-day waiting period in respect of disability. The first payment will be made seven days after the claim event occurred. 

A proportionate payment will be made in respect of any part of a month that the insured life is rehabilitated before the payment date. 

To qualify for a retrospective payment, the insured life must be disabled for more than seven days and the insured life's disability must NOT be as a result of one of the following: 

- Cosmetic surgery 

- Influenza* 

- Upper or lower respiratory tract infections including SARS Cov-2/Covid-19/Coronavirus* 

- • Bronchitis* 

- Mental or psychiatric disorders* 

- Gastric influenza* 

- Gastritis* 

- Constipation* 

- Diarrhoea* 

- Headaches* 

- Migraines* 

- Stress-related disorders 

- Chronic fatigue syndrome 

- Laryngitis, sinusitis and pharyngitis 

- Abortions 

- Surgical procedures for infertility 

- Back injury 

- Fibromyalgia 

*These conditions will be covered if they are chronic and require hospitalisation for longer than 24 hours. No retrospective payments will be made where the insured life was hospitalised for less than 24 hours. 

Off period ____________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

An "off period" of three months applies. 

This means that if the insured life is rehabilitated and claims again for the same cause within three months, the waiting period will be waived. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 9 

###### **Seven-day waiting period** 

The "off period" will only apply after the policyholder has been continuously disabled for more than 28 days. 

Commuted value _____________________________________________________________________________________________ 

In the event of the insured life becoming totally and permanently disabled or if the insured life qualifies for a 100% functional impairment claim, Momentum will commute the remaining monthly payments and pay this as a lump sum. 

The commuted value will be calculated as the sum of the remaining payments, taking post-claim benefit increases into account. 

The commuted value will only be available after Momentum has made three monthly payments under this benefit. 

Guaranteed insurability ______________________________________________________________________________________ 

Momentum will allow the policyholder to increase the benefit amount without any medical underwriting after the benefit anniversary if the insured life's business overhead increases at a rate that exceeds the maximum voluntary benefit amount increase percentage. 

The total annual increase (annual voluntary benefit amount increase plus the guaranteed insurability increase) will be limited to twice the inflation rate used for increases by Momentum at that point, capped to 20%. 

This additional benefit amount increase may not be exercised if any of the following apply: 

- the insured life is over the age of 55 

- voluntary benefit amount increases were not selected 

- the insured life is already disabled or was disabled during the 12 months preceding the date of the benefit amount increase 

- a health loading applies to the insured life 

Momentum must receive a written request to increase the benefit amount within one month after the benefit anniversary. 

End of benefit ________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

This benefit ends on the earliest of: 

- The death of the insured life. 

- The end of the benefit term (if applicable). 

- The business ceases to exist. 

- The cancellation of the policy or benefit as a result of: 

   - any event covered in the policy contract 

   - notification from the policyholder. 

Claim requirements __________________________________________________________________________________________ 

Refer to the Claim requirements section of this technical guide for information on the documents required to assess a claim under this benefit. 

Factors affecting monthly benefit payments __________________________________________________________________ 

The benefit payments end if: 

- the insured life no longer qualifies for a claim amount payment 

- the benefit ends

- the insured life is not receiving or is refusing the medical treatment he/she could reasonably be expected to undergo according to current best practice medical protocols and which could substantially improve or remove the condition being claimed for. 

- the aggregate benefit payment period for a single cause ends. 

- The benefit payment period ends. 

Ongoing assessments ________________________________________________________________________________________ 

Once a claim has been admitted and Momentum has started paying the monthly claim amount, the insured life's health will be assessed from time to time. If the insured life fails to undergo the reassessment within three months of Momentum's notification, the claim payments may be cancelled. 

These assessments will determine whether the insured life still qualifies for a claim and has been receiving such medical treatment as is appropriate for his condition. The benefit payments will end if the insured life no longer qualifies for a claim and the applicable premium must be paid. 

Momentum will cover the cost of the reassessment by a doctor chosen by Momentum. 

The ongoing assessment may be waived for the impairment or illness claim events. 

Following rehabilitation, the monthly benefit amount will start at the level of the last benefit payment and will increase on every benefit anniversary.

#### Business Overheads Protector 

Description __________________________________________________________________________________ 

Momentum will pay a monthly claim amount if: 

- the insured life is temporarily or permanently disabled as a result of a bodily injury or illness to such an extent that they are continuously unable to perform the main duties of their own occupation on a total or partial basis OR 

- the insured life meets the requirements of one of the defined impairment or illness claim events. 

Special conditions _____________________________________________________________________________ 

If a seven-day waiting period is selected the claim amount payments during the first month after the claim event, is paid in arrears. After the first month, claim payments are made in advance. 

Annual premiums are not allowed on the Business Overheads Protector. 

The insured life's disability must cause a significantly reduced income for the business. 

The insured life must be involved in the business on a full-time basis 

These benefits may not be added on one policy if the insured life is the same: 

- Business Overheads Protector and Business Protector (Self Employed) 

- Business Overheads Protector and Business Protector (Professional) 

The insured life can be any one of the following: 

- An individual who works entirely for himself and has no partners 

- A partner in a partnership with a maximum of four partners and who has at least a 25% share in the partnership and whose participation in the day-to-day running of the business is essential 

- An owner or an employee of a business with no more than four owners and no more than 10 employees (including the owners). Employees include all persons employed by the business. 

If the individual operates the business from a home address, evidence is required that he has converted a portion of the premises to business premises. 

If sales goods generate more than 20% of business turnover, the primary test is whether the insured life must be present on the premises on a full-time basis to provide a service that the employees cannot provide. 

In the case of professionals in private practice: 

- the insured life must be a highly skilled professional 

- the other employees must not be able to provide the service 

- the profession must be recognised by South African law 

- the insured life's participation in the day-to-day running of the business must be essential. 

The policy can only be owned by sole proprietors, a partner in a partnership, a company or a Closed Corporation (CC). 

The owner and the business must be the same legal entity.

The total annual increase (annual voluntary benefit amount increase plus the guaranteed insurability increase) will be limited to twice the inflation rate used for increases by Momentum at that point, capped to 20%. 

This additional benefit amount increase may not be exercised if any of the following apply: 

- the insured life is over the age of 55 

- voluntary benefit amount increases were not selected 

- The insured life is already disabled or was disabled during the 12 months preceding the date of the benefit amount increase 

- a health loading applies to the insured life 

Momentum must receive a written request to increase the benefit amount within one month after the benefit anniversary.

Claim event ______________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The insured life can qualify for a claim under either: 

- occupational disability or 

- impairment or illness. 

###### **Occupational disability** 

An occupational disability is a temporary or permanent disability caused by a bodily injury or an illness to such an extent that the insured life is continuously unable to perform the main duties of his own occupation on a total or partial basis. 

A claim amount will only be paid if the insured life is unable to perform at least 25% of the main duties of his own occupation. The claim amount payment will end once the insured life has recovered to the extent that he can perform more than 75% of the main duties of his own occupation. 

The claim amount will be calculated according to the loss of income or the severity of disability criteria. 

The insured life will not qualify for a claim under the occupational disability criteria if the insured life is not gainfully employed at the time of the claim event occurring. Such a claim will be assessed against the impairment and illness criteria. 

###### **Impairment or illness** 

The insured life can qualify for a claim under: 

- functional impairment or 

- critical illness or 

- fracture and hospitalisation 

Momentum will pay for the event that provides the highest payout if the insured life qualifies for a claim amount payment under more than one of the impairment or illness claim events. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 4 

If the insured life still qualifies for a functional impairment claim after a critical illness, fracture or hospitalisation claim has been paid, Momentum will continue to pay the defined payment for the balance of the payment period. 

###### <u>Functional impairment</u> 

The claim events are not linked to the insured life's ability to perform occupational activities. 

The claim amount is based on the severity of a medical impairment that occurs after the starting date of the benefit as diagnosed by an appropriate specialist (registered with the Health Professions Council of South Africa (HPCSA) and resulting in the specified functional restrictions defined below. 

The insured life will not be able to claim under functional impairment after the chosen expiry age. 

The insured life must undergo reasonable optimal treatment and their functional impairment will be determined after they have reached (reasonable) Maximal Medical Improvement (MMI). At this stage, a specialist approved by Momentum must declare the functional impairment total, permanent and continuous for the foreseeable future. 

The insured life will not be required to undergo reasonable optimal treatment if a specialist, that Momentum has approved, has established that the functional impairment is permanent, and that further treatment will not lessen the severity of the condition. 

- Reasonable optimal treatment: This is the treatment that Momentum may reasonably expect the insured life to undergo according to the guidelines for the specific condition under the generally accepted medical practice at claim stage. The insured life is expected to comply with his treatment routine.. 

- Maximal Medical Improvement (MMI): A condition or state that is well stabilised and unlikely to change substantially in the next year with or without medical treatment. There may be some change over time, but further recovery is not expected. 

A panel of accredited medical specialists will determine how many Activities of Daily Living (ADL) the insured life can perform. 

A claim will be admitted only if the claim event is a permanent condition. 

Momentum will pay for the event that provides the highest payout if the insured life qualifies for a claim amount payment under more than one of the events. 

Refer to Appendix 1 in the technical guide for the functional impairment claim events. 

###### <u>Critical illness</u> 

Momentum will pay a percentage of the benefit amount if the insured life meets the requirements of one of the defined critical illnesses claim events. 

Momentum will not pay for a subsequent critical illness claim event while the insured life is receiving a critical illness claim amount payment. 

Refer to Appendix 2 and Appendix 3 in the technical guide  for the critical illness claim events. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 5 

###### <u>Fracture and hospitalisation</u> 

Momentum will pay a percentage of the benefit amount if the insured life meets the requirements of one of the defined fracture and hospitalisation claim events. 

Momentum will pay for the event with the longest payment period if the insured life qualifies for a payment under more than one of the defined fracture or hospitalisation claim events. 

Momentum will not pay for a subsequent claim event for fracture or hospitalisation that occurs while the insured life is receiving a fracture and hospitalisation claim amount payment. 

Refer to Appendix 6 in the technical guide for the fracture and hospitalisation claim events. 

Claim amount ____________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

Momentum will use the following assessment criteria to determine the monthly claim amount and will use the criteria resulting in the highest claim amount: 

- Loss of income 

- Severity of disability 

- Severity of impairment or illness 

###### **Loss of income** 

Momentum will pay the actual loss of income up to the maximum of the benefit amount. 

Actual loss of income is calculated as the difference between the insured life’s net pre-disability income and any net income that the insured life earns during the period of disability. 

Two years after the claim event the actual loss of income is calculated as the difference between 75% of the insured life’s net pre-disability income and any net income that the insured life earns during disability. 

Net income refers to gross income less income tax payable on this income (determined by applying the relevant year of assessment’s income tax tables). 

###### **Severity of disability** 

The claim amount will be between 25% and 100% of the benefit amount, depending on the extent to which the insured life is unable to perform the main duties of his own occupation. 

The severity of disability assessment criteria, including the partial claim upgrade, will only apply during the first year after the claim event. For professional occupations these criteria will apply for the first two years after the claim event. 

Partial Claim Upgrade 

- If the full benefit amount has been paid for a continuous period of three months, the insured life will qualify for a Partial Claim Upgrade. 

- Momentum will continue to pay the full benefit amount after the three months, provided that the insured life is partially disabled 

- The full benefit amount will only be paid while the severity of disability assessment criteria applies (the first year after the claim event or the first two years after the claim event for professionals). 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 6 

###### **Severity of impairment or illness** 

Momentum will pay a percentage of the benefit amount for a specified payment period if the insured life meets any of the requirements for functional impairment, critical illness or fracture and hospitalisation claim events. 

Refer to Appendix 6 in the technical guide for payout levels and payment periods for severity of impairment and illness claim events. 

###### **General** 

The claim amount is paid monthly in arrears. 

The daily claim amount will be calculated as 1/30 of the monthly benefit amount. 

A proportionate payment will be made in respect of any part of a month should the insured life be rehabilitated before the payment date. Following rehabilitation, the insured life will retain his cover. 

Any outstanding debt will be deducted from the claim amount. 

###### **Premium waiver during a claim** 

The premium will be waived for this benefit while a claim is being paid. 

No proportionate premiums can be paid; therefore, premiums are waived from the next financial month after the expiry of the waiting period. 

If the claim amount is less than the full benefit amount, the whole premium will still be waived. 

For a seven-day waiting period, premiums will be waived after the insured life has been continuously disabled for more than 28 days. 

If Momentum collected premiums for a period not applicable for premium payment, it will be refunded to the policyholder as an advance on the policy. This (advance) amount will be deducted from the next premium payment. 

If this benefit is the only benefit on the policy, the policy fee will be waived while a claim is being paid. 

Definition of income _____________________________________________________________________________________________ 

Income is defined as one of the following: 

|Total Cost to Company|The total sum of all taxable income payable or benefits<br>receivable on account of the insured life's<br>employment, or any services rendered by the insured<br>life, plus<br>•<br>the value of any fringe benefits (as provided for in<br>the Income Tax Act) awarded to the employee<br>•<br>retirement fund contributions made by the life<br>insured's employer,<br>•<br>the cost of any other benefits paid for by the<br>insured life's employer, and<br>•<br>any dividends received by the life insured due to<br>shareholding or member's interest held in the<br>employer (where the employer is a company or<br>close corporation).|
|---|---|



Net income refers to Total Cost to Company (as defined above) less income tax payable on this Income (determined by applying the relevant year of assessment’s income tax tables). 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 7 

Pre-disability income will be increased by inflation from the date of the claim event to the date on which the loss of income is calculated. 

Benefit reductions _______________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The claim amount will be reduced if: 

- the benefit amount exceeds 75% of the insured life's pre-disability net income or 

- the policyholder is receiving a disability income from another insurance policy contract as a result of the insured life's disability. 

###### **Benefit amount exceeds 75% of the pre-disability net income** 

The benefit amount will be reduced to ensure that it does not exceed 75% of the insured life's pre-disability net income. 

###### **Income from other income disability policy contracts** 

The claim amount will be reduced to ensure that the total of the claim amount payment and the income from the other policy contract do not exceed 75% of the insured life's pre-disability net income. 

###### **General** 

Pre-disability net income will be calculated as the insured life’s net income (as defined under definition of income) averaged over the period of 12 months immediately preceding the date of disability. 

Any Functional Protector or Complete Functional Protector claim amount paid to the policyholder will not be considered in the benefit reduction calculations. 

Payments for lump sum disability benefits are excluded for the benefit reduction calculation. 

Additional benefit reductions _____________________________________________________________________________________ 

The following additional benefit reduction rules apply: 

- Six months after a claim, the claim amount will be reduced if the insured life is not covered under a group disability income policy contract or 

- the insured life is covered under a group disability income policy contract but is not receiving a disability income payment under the group disability income policy contract the claim amount will be reduced after the waiting period under the group disability income policy contract has been reached. 

In both instances, the reduction will be calculated as 70% of the claim amount. In other words, the claim amount will be reduced by 70%. 

Waiting period ___________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

A one month waiting period is available. 

Premiums are payable during the waiting period. 

If the insured life dies within the waiting period, a claim will not be paid. 

The first monthly claim amount payment will be made only after the insured life has been disabled for the waiting period he chose. 

Claim amount payments for functional impairment, critical illness or fracture and hospitalisation will only be made after the waiting period has expired. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 8 

Off period ________________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

An "off period" of three months applies. 

This means that if the insured life is rehabilitated and claims again for the same cause within the three months, the waiting period will be waived. 

Guaranteed insurability __________________________________________________________________________________________ 

Momentum will allow policyholder to increase the benefit amount without any medical underwriting after the benefit anniversary if the insured life's income increases at a rate that exceeds the maximum voluntary benefit amount increase percentage. 

The total annual increase (annual voluntary benefit amount increase plus the guaranteed insurability increase) will be limited to twice the inflation rate used for increases by Momentum at that point, capped to 20%. 

This additional benefit amount increase may not be exercised if any of the following apply: 

- the insured life is over the age of 55 

- voluntary benefit amount increases were not selected 

- the insured life is already disabled or was disabled during the 12 months preceding the date of the benefit amount increase 

- a health loading applies to the insured life 

Momentum must receive a written request to increase the benefit amount within one month after the benefit anniversary. 

Conversion Option _______________________________________________________________________________________________ The policyholder has the option to convert this benefit to one of the following benefits: 

- Functional Protector 

- Complete Functional Protector 

These benefits pay a monthly claim amount for the remainder of the insured's life if he is permanently impaired. 

The benefit amount being converted is subject to the maximum benefit limit for the chosen benefit at the time of the conversion. 

Medical underwriting will be required if: 

- any specific exclusion applies to this benefit, or 

- a health or occupational loading applies to this benefit. 

End of benefit ____________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

This benefit ends on the earliest of: 

- The death of the insured life. 

- The end of the benefit term. 

- Conversion to a Functional Protector or Complete Functional Protector 

- The cancellation of the policy or benefit as a result of: 

   - any event covered in the policy contract 

   - notification from the policyholder.

- <mark>fracture and hospitalisation</mark> 

Momentum will pay for the event that provides the highest payout if the insured life qualifies for a claim amount payment under more than one of the impairment or illness claim events. 

If the insured life still qualifies for a functional impairment claim after a critical illness, fracture or hospitalisation claim has been paid, Momentum will continue to pay the defined payment for the balance of the payment period. 

###### <u>Functional impairment</u> 

The claim events are not linked to the insured life's ability to perform occupational activities. 

The claim amount is based on the severity of a medical impairment that occurs after the starting date of the benefit as diagnosed by an appropriate specialist (registered with the Health Professions Council of South Africa (HPCSA) and resulting in the specified functional restrictions defined below. 

The insured life must undergo reasonable optimal treatment and their functional impairment will be determined after they have reached (reasonable) Maximal Medical Improvement (MMI). At this stage, a specialist approved by Momentum must declare the functional impairment total, permanent and continuous for the foreseeable future. 

The insured life will not be required to undergo reasonable optimal treatment if a specialist, that Momentum has approved, has established that the functional impairment is permanent and that further treatment will not lessen the severity of the condition. 

- <mark>Reasonable optimal treatment: This is the treatment that Momentum may reasonably expect the insured life to undergo according to the guidelines for the specific condition under the generally accepted medical practice at claim stage. The insured life is expected to comply with his treatment routine.</mark> 

- <mark>Maximal Medical Improvement (MMI): A condition or state that is well stabilised and unlikely to change substantially in the next year with or without medical treatment. There may be some change over time, but further recovery is not expected.</mark> 

A panel of accredited medical specialists will determine how many Activities of Daily Living (ADL) the insured life can perform. 

A claim will be admitted only if the claim event is a permanent condition. 

Momentum will pay for the event that provides the highest payout if the insured life qualifies for a claim amount payment under more than one of the impairment events. 

Refer to Appendix 1 in the technical guide for the functional impairment claim events. 

###### <u>Critical illness</u> 

Momentum will pay a percentage of the benefit amount if the insured life meets the requirements of one of the defined critical illnesses claim events. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 5 

Momentum will not pay for a subsequent critical illness claim event that occurs while the insured life is receiving a critical illness claim amount payment. 

Refer to Appendix 2 and Appendix 3 in the technical guide for the critical illness claim events. 

###### <u>Fracture and hospitalisation</u> 

Momentum will pay a percentage of the benefit amount if the insured life meets the requirements of one of the defined fracture and hospitalisation claim events. 

Momentum will pay for the event with the longest payment period if the insured life qualifies for a payment under more than one of the defined fracture or hospitalisation claim events. 

Momentum will not pay for a subsequent claim event for fracture or hospitalisation that occurs while the insured life is receiving a fracture and hospitalisation claim amount payment. 

Refer to Appendix 6 in the technical guide for the fracture and hospitalisation claim events. 

Claim amount ____________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

Momentum will use the following assessment criteria to determine the monthly claim amount and will use the criteria resulting in the highest claim amount: 

- <mark>Loss of income</mark> 

- <mark>Severity of disability</mark> 

- <mark>Severity of impairment or illness</mark> 

###### **Loss of income** 

Momentum will pay the actual loss of income up to the maximum of the benefit amount. 

Actual loss of income is calculated as the difference between the insured life’s net pre-disability income and any net income the insured life earns during the period of disability. 

Net income refers to gross income less income tax payable on this income (determined by applying the relevant year of assessment’s income tax tables). 

###### **Severity of disability** 

The claim amount will be between 25% and 100% of the benefit amount, depending on the extent to which the insured life is unable to perform the main duties of his own occupation. 

The severity of disability assessment criteria, including the partial claim upgrade, will only apply during the first year after the claim event. For professional occupations these criteria will apply for the first two years after the claim event. 

Partial Claim Upgrade 

- <mark>If the full benefit amount has been paid for a continuous period of three months, the insured life will qualify for a Partial Claim Upgrade.</mark> 

- <mark>Momentum will continue to pay the full benefit amount after the three months, provided that the insured life is partially disabled.</mark> 

- <mark>The full benefit amount will only be paid while the severity of disability assessment criteria applies (first year after the claim event or first two years after the claim event for professionals).</mark> 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 6 

###### **Severity of impairment or illness** 

Momentum will pay a percentage of the benefit amount for a specified payment period if the insured life meets any of the requirements for functional impairment, critical illness or fracture and hospitalisation claim events. 

Refer to <u><mark>Appendix 6</mark></u> in the technical guide for payout levels and payment periods for severity of impairment and illness claim events. 

###### **General** 

The claim amount is paid monthly in arrears. 

The daily claim amount will be calculated as 1/30 of the monthly benefit amount. 

A proportionate payment will be made in respect of any part of a month should the insured life be rehabilitated before the payment date. Following rehabilitation, the insured life will retain his cover. 

The premium will be waived for this benefit while a claim is being paid. 

Any outstanding debt will be deducted from the claim amount. 

###### **Premium waiver during a claim** 

The premium will be waived for this benefit while a claim is being paid. 

No proportionate premiums can be paid; therefore, premiums are waived from the next financial month after the expiry of the waiting period. 

If the claim amount is less than the full benefit amount, the whole premium will still be waived. 

For a seven-day waiting period, premiums will be waived after the insured life has been continuously disabled for more than 28 days. 

If Momentum collected premiums for a period not applicable for premium payment, it will be refunded to the policyholder as an advance on the policy. This (advance) amount will be deducted from the next premium payment. 

If this benefit is the only benefit on the policy, the policy fee will be waived while a claim is being paid. 

Definition of income _____________________________________________________________________________________________ 

Income is defined as one of the following: 

The total sum of all taxable income payable or benefits receivable on account of the insured life's employment, or any services rendered by the insured life, plus 

- the value of any fringe benefits (as provided for in the Income Tax Act) awarded to the employee, 

- • retirement fund contributions made by the life 

- Total Cost to Company insured's employer, • the cost of any other benefits paid for by the insured 

- life's employer, and 

- • any dividends received by the life insured due to shareholding or member's interest held in the employer (where the employer is a company or close corporation). 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 7 

**<mark>Net income</mark>** refers to Total Cost to Company (as defined above) less income tax payable on this Income (determined by applying the relevant year of assessment’s income tax tables). 

Pre-disability net income will be increased by inflation from the date of the claim event to the date on which the loss of income is calculated. 

Benefit reductions _______________________________________________________________________________________________ 

###### The claim amount will be reduced if: 

- <mark>the benefit amount exceeds 100% of the insured life's pre-disability net income</mark> or 

- <mark>the policyholder is receiving a disability income from another insurance policy contract as a result of the insured life's disability.</mark> 

###### **Benefit amount exceeds 100% of the pre-disability net income** 

The benefit amount will be reduced to ensure that it does not exceed 100% of the insured life's pre-disability net income. 

###### **Income from other income disability policy contracts** 

The claim amount will be reduced to ensure that the total of the claim amount payment and the income from the other policy contract does not exceed 100% of the insured life's pre-disability net income. 

###### **General** 

Pre-disability net income will be calculated as the insured life's net income averaged over the period of 12 months immediately preceding the date of the disability. 

Any Functional Protector or Complete Functional Protector claim amount paid to the policyholder will not be considered in the benefit reduction calculations. 

Payments for lump sum disability benefits are specifically excluded from the benefit reduction calculation. 

Additional benefit reductions _____________________________________________________________________________________ 

The following additional benefit reduction rules apply: 

- <mark>Six months after a claim, the claim amount will be reduced if the insured life is not covered under a group disability income policy contract or</mark> 

- <mark>the insured life is covered under a group disability income policy contract but is not receiving a disability income payment under the group disability income policy contract the claim amount will be reduced after the waiting period under the group disability income policy contract has been reached.</mark> 

In both instances, the reduction will be calculated as 70% of the claim amount. In other words, the claim amount will be reduced by 70%. 

Successive claims_________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The following benefit payment periods are available: 

- <mark>12-month benefit payment period</mark> 

- <mark>24-month benefit payment period</mark> 

Total payments throughout the benefit term will be limited to the chosen benefit payment period for claims due to the same bodily injury or related causes or illness.

Factors affecting monthly benefit payments ______________________________________________________________________ 

The benefit payments end if: 

- <mark>the insured life is no longer qualifies for a claim amount payment</mark> 

- <mark>the benefit ends</mark> 

- <mark>the insured life is not receiving or is refusing the medical treatment they could reasonably be expected to undergo according to current best practice medical protocols and which could substantially improve or remove the condition being claimed for.</mark> 

Ongoing assessments ____________________________________________________________________________________________ 

Once a claim has been admitted and Momentum has started paying the monthly claim amount, the insured life's health will be assessed from time to time. If the insured life fails to undergo the reassessment within three months of Momentum's notification, the claim payments may be cancelled. 

These assessments will determine whether the insured life still qualifies for a claim and has been receiving such medical treatment as is appropriate for his condition. The benefit payments will end if the insured life no longer qualifies for a claim and the applicable premium must be paid. 

Momentum will cover the cost of the reassessment by a doctor chosen by Momentum. 

The ongoing assessment may be waived for the impairment or illness claim events. 

Following rehabilitation, the monthly benefit amount will start at the level of the last benefit payment and will increase on every benefit anniversary.

###### **Conversion of Complete Income Protector** 

The policyholder has the option to convert a Complete Income Protector to this benefit, which pays a monthly claim amount for the remainder of the insured's life if he is permanently impaired. 

The benefit amount being converted is subject to the maximum benefit limit for this benefit at the time of the conversion. 

###### **General** 

Medical underwriting will be required if any of the abovementioned benefits: 

- any specific exclusion, or 

- include a health or occupational loading. 

The benefit may not be converted if: 

- a claim has been submitted for any of the benefits listed above or 

- a claim is in payment under a Complete Income Protector and Group Income Top-up Benefit. 

This benefit will not pay out if the claim event for any of the abovementioned benefits occurred before the conversion. 

A partial conversion will not be allowed. 

The policyholder may choose any increase option and premium pattern for this benefit subject to the new business rules. 

If there is a premium waiver benefit attached to the benefit being converted to a Functional Protector/Complete Functional Protector, then at conversion the policyholder has the option to add a new premium waiver benefit to the Functional Protector/Complete Functional Protector. If the new premium waiver is the same type of waiver that existed on the benefit being converted, only a declaration of health will be required to add this new premium waiver to the Functional Protector/ Complete Functional Protector. The policyholder can select any increase option on the premium waiver (increasing or level). The new premium waiver will be subject to the new business entry age and benefit limits. 

A new policy contract will be issued on conversion. 

The conversion will be an add and remove alteration. If this benefit is added without the removal of the benefit being converted, normal underwriting will apply. 

If the benefit being converted is removed or it is within three months of the expiry, special underwriting conditions will apply. 

End of benefit ________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

This benefit ends on the earliest of: 

- The death of the insured life. 

- The cancellation of the policy or benefit as a result of: 

   - any event covered in the policy contract 

   - notification from the policyholder.

- any specific exclusion, or 

- include a health or occupational loading. 

The benefit may not be converted if: 

- a claim has been submitted for any of the benefits listed above, or 

- a claim is in payment under a Complete Income Protector and Group Income Top-up Benefit. 

This benefit will not pay out if the claim event for any of the abovementioned benefits occurred before the conversion. 

A partial conversion will not be allowed. 

The policyholder may choose any increase option and premium pattern for this benefit subject to the new business rules. 

A new policy contract will be issued on conversion. 

The conversion will be an add and remove alteration. If this benefit is added without the removal of the benefit being converted, normal underwriting will apply.

The policyholder can select any increase option on the premium waiver (increasing or level). The new premium waiver will be subject to the new business entry age and benefit limits. 

If the benefit being converted is removed or it is within three months of the expiry, special underwriting conditions will apply. End of benefit ____________________________________________________________________________________________________

###### **Critical Illness** 

The diagnosis of the main life's spouse or the main insured life's biological or legally adopted children with one of the defined critical illnesses. 

A maximum of one claim for the spouse and one claim per child will be admitted for this category. An overall maximum of four claims will be admitted for this category. 

Momentum will not pay for a subsequent critical illness claim event that occurs while the insured life is receiving a critical illness claim amount payment. 

###### **Hospitalisation** 

The main insured life, the main insured life's spouse or the main insured life's biological or legally adopted children are admitted to the hospital for a period exceeding seven days. 

Multiple claims will be admitted per insured life for this category. An overall maximum of four claims will be admitted for this category. 

Momentum will not pay a second claim amount if an insured life is hospitalised again for the same reason within ten days of discharge. We will treat it as being related to the event that led to the previous hospital admission. 

If the readmission to the hospital is due to an unrelated event, the normal waiting period will apply. 

If this benefit is attached to a stand-alone benefit with a seven-day waiting period, the stand-alone benefit will pay out if the main insured life is admitted to the hospital for a period exceeding seven days. The main insured life will therefore only be covered under the hospitalisation benefit if the stand-alone benefit’s waiting period is more than seven days. 

Any claim submitted within the first 30 days of the start date of the benefit will not be paid. 

Any claim resulting from any physical defects, illnesses or diseases that the insured life suffered from, was aware of, or received medical advice or treatment in the three years before the start date of this benefit, is excluded for the first three years of the benefit. When restarting the benefit, a new three-year period will apply. 

###### **Pre-existing exclusion** 

The pre-existing exclusion applies to all claim events mentioned above for nonunderwritten insured lives. 

Any claims resulting from any physical defects, illnesses or diseases that the insured life suffered from, was aware of, or received medical advice or treatment in the three years before the start date of this benefit, are excluded for the first three years. 

When restarting the benefit, or increasing the benefit amount, a new three-year period will apply. 

Claim amount ________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

###### **Death of the main insured life** 

The claim amount is a lump sum equal to three monthly claim amount payments under the stand-alone to which this benefit is attached. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 4 

###### **Death of the main insured life's spouse** 

The claim amount is a lump sum equal to three monthly claim amount payments under the stand-alone to which this benefit is attached. 

The maximum lump sum payment will be limited to R100 000. 

###### **Death of the main insured life's biological or legally adopted children** 

The claim amount is a lump sum equal to three monthly claim amount payments under the stand-alone to which this benefit is attached. 

The maximum lump sum payment will be limited to: 

- R10 000 for children younger than age six next birthday and 

- R30 000 for children between age seven and 18 (19 next birthday). 

###### **Critical Illness** 

The claim amount is a lump sum equal to three monthly claim amount payments under the stand-alone to which this benefit is attached. 

The maximum lump sum payment will be limited to R100 000. 

###### **Hospitalisation** 

The claim amount is a lump sum equal to 50% of the monthly claim amount payments under the stand-alone to which this benefit is attached. 

The maximum lump sum payment will be limited to R75 000. 

Waiting period _______________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The claim amount for hospitalisation will only be paid after an insured life has been admitted to the hospital for a period exceeding seven days (the waiting period). 

Survival period _______________________________________________________________________________________________ 

There is no explicit survival period. 

A claim will only be admitted if the main insured life, the main insured life’s spouse or the main insured life’s biological or legally adopted children meets the requirements of the defined claim event, prior to their death. 

No medical test or examination concluded after the insured life’s death will be considered when evaluating a claim.

- The end of the stand-alone to which this benefit is attached. 

- The end of the benefit term. 

- The cancellation of the policy or benefit as a result of: 

   - any event covered in the policy contract 

   - notification from the policyholder.
