- Ancillary benefits_________________________________________________________________________________________________ The policyholder may add the following ancillary benefits: 

• Premium Waiver (increasing or level) - Death • Premium Waiver (increasing or level) - Comprehensive Disability • Premium Waiver (increasing or level) - Functional Impairment • Premium Waiver – Retrenchment • Longevity Protector® – Critical Illness • Specified Claim Event Enhancer Beneficiaries and cessions ________________________________________________________________________________________ The policyholder may not nominate beneficiaries. Collateral cessions are allowed on the stand-alone benefit. Claim event ______________________________________________________________________________________________________ The insured life or the insured life's biological or legally adopted child meets the requirements of one of the defined critical illness claim events. Claim event categories ___________________________________________________________________________________________ Claim events are divided into claim categories. For each category, the payout percentages are based on the severity of the critical illness event. Claims for the Early cancer category will be limited to a maximum of R100 000 per claim event. Claims under the Additional claim events for children category will be limited to a maximum benefit amount of R250 000. Refer to Appendix 2 and Appendix 3 in the technical guide for the claim events. 

Claim amount for ancillary benefits _______________________________________________________________________________ 

Each severity level has an associated “percentage payout”. 

If more than one claim event occurs as a result of the same cause, a claim will be admitted for the claim event resulting in the highest payout. 

Momentum will pay the balance of the benefit amount for claims with a percentage payout of 100%. 

All cardiac events that occur within 30 days of each other will be considered a single claim event. 

Any outstanding debt will be deducted from the claim amount. 

###### **Determining the claim amount** 

For the first claim, the claim amount is calculated as the percentage payout multiplied by the benefit amount. The benefit amount is reduced by the amount of any claim. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 4 

For a subsequent claim in a different category, the claim amount is calculated by multiplying the percentage payout by the reduced benefit amount. This amount is paid irrespective of the relative severity of the new claim and the original claim. 

A subsequent claim in the same category will be paid only if the claim event is more severe than previous claims in the same category. The amount that is paid is based on the difference between the percentage payout for the new claim and the total percentage paid for that category (the "additional percentage payout"). In this case, the claim amount is calculated as the "additional percentage payout" multiplied by the benefit amount (only adjusted for claims in other categories). 

Any claim under the stand-alone benefit to which this benefit is attached will reduce the benefit amount by the same proportion in which the benefit amount of the stand-alone benefit reduces. 

Any claim under this benefit will reduce the benefit amount under the stand-alone benefit to which this benefit is attached by the claim amount for the ancillary benefit. The benefit amount under any other ancillary benefit attached to the same stand-alone benefit will remain unchanged if the benefit amount of this other ancillary is less than the reduced stand-alone benefit amount. The benefit amount of the other ancillary will be reduced to the same level as the reduced stand-alone benefit amount of the other ancillary if the amount is greater than the reduced stand-alone benefit amount. 

Momentum will reduce the contract benefit premium if this benefit is cancelled due to a claim for the full benefit amount. 

The benefit premium will not reduce in the event of a partial claim. 

###### **Related claims** 

A related claim is a claim where the claim event progressed from a previous claim event. 

Momentum will treat a claim related to any previous claim in a different category as if it is in the same category as the claim it progressed from. 

Claim amount for stand-alone benefits ___________________________________________________________________________ 

The benefit automatically reinstates for unrelated claims. 

The benefit premium will not reduce in the event of a partial claim. 

All cardiac events that occur within 30 days of each other will be considered a single claim event. 

Any outstanding debt will be deducted from the claim amount. 

###### **Determining the claim amount** 

The claim amount is calculated as the percentage payout multiplied by the benefit amount. 

The benefit amount will not be reduced by the claim amount. 

If more than one claim event occurs due to the same cause, a claim will be admitted for the claim event resulting in the highest payout. 

###### **Unrelated claims** 

An unrelated claim is a claim where the claim event did not progress from a previous claim event and/or previous condition which gave rise to the claim event. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 5 

Subsequent unrelated claims will be paid for all claim event categories. In this case, the claim amount is calculated as the percentage payout, multiplied by the benefit amount. 

###### **Related claims** 

A related claim is a claim where the claim event progressed from a previous claim event. 

A claim that is related to any previous claim in a different category will be treated as if it is in the same category as the claim it progressed from. 

A subsequent related claim will only be paid if the claim event is more severe than the previous claim. The claim amount that we pay is based on the difference between the percentage payout for the new claim and the total percentage paid for the previous claim/s (the "additional percentage payout"). In this case, the claim amount is calculated as the additional percentage payout, multiplied by the benefit amount. 

Critical Illness Cover for Children _________________________________________________________________________________ 

Momentum will only admit claims in respect of the insured life's biological or legally adopted child from their date of birth to age 18 (19 next birthday) who is a permanent resident of the Republic of South Africa. 

The benefit amount under the Critical Illness Cover for Children is the lesser of: 

- 10% of the benefit amount under the insured life's benefit at the time of the claim and 

- R250 000 

The claim amount is calculated as the percentage payout multiplied by the benefit amount. 

###### **Child-related claims** 

A related claim is a claim where the claim event progressed from a previous claim event. Momentum will treat a claim related to any previous claim in a different category, as if it is in the same category as the claim it progressed from. 

If a child qualifies for a claim event as specified under the Additional claim events for children category, they will not be able to claim for this event under any of the other adult categories. 

A claim will not be admitted if any condition that existed before the child became eligible for this benefit, directly brought about or accelerated the claim event. This includes all symptoms for an illness or condition experienced by the child that could have allowed for the illness or condition to be diagnosed and was present before the start date of the policy. Congenital birth defects will be considered pre-existing conditions. They will not be covered, except where the benefit was in force for the entire duration of the pregnancy, or 12 months prior to the legal adoption of children. 

There is no limitation on the number of children covered on a parent’s benefit. 

Each child will be treated as a separate life on the policy and claims will be treated separately for each child. 

The number of claims per child is not limited to a specific number of claims. Claims within the congenital anomaly repair event definition are limited to three per child for unrelated events. 

A claim under the Critical Illness Cover for Children will not reduce the benefit amount on this benefit or any other benefit on the policy. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 6 

###### **Critical Illness Cover for Children claim example** 

Mike Myriad has a Complete Critical Illness Benefit of R2 610 253. His son develops bacterial meningitis and qualifies for a 10% payout. 

The benefit amount under the Critical Illness Cover for Children is the lesser of: 

- 10% of the benefit amount under the insured life’s benefit at the time of the claim and 

- R250 000 

(1) 10% of R2 610 253.00 = R261 025.30 

(2) The lesser of R261 025.30 and R250 000 = R250 000 

(3) The claim payment will be (10% of R250 000) = R25 000 

Survival period ___________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

There is no explicit survival period. 

A claim will only be admitted if the insured life meets the requirements of the defined claim event, prior to their death. 

No medical test or examination concluded after the insured life’s death will be considered when evaluating a claim. 

End of benefit ____________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

This benefit ends on the earliest of: 

- The death of the insured life. 

- The end of the benefit term. 

- The payment of the full benefit amount. (Applicable to ancillary benefits only). 

- The cancellation of the policy or benefit as a result of: 

   - any event covered in the policy contract 

   - notification from the policyholder.

Page 4 

For a subsequent claim in a different category, the claim amount is calculated by multiplying the percentage payout by the reduced benefit amount. This amount is paid irrespective of the relative severity of the new claim and the original claim. 

A subsequent claim in the same category will be paid only if the claim event is more severe than previous claims in the same category. The amount that is paid is based on the difference between the percentage payout for the new claim and the total percentage paid for that category (the "additional percentage payout"). In this case the claim amount is calculated as the "additional percentage payout" multiplied by the benefit amount (only adjusted for claims in other categories). 

Any claim under the stand-alone benefit to which this benefit is attached, will reduce the benefit amount by the same proportion in which the benefit amount of the stand-alone benefit reduces. 

Any claim under this benefit will reduce the benefit amount under the stand-alone benefit to which this benefit is attached, by the claim amount for the ancillary benefit. The benefit amount under any other ancillary benefit attached to the same stand-alone benefit will remain unchanged if the benefit amount of this other ancillary is less than the reduced stand-alone benefit amount. The benefit amount of the other ancillary will be reduced to the same level as the reduced stand-alone benefit amount of the other ancillary if the amount is greater than the reduced stand-alone benefit amount. 

Momentum will reduce the contract benefit premium if this benefit is cancelled due to a claim for the full benefit amount. 

The benefit premium will not reduce in the event of a partial claim. 

###### **Related claims** 

A related claim is a claim where the claim event progressed from a previous claim event. 

Momentum will treat a claim related to any previous claim in a different category, as if it is in the same category as the claim it progressed from. 

Claim amount for stand-alone benefits ___________________________________________________________________________ 

The benefit automatically reinstates for unrelated claims. 

All cardiac events that occur within 30 days of each other will be considered a single claim event. The benefit premium will not reduce in the event of a partial claim. 

Any outstanding debt will be deducted from the claim amount. 

###### **Determining the claim amount** 

The claim amount is calculated as the percentage payout multiplied by the benefit amount. 

The benefit amount will not be reduced by the claim amount. 

If more than one claim event occurs due to the same cause, a claim will be admitted for the claim event resulting in the highest payout. 

###### **Unrelated claims** 

An unrelated claim is a claim where the claim event did not progress from a previous claim event and/or previous condition which gave rise to the claim event. 

Subsequent unrelated claims will be paid for all claim event categories.

#### Breadth of Cover Upgrade Package 

Description _______________________________________________________________________________ 

The Breadth of Cover Upgrade Package is an optional ancillary package that upgrades the comprehensive critical illness benefit range to provide complete breadth of cover and additional features. 

The comprehensive critical illness benefit range refers to the: 

- Comprehensive Critical Illness Benefit 

- Comprehensive Critical Illness Plus Benefit 

- Elevated Comprehensive Critical Illness Benefit 

- Elevated Comprehensive Critical Illness Plus Benefit. 

Special conditions ____________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The Breadth of Cover Upgrade Package is only available on the comprehensive critical illness range. 

These features are automatically included in the complete critical illness range of benefits. 

Type of benefit _______________________________________________________________________________________________ 

Ancillary 

Packages _____________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

###### **Comprehensive Critical Illness Benefit or Elevated Comprehensive Critical Illness Benefit** 

If the package is added to one of these benefits, it will enhance the existing benefit by the following: 

- Five additional claim event categories: 

   - Breadth of Cover Guarantee® 

   - Early Cancer 

   - Additional claim events for children 

   - Trauma 

   - Endocrine and metabolic diseases 

- Additional claim events with payout percentages of 5%, 10% or 15% on the diagnosis of the insured life (or the insured life’s biological or legally adopted child) with one of the following critical illnesses or a critical illness that affects any of the following: 

   - Cardiac and arterial system; cancer; nervous system, connective tissue diseases; musculoskeletal system; gastrointestinal system; urinary tract; respiratory system; ear, nose and throat system; visual; HIV/aids; terminal illness, severe aplastic anaemia; major burns and catch-all 

   - The maximum benefit amount for Critical Illness Cover for Children increased to R250 000. 

   - All the claim event categories will automatically reinstate (for stand-alone benefits).

###### **Comprehensive Critical Illness Plus Benefit or Elevated Comprehensive Critical Illness Plus Benefit** 

If the package is added to one of these benefits, it will enhance the existing benefit by the following: 

- Three additional claim event categories: 

   - 

      - Breadth of Cover Guarantee<sup>®</sup> 

   - Early cancer 

   - Additional claim events for children 

- All the claim event categories will automatically reinstate for stand-alone benefits. 

- The cardiac and arterial claim category includes up to 3 stent payouts, provided the procedure is at least 30 days apart.

- The payout level for loss of hearing in one ear increased from 15% to 25%. 

- The maximum benefit amount for Critical Illness Cover for Children increased to R250 000.

Beneficiaries and cessions ______________________________________________________________________ 

The policyholder may not nominate beneficiaries. 

Collateral cessions are not allowed. 

Claim event __________________________________________________________________________________ 

Infection by any Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) or being diagnosed as having Acquired Immuno-deficiency Syndrome (Aids), if the insured life can prove to the satisfaction of Momentum that the infection is due to: 

- The transfusion of infected blood or blood products from a South African blood transfusion service that Momentum recognises, after the starting date of this policy, or 

- Executing his professional duties as a medical or dental practitioner registered with the Health Professions Council of South Africa (HPCSA) or a nurse registered with the SA Nursing Council, or 

- Receiving a transplanted organ that was previously infected with HIV, or 

- Any other medical or dental procedure that the HPCSA recognises and that a medical or dental practitioner registered with the HPCSA, or a nurse registered with the SA Nursing Council has performed on the insured life, or 

- Involvement in a road traffic accident, or 

- Involvement in a violent crime, or 

- Involvement in rape or an indecent assault crime. 

Momentum will consider a claim if the following requirements were followed: 

- Where HIV results from the transfusion of blood or blood products or a transplanted organ, the transfusion or organ donor service must accept liability for the incident. 

- In the event of an accident, violent crime, rape, indecent assault or infection in the execution of professional duties: 

   - An identified HIV test must be performed within 24 hours to confirm an HIVnegative status before the event. 

   - Proof that the insured life has started the prescribed treatment, a course of antiretroviral drugs, and the treatment course have been completed in full. 

In the event of an accident, violent crime, rape or indecent assault: 

- Momentum must receive notification within 14 days of an event where there is suspicion of HIV infection. 

- An identified HIV test must be performed within six months of the event to confirm an HIV-positive status. 

- If there was no suspicion of HIV infection and it can be proven that the insured life contracted HIV as a result of transfusion of infected blood or blood products or receiving a transplanted organ, Momentum must receive notification within six months of the insured life having tested HIV-positive. 

Momentum reserves the right to obtain independent diagnostic blood testing of the insured life (with proper identification, counselling and informed consent). 

If a cure for HIV/AIDS is found, cover under this benefit will no longer be available. 

Claim amount ________________________________________________________________________________ 

The claim amount is the lump sum benefit amount. 

Any outstanding debt will be deducted from the claim amount.

Claim event ______________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The insured life can qualify for a claim under either: 

- Occupational disability or 

- Functional impairment or 

- Critical illness 

###### **Occupational disability** 

An occupational disability is a disability caused by a bodily injury or illness to such an extent that the insured life is totally and permanently unable to perform the normal duties of their own occupation (up to the policy anniversary before the insured life's 65th birthday). The percentage payout for the occupational disability is 100% of the benefit amount. 

The insured life will not qualify for a claim under the occupational disability criteria if the insured life is not gainfully employed at the time of the claim event occurring. Such a claim will be assessed against the impairment and illness criteria. 

Momentum will not pay a claim if the insured life is not receiving or is refusing the medical treatment they could reasonably be expected to undergo according to current best practice medical protocols and which could substantially improve or remove the condition being claimed for. 

###### **Functional impairment** 

The claim events are not linked to the insured life's ability to perform occupational activities. 

The claim event is based on the severity of a medical impairment that occurs after the starting date of the benefit as diagnosed by an appropriate specialist (registered with the Health Professions Council of South Africa (HPCSA) and resulting in the specified functional restrictions. 

The insured life must undergo reasonable optimal treatment and their functional impairment will be determined after they have reached (reasonable) Maximal Medical Improvement (MMI). At this stage a specialist that Momentum have approved must declare the functional impairment total, permanent and continuous for the foreseeable future. 

The insured life will not be required to undergo reasonable optimal treatment if a specialist, that Momentum has approved, has established that the functional impairment is permanent and that further treatment will not lessen the severity of the condition. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 4 

- Reasonable optimal treatment: This is the treatment that Momentum may reasonably expect the insured life to undergo according to the guidelines for the specific condition under the generally accepted medical practice at claim stage. The insured life is expected to comply with their treatment routine. 

- Maximal Medical Improvement (MMI): A condition or state that is well stabilised and unlikely to change substantially in the next year with or without medical treatment. There may be some change over time, but further recovery is not expected. 

Momentum will not pay a claim if the insured life is not receiving or is refusing the medical treatment they could reasonably be expected to undergo according to current best practice medical protocols and which could substantially improve or remove the condition being claimed for. 

A panel of accredited medical specialists will determine how many Activities of Daily Living (ADL) the insured life can perform. 

A claim will be admitted only if the claim event is a permanent condition. 

Refer to Appendix 4 in the technical guide for the functional impairment claim events 

###### **Critical Illness** 

The insured life or the insured life's biological or legally adopted child meets the requirements of one of the defined critical illness claim events. 

Refer to Appendix 4 in the technical guide for the critical illness claim events.

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 5 

Refer to Appendix 4 in the technical guide for the claim events 

###### <u>Claim amount for ancillary benefits</u> 

For the first claim, the claim amount is calculated as the percentage payout multiplied by the benefit amount. The benefit amount for this benefit will be reduced by the claim amount. 

The claim amount for a subsequent claim in a different category is calculated by multiplying the percentage payout by the reduced benefit amount. This amount is paid irrespective of the relative severity of the new claim and the original claim. 

A subsequent claim in the same category will be paid if the claim event is more severe than previous claims in the same category. The claim amount paid is based on the difference between the percentage payout for the new claim and the total percentage paid for that category (the "additional percentage payout"). The claim amount is calculated as the "additional percentage payout" multiplied by the benefit amount (adjusted for claims in other categories). 

Any claim under the stand-alone benefit to which this benefit is attached, will reduce the benefit amount by the same proportion the benefit amount of the stand-alone benefit reduces. 

Any claim under this benefit will reduce the benefit amount under the stand-alone benefit to which this benefit is attached, by the claim amount for the ancillary benefit. 

The benefit amount under any other ancillary benefit attached to the same stand-alone benefit will remain unchanged if the benefit amount of this other ancillary is less than the reduced stand-alone benefit amount. 

The benefit amount of the other ancillary will be reduced to the same level as the reduced stand-alone benefit amount of the other ancillary if the amount is greater than the reduced stand-alone benefit amount. 

###### <u>Claim amount for stand-alone benefits</u> 

The benefit automatically reinstates for unrelated <u>claims.</u> 

An unrelated claim is a claim where the claim event did not progress from a previous claim event. 

Subsequent unrelated claims in the following categories will be paid regardless of the severity of the previous unrelated claim: 

- Cancer 

- Nervous system 

- Connective tissue diseases 

- Muskuloskeletal system 

- Gastrointestinal system 

- Urinary tract 

- Respiratory system 

- ENT system 

- Visual 

- HIV/aids 

- Terminal Illness 

- Severe aplastic anaemia 

- Major burns 

- Endocrine and metabolic diseases 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 6 

In this case, the claim amount is calculated as the percentage payout multiplied by the benefit amount. 

A subsequent claim in the same category will only be paid if the claim event is more severe than previous claims in the same category. The amount paid will be based on the difference between the percentage payout for the new claim and the total percentage paid for that category (the "additional percentage payout"). In this case, the claim amount is calculated as the additional percentage payout multiplied by the benefit amount. 

###### **Related claims** 

A related claim is where the claim event progressed from a previous claim event. Momentum will treat a claim that is related to any previous claim in a different category as if it is in the same category as the claim it progressed from. 

###### **General** 

If more than one claim event occurs as a result of the same cause, a claim will be admitted for the claim event resulting in the highest payment. 

Any outstanding debt will be deducted from the claim amount. 

Momentum will reduce the contract benefit premium if this is an ancillary benefit and is cancelled as a result of a claim. 

Momentum will always pay the balance of the benefit amount for claims with a percentage payout of 100%. 

Waiting period ___________________________________________________________________________________________________ There is no explicit waiting period. 

A claim will only be admitted once we have established the permanency of the disability according to our definition. 

No claim will be admitted if the insured life dies before permanency is established. 

Survival period ___________________________________________________________________________________________________ There is no explicit survival period. 

A claim will only be admitted if the insured life meets the requirements of the defined claim event, prior to their death. 

No medical test or examination concluded after the insured life’s death will be considered when evaluating a claim. 

Critical Illness Cover for Children _________________________________________________________________________________ 

Only children who are permanent residents of the Republic of South Africa qualify. 

All the insured life's biological or legally adopted children from their first to their 18th birthday (19 next birthday) qualify for the Critical Illness Cover for Children. 

Momentum will not admit a claim under the critical illness benefit if any condition existed prior to the child becoming eligible for this benefit directly or indirectly brought about or accelerated the claim event. This includes all symptoms experienced by the child that could have disclosed the illness or condition prior to eligibility. 

If both parents own a critical illness benefit, the child will qualify for a claim under both these benefits 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 7 

The child critical illness benefit will not apply within the first twelve months following the birth or adoption of a child. 

The benefit amount under the Critical Illness Cover for Children is the lesser of: 

- 10% of the insured life's benefit amount at the time of a claim and 

- R125 000. 

A subsequent claim will be paid in the same category only if the claim event is more severe than previous claims in the same category. The amount that is paid will be based on the difference between the percentage payout for the new claim and the total percentage paid for that category (the "additional percentage payout"). In this case, the claim amount is calculated as the additional percentage payout, multiplied by the benefit amount. 

End of benefit ____________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

This benefit ends on the earliest of: 

- The death of the insured life. 

- The end of the benefit term. 

- The payment of the full benefit amount. (for ancillary benefits only). 

- The cancellation of the policy or benefit as a result of: 

   - any event covered in the policy contract 

   - notification from the policyholder.

###### **Retrenchment** 

Retrenchment is the termination of employment by the insured life's employer as a result of "operational requirements". Operational requirements in this context means requirements based on the economic, technological, structural, or similar needs of an employer. 

Termination of employment for the following reasons shall not be considered as retrenchment: 

- Retirement (early, normal or ill-health) 

- Resignation or voluntary retrenchment 

- Dismissal 

- A fixed term employment contract coming to an end 

- Nervous breakdown, stress, burnout, disability or illness 

- Retrenchment resulting from government action 

- (The examples above should not be regarded as the only possible reason for termination of employment which would not be considered as retrenchment) 

Momentum will admit: 

- a maximum of two claims for retrenchment under this benefit. 

- a claim if the insured life has been continuously employed in a permanent fulltime occupation for at least two years of which one year must have been with the current employer. Self-employed individuals do not qualify for retrenchment cover. 

- a retrenchment claim from the official date of retrenchment or the date on which the insured life received their last salary-payment, whichever date occurs last.  The first payment will only be made after the waiting period has expired. 

Claim amount ____________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

###### Momentum will: 

- pay the full benefit amount as a lump sum if the insured life: 

   - suffers a disability caused by a bodily injury or illness to such an extent that he is totally and permanently unable to perform the normal duties of his own occupation (up to the policy anniversary before the insured life's 65th birthday) 

   - OR 

   - meets the requirements of one of the defined functional impairment claim events (up to the policy anniversary before the insured life's 70th birthday) 

   - − OR 

   - meets the requirements of one of the defined critical illnesses 

   - OR 

- pay 10% of the insured life's benefit amount up to a maximum of R125 000 if the insured life's biological or legally adopted child meets the requirements of one of the defined critical illnesses or functional impairment claim events 

- make a lump payment after every three months of continuous unemployment as the result of the insured life being retrenched (up to the policy anniversary immediately preceding the insured life's 65th birthday), limited to a maximum of three payments. Each payment will be equal to 4% of the benefit amount. 

A retrenchment claim will not reduce the benefit amount on this benefit or any other benefit on the policy. 

Any outstanding debt will be deducted from the claim amount. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 5 

Retrenchment benefit payments _________________________________________________________________ 

Momentum will make a lump sum payment after every three months of continuous unemployment as the result of the insured life being retrenched (up to the policy anniversary before the insured life’s 65th birthday), limited to a maximum of three payments. Each payment will be equal to 4% of the benefit amount. 

This means that the retrenchment benefit payments will be made as follows (per retrenchment claim): 

- 4% of the benefit amount as a lump sum after 3 months of continuous unemployment; plus 

- 4% of the benefit amount as a lump sum after 6 months of continuous unemployment; plus 

- 4% of the benefit amount as a lump sum after 9 months of continuous unemployment 

The retrenchment benefit payments will end if: 

- The insured life finds new employment before the next payment is due. 

- The insured life stop providing proof of unemployment on a quarterly basis (through registration as an unemployed individual with the unemployment insurance fund). 

- The Homeloan Protector benefit ends 

- The final payment under the Retrenchment category has been made 

Waiting period (occupational disability)___________________________________________________________________________ 

There is no explicit waiting period. 

A claim will only be admitted once we have established the permanency of the disability according to our definition. 

No claim will be admitted if the insured life dies before permanency is established. 

Waiting period (retrenchment) ___________________________________________________________________________________ 

The lump sum claim amount under retrenchment will only be paid after the insured life has been continuously unemployed for at least three months. 

No-claim period (retrenchment) __________________________________________________________________________________ 

No claim will be paid if a claim arises from retrenchment or notification of retrenchment within three months from the starting date of the benefit. 

When restarting the benefit, a new three-month period will apply. 

Any outstanding debt will be deducted from the claim amount. 

Critical Illness Cover for Children _________________________________________________________________________________ 

Only children who are permanent residents of the Republic of South Africa qualify. 

All the insured life's biological or legally adopted children from their first to their 18th birthday (19 next birthday) qualify for the Critical Illness Cover for Children. 

Momentum will not admit a claim under the critical illness benefit if any condition that existed prior to the child becoming eligible for this benefit directly or indirectly brought about or accelerated the claim event. This includes all symptoms experienced by the child that could have disclosed the illness or condition prior to eligibility. 

If both parents own a critical illness benefit, the child will qualify for a claim under both these benefits. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 6 

The child critical illness benefit will not apply within the first twelve months following the birth or adoption of a child. 

The benefit amount under the Critical Illness Cover for Children is the lesser of: 

- 10% of the insured life's benefit amount at the time of a claim and 

- R125 000. 

Only one claim per category will be paid. 

A related claim is a claim where the claim event progressed from a previous claim event. We will treat a claim that is related to any previous claim in a different category, as if it is in the same category as the claim it progressed from. 

A claim under the Critical Illness Cover for Children will not reduce the benefit amount on this benefit or any other benefit on the policy. 

End of benefit ____________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

This benefit ends on the earliest of: 

- The death of the insured life. 

- The end of the benefit term. 

- The payment of the full benefit amount. 

- The cancellation of the policy or benefit as a result of: 

   - any event covered in the policy contract 

   - notification from the policyholder. 

Claim requirements ______________________________________________________________________________________________ 

Refer to the Claim requirements section of this technical guide for information on the documents required to assess a claim under this benefit.

###### **If attached to a stand-alone disability benefit:** 

The insured life must qualify for payment of the full benefit amount under the stand alone disability benefit to which this ancillary is attached. 

For the conditions listed below, the insured life must satisfy the requirements for a 100% functional impairment claim event under the disability benefit to which this ancillary benefit is attached. 

**If attached to a Death Benefit** (with ancillary disability benefit) **:** 

The insured life must qualify for payment of the full benefit amount under the ancillary disability benefit that is also attached to the death benefit. 

For the conditions listed below, the insured life must satisfy the requirements for a 100% functional impairment claim event under the disability benefit that is also attached to the Death Benefit. 

###### **Conditions** 

- Conditions of the spinal column: Any disorder or condition of the spinal column (ranging from the neck to the coccyx. 

- Mental disorders: Any mental health disorder defined by the current version of the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders or equivalent diagnostic tool. 

- Chronic Fatigue Syndrome or similar conditions: Similar conditions include (but are not limited to) encephalomyalgia, chronic fatigue immune dysfunction syndrome (CFIDS), myalgic encephalitis, postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS), chronic tiredness, yuppie flu and fibromyalgia.

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 3 

Claim amount ____________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

Momentum will pay 10% of the benefit amount paid under: 

- the stand-alone disability benefit to which this ancillary is attached or 

- the ancillary disability benefit attached to a Death Benefit. 

###### **General** 

Payments will be made every five years. The first payment will be five years after the insured life has met the defined requirements. 

Payments will increase by the general increase in the South African consumer price index (CPI), capped at 15% per year, between the date of the disability claim payment and the date of longevity payment. 

Claim payments will not reduce the life cover amount. 

Once a claim is admitted, the policyholder will no longer have to pay the premium for the benefit and will not be allowed to make another claim under this benefit. 

Waiting period ___________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

Not applicable 

Longevity Enhancer ______________________________________________________________________________________________ 

Momentum will pay a lump sum when the insured life reaches age 80. This payment will equal 20% of the final benefit amount under the disability benefit to which this ancillary is linked. 

This payment will be made if: 

- The insured life never submits a claim under the disability benefit to which this ancillary is linked. 

- The disability benefit is converted to the maximum Functional Protector or Complete Functional Protector benefit amount allowed under the conversion option. 

- The disability benefit must be converted to a Functional Protector or Complete Functional Protector before the end of the grace period. 

- If the disability benefit is converted to a lesser amount, the payment is reduced proportionately. Functional Protector or Complete Functional Protector benefits taken out before the conversion date will be considered when determining whether the insured life has converted to the maximum Functional Protector or Complete Functional Protector benefit amount. _Refer to the relevant disability benefit to which this ancillary is linked for more information on the conversion option._ 

- The insured life never submits a claim under the Functional Protector or Complete Functional Protector. 

- The Functional Protector or Complete Functional Protector is kept in force until the insured life reaches age 80. The payment will be reduced proportionately if the Functional Protector benefit amount is reduced after the conversion. If the Functional Protector or Complete Functional Protector is cancelled before the insured life reaches age 80 no payment will be made. 

**Grace period:** The grace period will end six months after the end of the benefit term of the disability benefit to which this ancillary is linked.

This benefit allows the policyholder to purchase a Death Benefit, Comprehensive Disability Benefit, Own Occupation Disability Benefit, Comprehensive ADW Disability Benefit, Functional Impairment Benefit or ADW Disability Benefit (provided the insured life qualifies for the chosen benefit). 

If the policyholder exercises an option under an ancillary benefit, this amount will not count towards the total future cover amount exercised. 

The policyholder may not exercise any options under this benefit to purchase additional disability or impairment cover if a disability or impairment claim for the insured life has been submitted with Momentum or any other life insurance company. 

The policyholder may exercise this option on any existing stand-alone or ancillary benefit except for benefits where: 

- a premium waiver claim is being paid 

- a claim has been submitted. 

- The benefit amount increases applied and/or benefits issued under this option will be subject to the standard rates and standard terms and conditions applicable to the member's age, occupation, education, smoking status and pursuits at the time.

- suffers a disability caused by a bodily injury or illness to such an extent that they are totally and permanently unable to perform the normal duties of their own occupation (up to the policy anniversary before the insured life's 65th birthday) 

   - OR 

- meets the requirements of one of the defined functional impairment claim events with a 100% payout.

- Functional impairment 

###### **Occupational disability** 

Occupational disability is a disability  caused by a bodily injury or illness to such an extent that the insured life is totally and permanently unable to perform the normal duties of their own occupation. 

The insured life will not qualify for a claim under the occupational disability criteria if the insured life is not gainfully employed at the time of the claim event occurring. Such a claim will be assessed against the impairment and illness criteria. 

Momentum will not pay a claim if the insured life is not receiving or is refusing the medical treatment they could reasonably be expected to undergo according to current best practice medical protocols and which could substantially improve or remove the condition being claimed for. 

###### **Functional impairment** 

The claim events are not linked to the insured life's ability to perform occupational activities. 

The claim event is based on a medical impairment that occurs after the start date of the benefit as diagnosed by an appropriate specialist (registered with the Health Professions Council of South Africa (HPCSA) and resulting in the specified functional restrictions defined below. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 3 

The insured life must undergo reasonable optimal treatment and their functional impairment will be determined after they have reached (reasonable) Maximal Medical Improvement (MMI). At this stage a specialist approved by Momentum must declare the functional impairment total, permanent and continuous for the foreseeable future. 

The insured life will not be required to undergo reasonable optimal treatment if a specialist, that Momentum has approved, has established that the functional impairment is permanent, and that further treatment will not lessen the severity of the condition. 

- Reasonable optimal treatment: This is the treatment that Momentum may reasonably expect the insured life to undergo according to the guidelines for the specific condition under the generally accepted medical practice at claim stage. The insured life is expected to comply with their treatment routine. 

- Maximal Medical Improvement (MMI): A condition or state that is well stabilised and unlikely to change substantially in the next year with or without medical treatment. There may be some change over time, but further recovery is not expected.  A panel of accredited medical specialists will determine how many Activities of Daily Living (ADL) the insured life can perform. 

Momentum will not pay a claim if the insured life is not receiving or is refusing the medical treatment they could reasonably be expected to undergo according to current best practice medical protocols and which could substantially improve or remove the condition being claimed for. 

A panel of accredited medical specialists will determine how many Activities of Daily Living (ADL) the insured life can perform. 

A claim will be admitted only if the claim event is a permanent condition. 

Refer to Appendix 1 in the technical guide for the functional impairment claim events.

- Claim event ______________________________________________________________________________________________________ Retrenchment is the termination of employment by the insured life's employer due to "operational requirements". Operational requirements in this context mean requirements based on the economic, technological, structural or similar needs of an employer. Termination of employment for the following reasons shall not be considered retrenchment: • Retirement (early, normal or ill-health) • Resignation or voluntary retrenchment • Dismissal • A fixed-term employment contract coming to an end • Nervous breakdown, stress, burnout, disability or illness. 

   - (The specific examples above should not be regarded as the only possible 

   - reason for termination of employment which would not be considered retrenchment) 

Momentum will only admit a claim for this benefit if the insured life has been continuously employed in a permanent full-time job for at least two years, of which at least one year must have been with his current employer. 

A claim under the Premium Waiver - Retrenchment benefit will have no impact on the other premium waiver benefits. 

Momentum will admit a retrenchment claim from the official date of retrenchment or the date on which the insured life received their last salary-payment, whichever date occurs last.  The first payment will only be made after the waiting period has expired.

The premium that will be waived will cover any premium increases, but the increases will be limited to the minimum of the general increase in the CPI and 15% per annum. The premium increases will never be less than the chosen percentage for the Compulsory premium pattern. 

Payment period __________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

Premiums will be waived for 12 months regardless of whether the insured life returns to gainful employment or not.

Momentum will waive the premium only after the insured life under the premium waiver has been retrenched for one month.

A new six-month period will apply when: 

- restarting a benefit 

- making an ad-hoc increase to the premium of the stand-alone benefit to which the premium waiver is attached. The new six-month period will only apply to the ad-hoc increase portion.

- Competitive premium rates 

- Special benefit limits on selected benefits 

- Use of Gross Professional Income (GPI) as a definition of income. 

Definition of a professional _______________________________________________________________________________________ 

The following occupations/professions are allowed, subject to membership of the applicable statutory professional organisation and a qualification equivalent to at least a 4-year university degree: 

- Doctor registered with the Health Professional Council of South Africa. 

- Dentist registered with the Health Professional Council of South Africa. 

- Psychologist registered with the Health Professional Council of South Africa. 

- Pharmacist registered with the South African Pharmacy Council. 

- Attorney, advocate or judge registered with the Law Society of South Africa or any societies for advocates. 

- Chartered accountant or auditor registered with the Public Accountants and Auditors Board. 

- Actuary registered with any global statutory actuarial societies (eg Institute of Actuaries/Faculty of Actuaries/Society of Actuaries). 

- Certified Financial Planner (CFP) registered with the Financial Planning Institute. 

- Architect registered with the South African Council for Architectural profession. 

- Engineer registered as a professional engineer with the Engineering Council of South Africa. 

- Veterinarian registered with the South African Veterinary Council. 

- Optometrist registered with the Health Professional Council of South Africa. 

- Physiotherapist registered with the Health Professional Council of South Africa 

- Marine Biologist registered with the South African Association for Marine Biological Research (SAAMBR). 

- Occupational Therapist registered with the Health Professional Council of South Africa 

- Chiropractor registered with the Health Professional Council of South Africa. 

- Biomedical Engineer registered as a professional engineer with the Engineering Council of South Africa. 

- Construction Engineer registered as a professional engineer with the Engineering Council of South Africa. 

The insured life must be practising one of the above occupations to qualify as a professional. 

The insured life may be in private practice or employed. 

Momentum may review this list from time to time. 

Definition of a professional student ______________________________________________________________________________ 

The insured life must be a full-time or part-time student that is expected to qualify for any of the abovementioned occupations/professions within 12 months. 

Professional students will be rated as professionals.

Conversion Option _______________________________________________________________________________________________ 

###### **Conversion Option for Functional Impairment Benefit** 

The student has the option to convert this benefit to: 

- Comprehensive Disability Benefit, or 

- Own Occupation Disability Benefit, or 

- Complete Income Protector, or 

- Temporary Income Protector 

- (subject to the normal qualification criteria) without proof of insurability or health (except for a negative HIV test result). 

The Conversion Option may only be exercised within three months after the start date of the student's first full-time employment in his chosen field of study. 

If this benefit is converted to a Comprehensive Disability Benefit or Own Occupation Disability Benefit, a benefit amount of up to R2 000 000, subject to financial underwriting, can be purchased. 

If this benefit is converted to a Complete Income Protector or Temporary Income Protector: 

- The total benefit amount under the Complete Income Protector or Temporary Income Protector issued under this Conversion Option may never be more than the lesser of: 

   - R20 000 per month and 

   - 75% of the student's net income at the time of the increase. 

- The following increase options are available: 

   - the benefit amount may be increased by up to 100% within three months after the first anniversary of the student's first full-time employment in his chosen field of study 

   - the benefit amount may be increased by the same amount as on the first anniversary within three months after the second anniversary of the student's first full-time employment in his chosen field of study. 

- If the Functional Impairment Benefit is an ancillary benefit: 

   - The student has the option to convert this benefit to the ancillary Comprehensive Disability Benefit or Own Occupation Disability Benefit (subject to the normal qualification criteria) without proof of insurability or health (except for a negative HIV test result). 

   - This Conversion Option can only be exercised within three months after the start date of first full-time employment in his chosen field of study. 

###### **General rules** 

This Conversion Option is only available to students that were accepted at standard rates and without any exclusion. 

Written notice of the student's intention to exercise this Conversion Option must be received by Momentum within three months after the start date of the first full-time employment in his chosen field of study. 

If a disability or impairment claim has been submitted for the student with Momentum or any other life insurance company, the student may not exercise any of the options under this benefit. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 5 

Only claims in respect of events that happened after the conversion/ increase date will be admitted under the benefit and/or any increase in benefit amount issued under this Conversion Option. 

The benefit and/or any increase in benefit amount issued under this option will be subject to the standard rates and standard terms and conditions applicable to the student's age, occupation, education, smoking status and pursuits at the time. 

The benefit and/or any increase in benefit amount issued under this option will be subject to financial underwriting. 

A seven-day or 14-day waiting period under the Complete Income Protector or Temporary Income Protector may only be selected if, at the time of the conversion, the student has not suffered from or does not suffer from any disease, disorder or impairment that requires frequent hospitalisation or treatment, time off work, confinement to a bed/home, including (but not limited to) for example bronchitis, gout, depression, back pain, migraine and asthma. 

Only claims in respect of events that happened after the conversion/ increase date will be admitted under the benefit and/or any increase in benefit amount issued under this Conversion Option. 

###### **Conversion Option for Functional Protector or Complete Functional Protector** 

The student has the option to: 

- convert this benefit to the Complete Income Protector or Temporary Income Protector with a benefit amount of up to 3 times the benefit amount under this benefit, or 

- purchase the Complete Income Protector or Temporary Income Protector in addition to this benefit with a benefit amount of up two times the benefit amount under this benefit (subject to the normal qualification criteria) without giving Momentum proof of insurability or health (except for a negative HIV test result). The Conversion Option may only be exercised within three months after the start date of the student's first full-time employment in his chosen field of study. 

- If the student does not exercise the full benefit amount that is available on the conversion date, the balance may be applied as follows: 

   - the benefit amount under the Complete Income Protector or Temporary Income Protector may be increased by up to 100% within three months after the first anniversary of first full-time employment in his chosen field of study 

   - − the benefit amount under the Complete Income Protector or Temporary Income Protector may again be increased by the same amount as on the first anniversary within three months after the second anniversary of first full-time employment in his chosen field of study. 

- The total benefit amount under the Complete Income Protector or Temporary Income Protector may never be more than the lesser of: 

   - the benefit amount that was available to the student on the conversion date and 

   - R20 000 per month and 

   - 75% of the student's net income at the time of the increase. 

###### **General rules** 

This Conversion Option is only available to students that were accepted at standard rates and without any exclusions.

#### Appendix 1 - Functional impairment claim events 

The claim amount is dependent on the severity of the permanent impairment: 

- Claims criteria for impairment benefits 

- The impairment must be moderate or severe (based on the specific definitions). 

- • The impairment must be permanent. 

- No loss of income is required. 

- The claim events are not in any way linked to the insured life's ability to perform occupational activities. 

- Impairments include medical and physical impairment definitions, and Activities of Daily Living criteria (ADL). 

25%, 50%, 75% and 100% benefit amount payouts: __________________________________________________ 

The tiered approach covers both severe and moderate impairments. The severity of the permanent impairment determines the level of claim payable. 

- Functional Impairment 

- Comprehensive ADW Disability Benefit 

- Comprehensive Disability Benefit 

- Complete Income Protector** 

- Temporary Income Protector 

- Business Overheads Protector 

- Business Protector (Self Employed) 

- Business Protector (Professional) 

- Group Income Top-up Benefit 

- Temporary Group Income Top-up Benefit 

- Complete Functional Protector* 

- Comprehensive Living Benefit 

Note: The policyholder may not claim under the benefit after the policy anniversary immediately preceding the insured life’s chosen benefit term. 

100% benefit amount payout ____________________________________________________________________ 

The full benefit (100% of the benefit amount) is paid in the event of a severe impairment. 

- Own Occupation Disability Benefit 

- ADW Disability Benefit 

- Education Protector - Death and Disability 

- Education Protector - Death and Impairment 

- Premium Waiver - Comprehensive Disability 

- Premium Waiver - Functional Impairment 

- Functional Protector* 

- Homeloan Protector 

Complete Functional Protector and Functional Protector* _____________________________________________ 

The following claim events excluded for Complete Functional Protector and Functional Protector: 

- Hearing 

- Speech 

- Facial disorders and/or disfigurement 

- Cranial nerve VII (facial nerve) 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Complete Income Protector (Whole life) ** ________________________________________________________ 

The insured life will not be able to submit a claim for any of the 25% functional impairment events if that event occurs after the benefit anniversary immediately preceding the insured life's 70th birthday. 

If the insured life met the requirements for a 25% functional impairment severity before the stipulated benefit anniversary (other than for Hearing) and received a payout or a series of payouts and after undergoing a reassessment at age 70 still qualifies for a payout, the payment will continue until death. 

All claim events in the following categories will not qualify for a claim payment after the stipulated benefit anniversary, even in instances where the insured life qualified for a claim before the benefit anniversary (preceding the insured life's 70th birthday): 

- Hearing 

- Speech 

- Facial disorders and/or disfigurement 

- Cranial nerve VII (facial nerve) 

- Peripheral venous disease 

Refer to the benefit section for details on the claim event payments for Complete Income Protector (Whole Life)

- Visual impairment: refer to visual parameters.

#### Activities of Daily Living 

- The Activities of Daily Living Scale works on a points system.  Only one item in each of the seven categories may be checked before the total score is calculated. 

- The level of benefit that we pay depends on the score achieved: 

|Percentage of benefit|Score|
|---|---|
|50%|Score of 4 or more|
|100%|Score of 6 or more.|



- The insured life must be totally and continually unable to perform the specified Activity of Daily Living, with no possibility of improvement in the future (i.e. Maximum Medical Improvement must have been reached). Suitable treatment and/or rehabilitation options must be followed before the benefit is paid. 

- The scales are used to assess the insured life's current ability to perform the following activities, with the use of the appropriate assistive aids and appliances where necessary. Where an assistive device is available but the insured life's chooses not to make use of it, the criteria will be assessed based on the ability to perform the task with the use of the assistive device. Note that one and only one criterion may be selected in each category.

###### Cancer 

- Cancer develops when cells in the body begin to grow out of control. Normal cells grow, divide, and die. Instead of dying, cancer cells continue to grow and form new abnormal cells. Cancer cells often travel to other body parts where they grow and replace normal tissue. The diagnosis must be confirmed with histology and supported by appropriate specialist reports with disease staging and relevant oncology treatment. All in -situ cancers (that are specifically listed) must be supported by the appropriate histological and imaging (i.e. CT and/or MRI) findings All Grade I brain tumours (WHO classification) will be considered under the benign brain ✓ ✓ ✓ 

- tumour category. Histological confirmation is required for Brain tumours (WHO grade II to IV) and there is no requirement to undergo treatment for these. The following are specifically excluded, unless defined as a claim event: • all skin cancers, (except invasive malignant melanoma's and lentigo melanoma's that have progressed to at least TNM classification of T1aN0M0). 

- • all conditions which are histologically described as pre-malignant or cancer in situ unless specifically listed as a claim event. 

- Early cancer • Histological confirmation of a malignant tumour which is characterised by the growth of malignant cells without the invasion of surrounding tissue. The tumour must be classified as tumour in situ (Tis) according to the TNM classification system unless otherwise specified. The diagnosis must be confirmed with histology and supported by appropriate specialist reports with/and relevant oncology treatment. The claim event qualify for a 15% payout of the benefit amount to a maximum of R100 000. 

- • Carcinoma in situ of one or both ovaries for which an oophorectomy has been performed. 

- • Carcinoma in situ of the larynx for which a total laryngectomy has been performed. 

- • Carcinoma in situ of the stomach defined as intraepithelial tumour without invasion of the lamina propria for which a partial or total gastrectomy has been performed. 

- • Carcinoma in situ of the vagina or vulva for which a hysterectomy has been performed or for which other surgery defined as a skin flap or skin graft has been performed. 

- • A neuroendocrine tumour of low malignant potential for which surgery has been ✓ performed. 

- • Carcinoma in situ of the oesophagus for which surgery to remove the tumour has been performed. This excludes treatment by any other method and also any treatment for Barrett’s oesophagus. 

- • Carcinoma in situ of the urinary bladder as confirmed histologically. This excludes noninvasive papillary carcinoma and Stage Ta bladder. 

- • Lobular carcinoma in situ or ductal carcinoma in situ of the breast resulting in chemotherapy, lumpectomy or breast conserving. 

- • Carcinoma in situ of the cervix uteri or cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3 (CIN 3) for which a hysterectomy has been performed.  This excludes all other forms of treatment including trachelectomy (removal of the cervix), loop excision, laser surgery, conisation and cryosurgery.

###### Cardiac and arterial system 

The cardiac and arterial system combined is known as the cardiovascular system. The cardiovascular system circulates blood throughout the body, includes the heart, veins, and arteries.  Its main function is to transport oxygen and nutrients to all areas of the body and removes carbon dioxide and other wastes. All cardiac events that occur within 30 days of each other will be considered as a single claim event. The number of payments for coronary artery stenting will be limited to 3 payments. 

###### **Heart attack** 

Myocardial infarction (MI) / heart attack is the irreversible death of heart muscle secondary to prolonged ischemia. This usually results from an imbalance between oxygen supply and demand. The appearance of raised cardiac enzymes in the circulation generally indicates death of heart muscle. Acute myocardial infarction (MI) refers to the spectrum of clinical presentations ranging from ST-segment elevation heart attacks (STEMI) to non–ST-segment elevation heart attacks (NSTEMI). 

A full cardiologist's or cardiac specialist's report confirming that the signs and symptoms equate to the diagnosis; with raised cardiac enzymes and relevant ECG findings should be compatible with diagnosis of myocardial infarction. The evidence must show a definite acute myocardial infarction.  Other acute coronary syndromes, including but not limited to angina, are not covered by this definition. 

###### **Level D: Mild heart attack of specified severity** 

Evidence by no ECG changes and the following criteria: 

1. Compatible clinical symptoms 

2. Raised cardiac biomarkers defined as any one of the following Troponin or Non-Troponin Markers: 

   - Trop T > 0.5 ng/ml (500ng/L) < 1.0ng/ml (1000 ng/L) or 

   - Trop I > 0.25ng/ml (250 ng/L) < 0.5 ng/ml (500ng/L), or 

   - Raised CK-MB mass (defined below), or 

      - above the upper limit of normal laboratory reference range but below 2 times the upper limit of normal laboratory reference range in acute presentation phase 

      - Raised above the upper limit of normal laboratory reference range but below 4 times the upper limit of normal laboratory reference range post intervention 

   - Total CPK elevation (defined below) 

      - Raised above the upper limit of normal laboratory reference range but below 2 times the upper limit of normal laboratory reference range in acute presentation <u>phase, with at least 6% being CK-MB</u>

###### **Level C: Moderate heart attack of specified severity** 

This is defined as the death of heart muscle, due to inadequate blood supply, as evidenced by any of the following combinations of criteria: 

- Compatible clinical symptoms AND raised cardiac biomarkers 

- OR 

- Compatible clinical symptoms AND new pathological Q-waves on ECG as defined in the ASISA definitions. 

- New pathological Q-waves on ECG as defined in Annexure A (b) AND raised cardiac biomarkers 

- ST-segment and T-wave changes on ECG indicative of myocardial injury as defined in the ASISA definitions AND raised cardiac biomarkers 

Where raised cardiac biomarkers are referenced above, they are defined as any one of the following Troponin or Non-Troponin Markers: 

✓ ✓ ✓ 

- Trop T > 1.0ng/ml (1000 ng/L) or 

- Trop I > 0.5 ng/ml (500ng/L), or 

- Raised CK-MB mass (defined below), or 

   - Raised 2 times or more above the upper limit of normal laboratory reference range in acute presentation phase 

   - Raised 4 times or more above the upper limit of normal laboratory reference range post intervention 

- Total CPK elevation (defined below) 

   - Raised 2 times or more the upper limit of normal laboratory reference range in acute presentation phase, with at least 6% being CK-MB 

Please refer to the ASISA claim event definitions (at the end of the critical illness definitions) for details on reference ranges, including Sensitive Troponin Markers)

###### Gastrointestinal system 

This system includes the liver, biliary system, pancreas and gastrointestinal tract from the oesophagus to the stomach through to the rectum.  Diseases or interventions must be related to primary organic pathology of the gastrointestinal system, must not be related to drug or alcohol abuse and be diagnosed by an appropriate consultant specialist supported by objective and relevant investigations including blood tests, X-rays, scans and scopes as necessary.

###### **Inflammatory bowel disease** 

- Crohn's disease 

   - Crohn's disease is a chronic granulomatous inflammatory disease. The disease must result in complications, must be unresponsive to medical therapy and require surgical intervention. The characteristic colonoscopy and histopathalogical features must be present to confirm the diagnosis. 

- Ulcerative colitis 

   - For the purposes of this policy, ulcerative colitis shall be covered when the disease results in complications and is not responsive to medical therapy and requires surgical intervention. Diagnosis for this policy must be based on colonoscopy and histopathalogical features.

###### HIV/Aids 

Infection by any Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) or being diagnosed as having Acquired Immuno-deficiency Syndrome (Aids), if the insured life can prove to the satisfaction of Momentum that the infection is due to: 

- The transfusion of infected blood or blood products from a South African blood transfusion service that Momentum recognises, after the starting date of this policy, or 

- Executing his professional duties as a medical or dental practitioner registered with the Health Professions Council of South Africa (HPCSA) or a nurse registered with the SA Nursing Council, or 

- Receiving a transplanted organ that was previously infected with HIV, or 

- Any other medical or dental procedure that the HPCSA recognises and that a medical or dental practitioner registered with the HPCSA or a nurse registered with the SA Nursing Council, has performed on the insured life, or 

✓ ✓ 

- Involvement in a road traffic accident, or 

- Involvement in a violent crime, or 

- Involvement in a rape or an indecent assault crime 

Momentum will consider a claim if the following requirements were followed: 

- Where the HIV is a result of the transfusion of blood or blood products or a transplanted organ, the transfusion or organ donor service must accept liability for the incident. 

- In the event of an accident, violent crime, rape, indecent assault or infection in the execution of professional duties: 

   - An identified HIV test needs to be performed within 24 hours to confirm an HIVnegative status before the event. 

   - Proof that the insured life has started the prescribed treatment, a course of antiretroviral drugs, and that the treatment course has been completed in full. 

- In the event of an accident, violent crime, rape or indecent assault: 

   - The event must have been reported to the SAPS and a case number issued and/or criminal case opened. 

   - A medical examination of the victim needs to have been performed directly after the event. 

   - Medically documented proof of acute trauma and HIV infection suspicion must have been submitted. 

- Where the accidental HIV is a result of emergency assistance at the scene of a road traffic accident or violent crime, an SAPS or eyewitness affidavit to prove assistance must have been submitted. 

- Momentum must receive notification within 14 days of the occurrence of an event, where there is suspicion of HIV infection. 

- An identified HIV test needs to be performed within 6 months of the event to confirm an HIV positive status.  If there was no suspicion of HIV infection and it can be proven that the insured life contracted HIV as a result of transfusion of infected blood or blood products or receiving a transplanted organ, Momentum must receive notification within 6 months of the insured life being tested positive for HIV.

###### **Aids** 

The following must support the clinical manifestation of aids (the Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome): 

- the results of a positive HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus) antibody test or other recognised test for the presence of aids (provided that, in all cases, Momentum accepts the type of test), 

- the insured life must have a CD4 cell count of less than 200 

- and one of the following criteria must be met: 

   - the existence of at least three conditions of stage 3 according to the current WHO Clinical Classification System 

      - OR 

   - the diagnosis of at least one of the aids-defining diseases according to the current WHO Clinical Classification System.

###### Musculoskeletal system 

Confined to diseases, disorders or interventions of muscle, bone, joints and any directly associated nerve supply. An orthopaedic or neurosurgeon must make the diagnosis and diagnostic X-rays and CT or MRI scans must support it. 

###### **Diplegia** 

The total and permanent loss of function of both sides of the body, due to an injury or a disease of the spinal cord that affects the legs more than the arms as a neurologist/neurosurgeon confirmed. 

###### **Hemiplegia** 

The total and permanent loss of function of only one side of the body due to brain injury or disease as a neurologist/neurosurgeon confirmed. 

✓ ✓ ✓ 

###### **Paraplegia** 

The total and permanent loss of function of both legs due to injury or disease of the spinal cord as a neurologist/neurosurgeon confirmed. 

###### **Quadriplegia** 

The total and permanent loss of function of both upper and both lower limbs due to injury or disease of the spinal cord as a neurologist/neurosurgeon confirmed.

###### Nervous system 

The nervous system comprises the central and peripheral nervous systems. The central nervous system includes the brain, brainstem and spinal cord. The peripheral nervous system contains the body’s other nerves. Made of billions of interconnected nerve cells. the nervous system is a vast communication network linking all body parts and allowing us to interact with our environment. Only central nervous system conditions as defined are covered. A neurologist or neurosurgeon must confirm the diagnosis or intervention and the deficit must be of a permanent nature and objective investigations including blood tests, X-rays and CT or MRIscans must support it. 

The clinical symptoms and signs must be compatible with the diagnosis and any neurological deficit must be anatomically compatible with the primary lesion. 

###### **Stroke** 

Death of brain tissue due to inadequate blood supply or haemorrhage within the brain tissue resulting in neurological deficit. A neurologist must confirm the diagnosis and objective neuroimaging investigations including CT or MRI-scans must support it. Any deficit must be of a permanent nature. The clinical symptoms and signs must be compatible with the diagnosis and any neurological deficit must be anatomically compatible with the primary lesion. Severity levels will be assessed by a full neurological examination by a specialist neurologist or neuropsychologist after 3 months. The neurological domains to be assessed include motor, speech, visual, sensory, language and cognition. 

WPI figures are calculated as per the American Medical Association Guides to the Evaluation of Permanent Impairment 6th edition. Where we make reference to ADLs it is specifically the ASISA Stroke ADL list as below: 

✓ ✓ ✓ 

###### **Basic activities of Daily Living** 

- Bathing – the ability to was/bathe oneself independently 

- Transferring – the ability to move oneself from a bed to a chair or from a bed to a toilet independently 

- Dressing – the ability to take off and put on ones clothes independently 

- Eating - the ability to feed oneself independently. This does not include the making of food 

- Toileting – the ability to use a toilet and cleanse oneself thereafter, independently 

- Locomotion on a level surface – the ability to walk on a flat surface, independently 

- • Locomotion on an incline – the ability to walk up a gentle slope, or a flight of steps independently. 

###### **Advanced activities of Daily Living** 

- Driving a car – the ability to open a car door, change gears or use a steering wheel 

- Medical care: the ability to prepare and take the correct medication 

- Money management – the ability to do one’s own banking and to make rational financial decisions 

- Communicative activities: - the ability to communicate either verbally or written 

- Shopping: - the ability to choose and lift groceries from shelves as well as carry them in bags 

- Food preparation – the ability to prepare food for cooking as well as using kitchen utensils 

- Housework – the ability to clean a house or iron clothing

- Community ambulation with or without assistive device, but not requiring a mobility device – the ability to walk around in public places using only a walking stick if necessary 

- Moderate activities:-activities like moving a table, pushing a vacuum cleaner, bowling, golf 

- • Vigorous activities: - able to partake in running, heavy lifting, sports 

###### **For above definition, the following are not covered:** 

1. Transient ischaemic attack/reversible ischaemic neurological deficit (as defined below) 

   - A Transient Ischaemic Attack (TIA) occurs when the blood supply is momentarily interrupted, but restored before any permanent damage can occur. It usually results in one of more of the following symptoms: 

   - a loss of sensation 

   - dizziness 

   - lameness of a limb 

   - loss of speech 

   - The symptoms only occur for a few minutes to hours and recovery is quick and spontaneous with no evidence of infarction or haemorrhaging that exists on objective neuro-imaging investigations including CT or MRI-scans. 

2. Vascular disease affecting the eye or optic nerve. 

3. Cerebral symptoms due to migraine.

###### **Pulmonary function test** 

Pulmonary function test measure how well the lungs take in and exhale air and how efficiently they transfer oxygen into the blood. Spirometry measures how well the lungs exhale. The information gathered during this test is useful in diagnosing certain types of lung disorders, but is most useful when assessing for obstructive lung diseases (especially asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, COPD).
