###### Catch-all 

Any disease, where the severity of the disease that has resulted in a Whole Person Impairment (WPI) > 35% and the percentage is dependent on the system or systems that are affected. It will be assessed according to the criteria stipulated in AMA Guidelines 6th Edition. Any Whole Person Impairment as a result of traumatic injury or mental and behavioural disorders will not be covered by this category. WPI scores are determined when the condition is ✓ ✓ ✓ permanent at optimal treatment. A payment will only be made under this category if the condition suffered from does not qualify for a claim payment under any of the other categories listed above. Endocrine and metabolic diseases Diagnosis or disease process resulting in permanent dysfunction of the thyroid, pituitary, pancreas or adrenal glands where such function cannot be medically controlled.  The diagnosis ✓ must be confirmed by an appropriate consultant specialist and supported by relevant blood or other diagnostic tests as appropriate to the condition. 

###### Additional claim events for children 

The Critical Illness Cover for Children (child benefit) benefit amount is 10% of the critical illness ✓ benefit amount for the parent. 



Breadth of Cover Guarantee<sup>TM</sup> 

Momentum guarantees that the policyholder will receive a payout if: 

- the claim event does not meet the requirements for a claim payout under the critical illness benefit  but does meet the requirements for a claim payout under a competitor's qualifying critical illness benefit. 

The percentage payout will be the lesser of: 

- the percentage payout under the competitors' qualifying critical illness benefit; and 

- • 20% 

The claim amount  is calculated as the percentage payout multiplied by the benefit amount. The insured life does not need to have a critical illness benefit in force with any competitor to ✓ qualify for this benefit; the qualifying benefit need only be available in the market from the competitors. 

###### **Qualifying competitor critical illness benefit** 

For a benefit to be classified as a qualifying critical illness benefit, the benefit must: 

- be open to new business in South Africa; and 

- be available on an individual life policy contract; and 

- provide a claim payout for all claim events and severity levels as currently defined by ASISA's SCIDEP; and 

- be underwritten by an ASISA member office 



Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 13 



###### **Exclusions** 

- The following conditions are specifically excluded as they are not considered to be critical illness claim events. This list will be reviewed from time to time: 

   - All mental health disorders including but not limited to major depression and schizophrenia. 

   - Fibromyalgia (or conditions similar thereto) and chronic fatigue syndrome (or conditions similar thereto). 

   - Chronic pain disorders. 

   - Influenza 

- We will not admit a claim under the Breadth of Cover Guarantee<sup>TM</sup> for any condition that existed prior to the start date of this guarantee which directly brought about or accelerated the claim event. This includes: 

   - All symptoms for an illness or condition experienced by the insured life or 

   - Any illness or condition the insured life sought medical advice for or 

   - Any illness or condition that was diagnosed prior to the start of the policy, 

   - Any condition excluded due to a medical exclusion and/or deferment applied on the insured life will not be covered under the Breadth of Cover Guarantee<sup>TM</sup> . 

Any optional features or add-on benefits will not be considered as part of the qualifying critical illness benefit. 

Ex gratia or business decisions on claims from competitors will not be considered. Any and/or all the Exclusions and/or Special Conditions applicable on the Myriad critical illness benefit will also apply to the Breath of Cover Guarantee<sup>TM.</sup> 

###### **Survival period** 

There is no explicit survival period. A  claim will only be admitted if the insured life meets the requirements of the defined claim event, prior to their death. No medical test or examination concluded after the insured life’s death will be considered in evaluating a claim.

#### ASISA standard on disclosures for critical illness products 

Introduction ______________________________________________________________________ 

The FSB and the Competition Commission gave South African life insurers the go-ahead to standardise certain disclosures to consumers of when critical illness products will pay out. This takes the form of a “disclosure grid” underpinned by standard medical definitions to which companies will have to refer when they make the required disclosures and when a claim is assessed. The grid and the definitions were developed by members of the Standardised Critical illness Definitions Project (SCIDEP) committee.

Example _____________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

Mike has a Future Cover – Death with a benefit amount of R5 million. 

- Mike gets married and decides to exercise his Marriage option for 50% of his benefit amount to purchase a new Death Benefit. 

- He is left with a benefit amount of R2 500 000 (R5 million less R2 500 000) for future options. 

- Mike can now exercise any of the above options within 60 days after the event occurs (up to a maximum of R2 500 000) to buy new standalone Death Benefit. 

Mike and his wife welcome a new baby girl and he opts to exercise his option of 25% for a new child dependant within the required 60 days of the birth. 

- The maximum future cover amount for this event is R5 million x 25% = R1 250 000 million. 

- He decides to exercise the full benefit amount of R1 250 000. 

Mike has exercised R3 750 000 of his future cover benefit so far (R2 500 000 + 1 250 000). 

He therefore has R1 250 000 left to be exercised (initial benefit amount of R5 million less R3 750 000 exercised to date). 

Mike purchases a house, and he decides to exercise his option of 100% for Mortgage bond registration within the required 60 days of the registration. 

- The maximum future cover amount for this event is R5 million x 100% = R5 million. 

- However, the total future cover he exercises over all events cannot exceed his initial benefit amount of R5 million and there is only R1 250 000 left to be exercised. 

If Mike opts to take the R1 250 000, his benefit will be cancelled as he has exercised the full initial benefit amount, he chose at new business.

#### Purpose of underwriting 

Description ___________________________________________________________________________________ 

The purpose of underwriting is to correctly assess the risk associated with the life to be insured. Underwriters will use the occupational, avocational, medical and financial information provided to arrive at an appropriate rating. 

###### **Rating a client** 

Every person's lifestyle, occupation, medical and financial circumstances are considered. This enables Momentum to calculate the most appropriate premium for each application. 

All applicants are evaluated for insurance on an individual basis to determine premium rates. 

Momentum's approach is to categorise a client as accurately as possible. 

Clients will not be placed in rate groups. 

Momentum differentiates between males and females and also between smokers and non-smokers. 

It is only possible to calculate a premium through a formal Momentum quotation. 

Individual rating occurs automatically when the insured life's particulars are entered into the quote system. 

###### **Qualifications** 

The following are examples of a 4-year technikon qualification/diploma: 

- T4, T5, T6 or National Higher Diploma (NHD), BTec, Mtec. 

- The following are examples of a 3-year technikon qualification/diploma: 

- T3 or National Diploma (ND), S4. 

Technical College qualifications (NTS or N) are considered as follows for occupational selection: 

- N1 and N2: equivalent to Grade 11 (Std 9) 

- N3 and N5: equivalent to Grade 12 (Std 10) 

- N6: equivalent to National Diploma (ND). 

Grade 12/Standard 10 

- For occupational underwriting Grade 12 (Std 10) is a Senior Certificate or equivalent qualification at a recognised educational institution. 

Definition of income _____________________________________________________________________________________________ 

Gross taxable income 

- Taxable income payable or benefits receivable on account of the insured life's employment or any services rendered by the insured life. 

Cost to company earnings 

- This equals gross taxable income plus the value of the use of a motor vehicle, as well as the employer's contributions to a medical scheme and a pension fund and the cost of any other benefits paid for by the insured's employer. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 3 

Gross professional income (professionals only) 

- For professionals that charge a fee for services, this equals the sum of the professional fee and the net income from trading activities after deducting business overheads expenses. 

Married applicants 

- For married applicants the more favourable combination of income and education of either life will be used. Each life insured will be underwritten individually. 

###### Housewives 

- The income of the spouse will be used to determine a rating classification. 

###### Students 

   - The parent's income will be used to determine a rating classification, subject to a maximum of R10 000. 

- Change in risk factors ____________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The information that the insured life gives Momentum in the application form or in any other documents that he provides in support of his application, forms the basis on which the policy is issued. 

If the insured life's risk factors (e.g. health, occupation, avocation or country of residence) change, Momentum has to be informed before the policy's starting date. 

If the insured life fails to inform Momentum of any of the above, Momentum may: 

- cancel the policy with immediate effect and keep any premiums paid to Momentum as a penalty 

- refuse to pay out any current or future claims 

- apply altered terms and conditions.

#### General underwriting requirements 

HIV testing _______________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

Underwriting at new business stage includes an HIV test. Cover will be declined if the test is positive. 

Guideline for underwriting requirements _________________________________________________________________________ 

Underwriters may call for additional requirements based on medical and other information at their disposal. These additional requirements are based on the following risk factors: 

- The age of the insured life, 

- • Body Mass Index (BMI) 

- • Family history 

- • The insured life’s drinking and smoking habits 

- Any other factors that may influence the risk assessment i.e. occupation, territory, socio-economic etc.

#### Personal insurance 

Family protection ________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The main objective of family protection is to replace the income that will be lost upon the death of the insured life. 

The following broad guidelines may be used to determine the appropriate level of cover: 

|Age|Multiple of gross<br>|annual income<br>|
|---|---|---|
||Married|Unmarried|
|To 25|20|15|
|26 — 50|25|20|
|51 — 59|18|15|
|60 — 65|10|8|



Every application is dealt with on its own merits. 

Security for loans ________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

If application is made for insurance which is to be offered as security for a loan, full particulars of the loan as well as the reason for the loan (for example mortgage bond) must be supplied. 

A letter of confirmation from the bank or financial institution is needed for loan applications to determine the level of cover that may be allowed. 

Estate duty _______________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

Currently estate duty is only payable on that portion of your estate that exceeds the Section 4 (A) abatement of R3.5 million, i.e. the taxable amount. If you had a spouse (as defined in the Estate Duty Act) who predeceased you, your R3.5 million abatement may be increased with the unutilised portion of that spouse’s own R3,5 million abatement, depending on the number of spouses involved. 

When one considers that the estate includes the assets and may also include insurance and group cover, then it is possible that the R3.5 million (plus roll-over, if applicable) threshold may be exceeded. After the total value of the assets have been determined, the next step is to deduct any liabilities such as outstanding debts and taxes. 

Liabilities also include funeral expenses, master's fees and executor's fees, referred to as allowable deductions. Executor's fees are currently 3,5% of the gross value of the assets and VAT may in certain instances be charged on this fee, in which case the executors' fees amount to 4.03% (3.5% + 15% VAT) of the gross estate value. The balance remaining after allowable deductions are taken into account is the net asset value of the estate. The allowable R3.5 million (plus roll-over, if applicable) rebate is deducted from this amount. 

The residue is taxed at a fixed rate of 20%. When insurance is required to provide for estate duty, the estimated estate duty calculation must accompany the application. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 19 

#### Business insurance 

Key person insurance ____________________________________________________________________________________________ 

In most businesses, there are usually one or two individuals who are considered to be key persons by virtue of their training, experience, marketing ability, etc. 

In the event of their early death or disability, the company would be put in a rather difficult situation to replace such individuals from both a financial and a convenience point of view. 

Please provide full details and motivation for the cover amount requested and reasons for key person insurance. 

uy-and-Sell insurance ___________________________________________________________________________________________ 

An insurable interest exists between partners when the partnership agreement stipulates that the surviving partners are obligated to purchase the deceased partner's share in the partnership. 

The method by which the partnership has been valued and a copy of the partnership agreement are required. 

Momentum has the right to request financial statements if the amount of cover appears to be excessive. 

Contingent liability insurance _____________________________________________________________________________________ 

The requirements for business loans are similar to the requirements for personal loans. The type of policy, policy terms and insured amount should correspond as much as possible with the particulars of the loans. (Refer to Personal Insurance, Security for Loans section.) 

Unnatural Death Benefits are not available on Business Insurance. 

Insolvent estates _________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

According to law, an insolvent has no contractual capacity and may, therefore, not enter into an insurance contract without the permission of the trustee of the insolvent estate. 

Momentum realises that an insolvent also requires life cover for his family in the event of his death and are prepared to underwrite him, subject to individual consideration, limited life cover, and the trustee's consent. 

The trustees of the insolvent estate are required to fill in the necessary section on the Insolvency Questionnaire, thus giving their approval to the insolvent entering into such a contract. The Insolvency Questionnaire must accompany the application form. 

Automatic rehabilitation occurs after 10 years of final date of sequestration and no Insolvency Questionnaire will then be required.

Description ______________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

Momentum's quotation system will determine occupational classes and certain loadings. 

To ensure that a client is rated accurately and fairly, it is important to choose the occupation that best describes the occupational duties of the client. If, for example, the client is the Managing Director and the Accountant of the business, the occupation should be captured as Accountant and not Managing Director. 

Where necessary, the underwriters may request an Occupational Questionnaire. 

All occupations are subject to underwriting.

Diving _______________________________________________________________________________________ 

A fully completed questionnaire is required. 

The diving loadings are divided into four sections: 

- recreational scuba diving 

- technical scuba diving 

- commercial diving 

- additional loadings for divers, depending on the type of risk involved. 

The diving ratings listed in this guide are only guidelines and the final decision may differ from the ratings listed. 26B 

###### **Recreational scuba diving** 

The insured life must have an appropriate diving certification with one of the following recognised organizations: NAUI, SAUU, BSAC, PADI, CMAS, etc., and: 

- has dived within the past two years 

- dives to a maximum depth of 60 meters 

- always dives in a group or with a suitably qualified diving partner. 

The insured life does not participate in: 

- wreck penetration diving 

- cave or pothole diving 

- competitive diving 

- record attempts 

- any form of hazardous diving 

- Heliox or Tri-Mix diving. 

   - (Refer to diving loadings in the table below.) 

27B 

###### **Technical scuba diving** 

Technical diving is a form of scuba diving that exceeds the scope of recreational diving: 

- technical divers require advanced training, extensive experience, and specialised equipment 

- technical diving often involves the use of special gas mixtures for breathing. (Refer to diving loadings in the table below.) 

28 

###### **Commercial diving** 

Commercial diving is a branch of professional diving carried out by commercial organizations for purposes such as: 

- civil engineer in harbours, water supply and drainage systems 

- constructing, testing and maintaining equipment for the crude oil and offshore construction industries 

- boat and ship inspection, cleaning and maintenance 

- fishing, such as harvesting higher value animals like molluscs and crustaceans 

- underwater salvaging, for example in sunken ships and aircraft 

- mining activities, e.g. diamond mining. 

   - (Refer to diving loadings in the table below.)

#### Acceptance of foreign business 

Momentum will accept life business from South Africans who reside in countries where the risks, in the opinion of Momentum, are no greater than those to which they would have been exposed in South Africa. This is subject to the applicant meeting all the medical requirements as set in South Africa. Medicals need to be done by a medical doctor as prescribed in a letter issued by underwriting on request. The applicant must have a valid South African bank account. 

Only claims where the claimant meets Momentum's standard claims requirements will be accepted. For example, if Momentum requires a medical practitioner's report at claim stage, a claim will not be admitted until the report has been received, irrespective of where the client lives. Momentum will pay the South African tariff rate for medical requirements and the policyholder must pay any other costs. The proceeds will be paid into a South African bank account. 

New business by South Africans who live in, do contract work in, or are planning an extensive tour of two months or more to another country, where, in the opinion of Momentum, the risks are more severe than the corresponding risks in South Africa, will not be accepted until the applicants have permanently returned to South Africa. 

(The above is subject to completion of a _Foreign travel and work questionnaire_ that is available on VIA) 

Foreign passport holders who live in South Africa will be accepted, subject to the following criteria: 

- they must have been living in South Africa permanently for at least five years and must have a valid Permanent Residence Permit (proof must be submitted to Momentum) 

- they must be in possession of a valid work permit where the expiry date is no less than twelve months hence (proof must be submitted to Momentum) 

- they must own property in South Africa, and 

- they must not travel more than twice a year to a country where, in the opinion of Momentum, the risks are more severe than the corresponding risks in South Africa. 

Momentum will not accept insured lives with a refugee status. 

The above is subject to completion of a _Foreign insured life questionnaire_ that is available on VIA. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 32 

#### Underwriting exclusions 

Momentum may apply three different kinds of exclusions to benefits, depending on the circumstances: 

- medical exclusions on conditions that existed before the application, eg back conditions, 

- avocational exclusions for part-time activities, eg risky aviation activities, and 

- • territorial exclusions where insured lives travel in the course of their occupations to other countries where the risk, according to Momentum, is more severe than in South Africa 

Momentum applies exclusions: 

- where it cannot load an additional premium on a benefit because the risk is just too great and no additional premium will cover the risk, or 

- where the risk pool is too small, eg where the total number of applicants participating in potholing is very small and no loading would be sufficient. 

Momentum will, in most instances, try to accommodate clients using loadings and will only apply exclusion clauses where absolutely necessary. 

All exclusion clauses need to be read in conjunction with the wording following after the exclusion. This wording clearly explains Momentum's intent with regards to the practice at claim stage. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 33 

#### Replacements 

A fully completed Replacement Advice Record must accompany all replacements. This could help to reduce underwriting requirements. 

The Replacement Advice Record completed with the application form indicates that the benefit should replace an existing insurance policy or benefits(s). 

The policyholder is responsible for cancelling the policy or benefits to be replaced. 

Any amount payable under the policy will be subject to the cancellation of any policy or benefits that the new policy has to replace. 

If the policyholder fails to cancel the policy or benefits that the new policy had to replace, Momentum reserves the right to: 

- cancel the benefit/s and keep all premiums from the starting date of the benefits 

- decline a claim 

- adjust the premium or benefit amount from the starting date of the policy 

- recover amounts that have already been paid for a claim and/or set them off against benefits payable 

- apply altered terms and conditions 

- use any other remedies available by law. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024

#### Disclosure 

Consequences of nondisclosure/ misrepresentation ______________________________________________________________ 

The information that the insured life gives Momentum in the application form or in any other documents provided in support of his application, forms the basis on which the policy is issued. 

If the insured life fails to disclose any information, provides false information, or distorts information when applying for the policy, Momentum will have the right to suspend the cover from the policy's starting date. In addition, Momentum will also have the right to: 

   - refuse to pay out any current or future claims that relate to the misrepresentation or nondisclosure 

   - adjust the premium or benefit from the date of misrepresentation or nondisclosure 

   - recover money that has already been paid to the insured life for claims that relate to the misrepresentation or nondisclosure 

   - cancel the policy with immediate effect and keep any premiums paid to Momentum as a penalty. 

- Consent to disclosure ____________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The insured life is required to give his consent to exchange information, including medical information, between Momentum and any medical practitioner whom the insured life has consulted, or any other life office. 

The insured life gives Momentum permission to access this information on his behalf. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 35 

#### Factors which affect premiums paid 

Momentum will have the right to review the premium, apply altered terms and conditions, impose additional requirements or cancel the benefit if any of the factors mentioned below change. 

The insured life must notify Momentum if there is a change in his occupation or a change in smoking status. This rule applies to the following products: 

- Mortality benefits 

- Income disability and impairment benefits 

- Income enhancer benefits 

- Group income top-up benefits 

- Complete family protector benefits 

- Critical illness benefits 

- Accidental HIV Benefit 

- Living benefits 

- Premium waiver benefits 

- Future cover benefits 

- Longevity Protector® 

If the insured life fails to inform Momentum of any of the above changes, Momentum may: 

- decline a claim related to the nondisclosure 

- cancel the benefit/s and keep all premiums from the starting date of the benefits as a penalty 

- adjust the premium or benefit amount/s from the date of nondisclosure 

- recover amounts that have already been paid for a claim that is related to the nondisclosure 

- apply altered terms and conditions 

- use any other remedies available by law. 

Smoking status ___________________________________________________________________________________________________ 

The insured life must have stopped smoking for at least six consecutive months when changing the smoking status. 

In order to effect the change to non-smoker rates, the insured life must complete a nonsmoker declaration. 

A cotinine test may be requested at the discretion of the underwriters.

Momentum will accept medical reports for two years and questionnaires and blood tests for six months if there were no medical abnormalities or previous history of medical problems and there has been no subsequent change in the insured life's health.

#### Claims 

Introduction ______________________________________________________________________________ 

All claims are processed in the same area at Momentum. 

The documents required to facilitate claims processing are set out below. 

Please note that these are initial requirements only and that further requirements may be set at a later stage. 

As all claims are assessed on their merit, some claims may be repudiated. 

The most common reasons for repudiation are as follows: 

- nondisclosure of material information 

- misrepresentation of facts 

- failure to meet benefit definitions 

- benefits are no longer in force 

- insured life is not covered for the claim event. 

Should such a situation arise, Momentum will act strictly under the provisions contained in the policy contract. 

Claim amounts will only be paid within the borders of the Republic of South Africa in South African rand after any debt has been deducted. 

Payment of a claim ___________________________________________________________________________________________ 

If a valid death claim is admitted, the claim amount will be paid to the following people in the following order: 

- The cessionary (if any) 

- The beneficiary for proceeds (if any) 

- The policyholder, if different to the insured life (in the absence of a beneficiary for proceeds) 

- The deceased estate of the policyholder if the insured life and policyholder is the same person. (In the absence of a beneficiary for proceeds.) 

If a valid claim is admitted other than a death claim, the claim amount will be paid to the following people in the following order: 

- The cessionary (if any) 

- The policyholder 

The policyholder has the right to change the beneficiary nomination before an insured event takes place 

If a premium waiver benefit is in force, Momentum will pay the premiums payable on the policy.

Please note: 

Premiums are payable until the claim has been admitted. 

The policyholder must provide Momentum with written notice of a claim within six months of the claim event if the insured life is alive. 

For income disability claims the insured life will have six months to provide proof of income after the claim event occurs. Claim payments will be made during this period (where applicable). If the benefit amount is reduced after receiving such proof, Momentum reserves the right to recoup any overpayments. For waiting periods longer than six months proof of income will be required before a claim is admitted. 

Momentum reserves the right to have the insured life examined by a doctor of its choice before a claim is admitted. This medical examination is required to make sure that the insured life qualifies for a claim. 

The policyholder is responsible for the cost associated with any medical examinations.

#### Questions and Answers 

**Please note** unless specifically stated, all questions relating to the payment of a Death Benefit. The below guidelines will remain subject to the specific wording of the Myriad policy contract. 

**1. Who will receive the proceeds if the policyholder and insured life is the same person, and the insured life dies, and no beneficiary is nominated on the policy?** 

Momentum will pay the proceeds of the policy to the estate of the policyholder. 

**2. What happens if a beneficiary is nominated on the policy but only for 50% of the proceeds?** 

Momentum will pay 50% of the proceeds to the nominated beneficiary. The remaining 50% of the proceeds will be paid to the estate of the policyholder. 

**3. What happens if the nominated beneficiary is a minor?** 

Momentum will pay the proceeds to the minor’s legal guardian or any other person or a fund authorised thereto. 

**4. Can a testamentary trust be nominated as a beneficiary even though it is only created on the death of the insured life?** 

Yes, in this case, the proceeds will not be paid until the trust is registered and a bank account is opened for the trust. This may be a lengthy process. 

**5. If the policyholder and insured life is not the same person, can the policyholder appoint a third party as a beneficiary for the death benefit payable under the policy?** 

Yes, in terms of the policy contract a duly appointed beneficiary will always be paid the benefits attached to the policy, unless predeceased. 

**6. If the client signed a Beneficiary nomination form but did not submit it to Momentum before the claim event, will Momentum pay the old or new beneficiary?** 

Momentum will pay the existing beneficiary as reflected on Momentum’s records.  The only way to alter a beneficiary on a policy is to inform Momentum in writing of this change. This notification has to reach Momentum before the claim event takes place. 

**7. What will happen if the beneficiary dies before the claim event takes place?** 

In terms of the policy contract, the beneficiary nomination will not apply, as the beneficiary must be alive at the time of the claim event taking place. Therefore, the proceeds will be payable to the policyholder (if the policyholder and life insured is not the same person) or to the policyholder’s estate (where the life insured is also the policyholder). 

If the life insured and the beneficiary die simultaneously (in the case of husband and wife where they are beneficiaries on each other’s policies) due to the same event and there is no evidence to prove who died first, both beneficiary 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 10 

nominations will terminate, and the death benefit will be payable to the policyholder or the policyholder’s estate. 

###### **8. What impact does an outright cession have on the existing beneficiaries on the policy?** 

By doing an outright cession the policyholder transfers the full ownership of the policy to another person. The cession will result in the existing beneficiaries on the policy being cancelled. The new policyholder (cessionary) has to nominate new beneficiaries on the policy. If this is not done, the policy proceeds will be payable to the policyholder (cessionary) or his/her estate. The policy contract will specify what happens in a specific case. 

###### **9. What impact does a collateral cession have on the existing beneficiaries on the policy?** 

In this case, the policyholder retains ownership of the policy but with limited rights.  The cession results in the cessionary having a right to the policy proceeds in terms of an obligation the policyholder have towards the cessionary. The most common example will be where a policyholder cedes the policy to the bank as security for a loan. The bank will only be entitled to the proceeds insofar as it settles the outstanding debt. 

When a security cession is noted on the policy the existing beneficiary nomination is suspended in favour of the cessionary. 

When a claim is made, the cessionary will be paid.  If the cessionary claims the full benefit amount, the balance (that the cessionary is not legally entitled to) must be recouped from the cessionary by the estate.  The beneficiary that was suspended as a result of the cession being noted has no right to any proceeds. 

If the cessionary claims less than the full benefit amount (so they limit their claim to the amount owed to them by the cedent), Momentum will pay the balance to the beneficiary that was noted on the policy at the time of the cession being noted or the policyholder or his/her estate if no beneficiary is noted on the policy 

The contract will determine what happens in a specific case. 

If the security cession is cancelled before a claim, the existing beneficiaries will be reinstated in full or the policyholder can nominate new beneficiaries by informing Momentum in writing, before a claim event takes place. 

What if no beneficiary is noted on the policy? 

If the cessionary claims the full benefit amount, the balance must be recouped from the cessionary by the estate.  If the cessionary claims less than the full benefit amount, Momentum will pay the balance to the policyholder or his/her estate. 

###### **10. What happens if the policyholder’s Will and the beneficiary nomination conflict with each other?** 

The only way to change the beneficiary on a policy is if the policyholder informs Momentum in writing before a claim event taking place. The contract also stipulates that no cancellation or change is possible by means of a Will or otherwise. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 11 

###### **11. When will a beneficiary for ownership be used?** 

This is used if the policyholder and insured life is not the same person or where there are multiple insured lives under one policy. If the policyholder or one of the policyholders (in the case of multiple policyholders) die, that policyholder’s ownership will be transferred to the beneficiary for ownership. 

Note – where the policyholder was the premium payer, and he/she die, the premiums will not be paid on the policy unless a premium waiver was added. Momentum will communicate to the policyholder/the policyholder’s estate/the beneficiary for ownership that the policy will lapse after two unpaid premiums, unless they inform Momentum urgently of their new banking details. 

###### **12. When will disability benefits, impairment benefits and critical illness benefits be paid to a party other than the insured life?** 

Even though the benefits are personal they will always be payable to the policyholder. Should a cessionary be noted on the policy, the proceeds will be payable to the cessionary. The policy contract will determine what happens in each case. 

###### **13. A Myriad policy is taken out and A is the policyholder with A and B as insured lives. A’s benefits include a death benefit, a disability benefit and a critical illness benefit. B has a death benefit and a critical illness benefit. No beneficiaries are nominated on the policy.** 

<u>Who is paid should A’s disability or critical illness claim be admitted?</u> Policyholder A will be paid. 

<u>Who is paid should B’s critical illness claim be admitted?</u> 

Policyholder A will be paid because the contractual liability is towards the policyholder. 

###### <u>Who is paid if A dies?</u> 

If A dies his/her estate will be paid the proceeds of the death claim. 

###### <u>Who is paid if B dies?</u> 

Policyholder A will be paid because the contractual liability is towards the policyholder. 

###### <u>What is the case if C is nominated as the beneficiary on the policy?</u> 

Only A, as policyholder, can appoint a beneficiary for proceeds and a beneficiary for ownership.  If A appoints C as the beneficiary for ownership and A dies, the policy’s ownership will transfer to C and C will be the policyholder.  If A appoints C as the beneficiary for proceeds on both death benefits and either A or B dies, the death benefit will be payable to C.  It is also possible that A only appoints C as a beneficiary for proceeds on the death benefit on his own life.  In this case, A will receive the proceeds if B dies, and C will only receive the proceeds if A dies. 

Myriad technical guide – February 2024 

Page 12 

**14. A Myriad policy is taken out and A is the policyholder with A and B as insured lives. A's benefits include a death benefit, a disability benefit and a critical illness benefit. B has a death benefit and a critical illness benefit. No beneficiaries are nominated on the policy. A and B are joint owners of the policy?** 

<u>Who is paid should A’s disability or critical illness claim is admitted?</u> 

Because A and B are equal owners on the policy, they are each paid 50% of the benefit amount. 

<u>Who is paid should B’s critical illness claim be admitted?</u> 

Because A and B are equal owners on the policy, they are each paid 50% of the benefit amount. 

###### <u>Who is paid if A dies?</u> 

Because no beneficiary is noted on the policy, 50% of the proceeds that belong to A will be paid to his/her estate and the other 50% that belongs to B will be payable to B. 

###### <u>Who is paid if B dies?</u> 

Because no beneficiary is noted on the policy, 50% of the proceeds that belong to B will be paid to his/her estate and the other 50% that belongs to A will be payable to A. 

###### <u>What happens if C is nominated as the beneficiary on the policy?</u> 

If A and B appointed C as the beneficiary for proceeds on both their death benefits, C will receive 100% of the benefit should either one of them die.
